9.s: evaṃ sarvānimān rājā vyavahārān samāpayan vyapohya kilbiṣaṃ sarvaṃ prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim
9.d: एवं सर्वानिमान् राजा व्यवहारान् समापयन् व्यपोह्य किल्बिषं सर्वं प्राप्नोति परमां गतिम्

9.s: puruṣasya striyāścaiva dharme vartmani tiṣṭhatoḥ dharmye saṃyoge viprayoge ca dharmān vakṣyāmi śāśvatān
9.d: पुरुषस्य स्त्रियाश्चैव धर्मे वर्त्मनि तिष्ठतोः धर्म्ये संयोगे विप्रयोगे च धर्मान् वक्ष्यामि शाश्वतान्
9.e: I shall now expound the eternal duties of the man and woman, who keep to the righteous path, during union and separation.

9.s: asvatantrāḥ striyaḥ kāryāḥ puruṣaiḥ svairdivāniśam viṣayeṣu ca sajjantyaḥ saṃsthāpyā ātmano vaśe
9.d: अस्वतन्त्राः स्त्रियः कार्याः पुरुषैः स्वैर्दिवानिशम् विषयेषु च सज्जन्त्यः संस्थाप्या आत्मनो वशे
9.e: During the day and the night women should not be left to themselves by their men. If they become addicted to sensual objects, they should be kept under one’s control.

9.s: pitā rakṣati kaumāre bhartā rakṣati yauvane rakṣanti sthavire putrā na strī svātantryamarhati
9.d: पिता रक्षति कौमारे भर्ता रक्षति यौवने रक्षन्ति स्थविरे पुत्रा न स्त्री स्वातन्त्र्यमर्हति
9.e: The father guards her during virginity, the husband guards her in youth, the sons guard her in old age; the woman is never fit for independence.—(iii).

9.s: kāle 'dātā pitā vācyo vācyaścānupayan patiḥ mṛte bhartari putrastu vācyo māturarakṣitā
9.d: काले ऽदाता पिता वाच्यो वाच्यश्चानुपयन् पतिः मृते भर्तरि पुत्रस्तु वाच्यो मातुररक्षिता
9.e: Censurable is the father who gives her not away at the right time; censurable the husband who approaches her not; and censurable the son who, on the death of her husband, does not take care of her

9.s: sūkṣmebhyo 'pi prasaṅgebhyaḥ striyo rakṣyā viśeṣataḥ striyā dvayorhi kulayoḥ śokamāvaheyurarakṣitāḥ
9.d: सूक्ष्मेभ्यो ऽपि प्रसङ्गेभ्यः स्त्रियो रक्ष्या विशेषतः स्त्रिया द्वयोर्हि कुलयोः शोकमावहेयुररक्षिताः
9.e: Women should be specially guarded against even small attachments; for, if not guarded, they would bring grief to both families.

9.s: imaṃ hi sarvavarṇānāṃ paśyanto dharmamuttamam yatante rakṣituṃ bhāryāṃ bhartāro durbalā api
9.d: इमं हि सर्ववर्णानां पश्यन्तो धर्ममुत्तमम् यतन्ते रक्षितुं भार्यां भर्तारो दुर्बला अपि
9.e: Looking upon this as the highest duty of all castes, even weak husbands strive to guard their wives

9.s: svāṃ prasūtiṃ caritraṃ ca kulamātmānameva ca svaṃ ca dharmaṃ prayatnena jāyāṃ rakṣan hi rakṣati
9.d: स्वां प्रसूतिं चरित्रं च कुलमात्मानमेव च स्वं च धर्मं प्रयत्नेन जायां रक्षन् हि रक्षति
9.e: He who carefully protects his wipe preserves his offspring, his character, his family, his own self, and also his religion.

9.s: patirbhāryāṃ saṃpraviśya garbho bhūtvaiha jāyate jāyāyāstaddhi jāyātvaṃ yadasyāṃ jāyate punaḥ
9.d: पतिर्भार्यां संप्रविश्य गर्भो भूत्वैह जायते जायायास्तद्धि जायात्वं यदस्यां जायते पुनः
9.e: The husband, entering the womb of his wife, becomes the embryo and is then born; the wife-hood of the ‘wife’ consists in this that the husband is re-born of her.

9.s: yādṛśaṃ bhajate hi strī sutaṃ sūte tathāvidham tasmāt prajāviśuddhiarthaṃ striyaṃ rakṣet prayatnataḥ
9.d: यादृशं भजते हि स्त्री सुतं सूते तथाविधम् तस्मात् प्रजाविशुद्धिअर्थं स्त्रियं रक्षेत् प्रयत्नतः
9.e: As the man to whom the woman clings, so the offspring that she brings forth; hence for the sake of the purity of the offspring one should carefully guard the woman.

9.s: na kaścidyoṣitaḥ śaktaḥ prasahya parirakṣitum etairupāyayogaistu śakyāstāḥ parirakṣitum
9.d: न कश्चिद्योषितः शक्तः प्रसह्य परिरक्षितुम् एतैरुपाययोगैस्तु शक्यास्ताः परिरक्षितुम्
9.e: No man can guard women forcibly; they can however be guarded by the employment of these expedients.

9.s: arthasya saṅgrahe caināṃ vyaye caiva niyojayet śauce dharme 'nnapaktyāṃ ca pāriṇāhyasya vekṣaṇe
9.d: अर्थस्य सङ्ग्रहे चैनां व्यये चैव नियोजयेत् शौचे धर्मे ऽन्नपक्त्यां च पारिणाह्यस्य वेक्षणे
9.e: He shall employ her in the accumulation and disbursement of wealth, as also in cleanliness, in religious acts, in the cooking of food and in taking care of the household furniture.

9.s: arakṣitā gṛhe ruddhāḥ puruṣairāptakāribhiḥ ātmānamātmanā yāstu rakṣeyustāḥ surakṣitāḥ
9.d: अरक्षिता गृहे रुद्धाः पुरुषैराप्तकारिभिः आत्मानमात्मना यास्तु रक्षेयुस्ताः सुरक्षिताः
9.e: Women confined in the house under trusted servants are not well guarded; really well guarded are those who guard themselves by themselves.

9.s: pānaṃ durjanasaṃsargaḥ patyā ca viraho 'ṭanam svapno 'nyagehavāsaśca nārīsaṃdūṣaṇāni ṣaṭ
9.d: पानं दुर्जनसंसर्गः पत्या च विरहो ऽटनम् स्वप्नो ऽन्यगेहवासश्च नारीसंदूषणानि षट्
9.e: Drinking, associating with wicked people, separation from her husband, rambling, sleeping and residence at other’s house are the six corrupters of women.

9.s: naitā rūpaṃ parīkṣante nāsāṃ vayasi saṃsthitiḥ surūpaṃ vā virūpaṃ vā pumānityeva bhuñjate
9.d: नैता रूपं परीक्षन्ते नासां वयसि संस्थितिः सुरूपं वा विरूपं वा पुमानित्येव भुञ्जते
9.e: They care not for beauty; they have no regard for age; be he handsome or ugly, they enjoy the man simply because he is a male.

9.s: pauṃścalyāccalacittācca naisnehyācca svabhāvataḥ naiḥsnehyāc rakṣitā yatnato 'pīha bhartṛṣvetā vikurvate
9.d: पौंश्चल्याच्चलचित्ताच्च नैस्नेह्याच्च स्वभावतः नैःस्नेह्याच् रक्षिता यत्नतो ऽपीह भर्तृष्वेता विकुर्वते
9.e: Even though carefully guarded, they injure their husbands, on account of their passion for males, of ficklemindedness and of innate want of tenderness.

9.s: evaṃ svabhāvaṃ jñātvā 'sāṃ prajāpatinisargajam paramaṃ yatnamātiṣṭhet puruṣo rakṣaṇaṃ prati
9.d: एवं स्वभावं ज्ञात्वा ऽसां प्रजापतिनिसर्गजम् परमं यत्नमातिष्ठेत् पुरुषो रक्षणं प्रति
9.e: Knowing this disposition to be innate in them, from the very creation of the lord, the man should make the highest effort to guard them.

9.s: śayyā ''sanamalaṅkāraṃ kāmaṃ krodhamanārjavam anāryatāṃ drohabhāvaṃ kucaryāṃ ca strībhyo manurakalpayat drogdhṛbhāvaṃ
9.d: शय्या 'ऽसनमलङ्कारं कामं क्रोधमनार्जवम् अनार्यतां द्रोहभावं कुचर्यां च स्त्रीभ्यो मनुरकल्पयत् द्रोग्धृभावं
9.e: Manu assigned to women sleep, sitting, ornament, lust, anger, dishonesty, malice and bad conduct.

9.s: nāsti strīṇāṃ kriyā mantrairiti dharme vyavasthitiḥ nirindriyā hyamantrāśca strībhyo anṛtamiti sthitiḥ striyo
9.d: नास्ति स्त्रीणां क्रिया मन्त्रैरिति धर्मे व्यवस्थितिः निरिन्द्रिया ह्यमन्त्राश्च स्त्रीभ्यो अनृतमिति स्थितिः स्त्रियो
9.e: For women there is no dealing with the sacred texts; such is the rule of law; the fact is that, being destitute of organs and devoid of sacred texts, women are ‘false’

9.s: tathā ca śrutayo bahvyo nigītā nigameṣvapi svālakṣaṇyaparīkṣārthaṃ tāsāṃ śṛṇuta niṣkṛtīḥ
9.d: तथा च श्रुतयो बह्व्यो निगीता निगमेष्वपि स्वालक्षण्यपरीक्षार्थं तासां शृणुत निष्कृतीः
9.e: So also there are many texts sung in the vedas with a view to indicate the true character of women. from among these listen to those texts that are meant to be expiatory.

9.s: yan me mātā pralulubhe vicarantyapativratā tan me retaḥ pitā vṛṅktāmityasyaitannidarśanam
9.d: यन् मे माता प्रलुलुभे विचरन्त्यपतिव्रता तन् मे रेतः पिता वृङ्क्तामित्यस्यैतन्निदर्शनम्
9.e: ‘If my mother, unfaithful unto her lord, became enamoured while roaming about,—may my father’s semen remove that from me’;—this is an example of this.

9.s: dhyāyatyaniṣṭaṃ yat kiṃ cit pāṇigrāhasya cetasā tasyaiṣa vyabhicārasya nihnavaḥ samyagucyate
9.d: ध्यायत्यनिष्टं यत् किं चित् पाणिग्राहस्य चेतसा तस्यैष व्यभिचारस्य निह्नवः सम्यगुच्यते
9.e: What is said here is the proper expiation for whatever ill she thinks in her mind of her husband.

9.s: yādṛgguṇena bhartrā strī saṃyujyeta yathāvidhi tādṛgguṇā sā bhavati samudreṇaiva nimnagā
9.d: यादृग्गुणेन भर्त्रा स्त्री संयुज्येत यथाविधि तादृग्गुणा सा भवति समुद्रेणैव निम्नगा
9.e: When a woman is united in one form with a man possessed of certain qualities, she becomes herself endowed with similar qualities,—like a river united with the ocean.

9.s: akṣamālā vasiṣṭhena saṃyuktā 'dhamayonijā śāraṅgī mandapālena jagāmābhyarhaṇīyatām
9.d: अक्षमाला वसिष्ठेन संयुक्ता ऽधमयोनिजा शारङ्गी मन्दपालेन जगामाभ्यर्हणीयताम्
9.e: The low-bornAkṣamālāunited withVaśiṣṭha, and the doe united withMandapālū, became worthy of worship.

9.s: etāścānyāśca loke 'sminnapakṛṣṭaprasūtayaḥ 'vakṛṣṭaprasūtayaḥ utkarṣaṃ yoṣitaḥ prāptāḥ svaiḥ svairbhartṛguṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ
9.d: एताश्चान्याश्च लोके ऽस्मिन्नपकृष्टप्रसूतयः ऽवकृष्टप्रसूतयः उत्कर्षं योषितः प्राप्ताः स्वैः स्वैर्भर्तृगुणैः शुभैः
9.e: These as well as other women, of low birth, have attained eminence in the world, through the good qualities of their respective husbands.

9.s: eṣauditā lokayātrā nityaṃ strīpuṃsayoḥ śubhā pretyaiha ca sukhaudarkān prajādharmānnibodhata
9.d: एषौदिता लोकयात्रा नित्यं स्त्रीपुंसयोः शुभा प्रेत्यैह च सुखौदर्कान् प्रजाधर्मान्निबोधत
9.e: Thus has been declared the common practice, as between husband and wife, which is always happy; now understand the laws relating to children, which are conducive to happiness here as well as after death.

9.s: prajanārthaṃ mahābhāgāḥ pūjārhā gṛhadīptayaḥ striyaḥ śriyaśca geheṣu na viśeṣo 'sti kaścana
9.d: प्रजनार्थं महाभागाः पूजार्हा गृहदीप्तयः स्त्रियः श्रियश्च गेहेषु न विशेषो ऽस्ति कश्चन
9.e: There is no difference whatever between the goddess of fortune and the women who secure many blessings for the sake of bearing children, who are worthy of worship and who form the glory of their household

9.s: utpādanamapatyasya jātasya paripālanam pratyahaṃ lokayātrāyāḥ pratyakṣaṃ strī nibandhanam pratyarthaṃ
9.d: उत्पादनमपत्यस्य जातस्य परिपालनम् प्रत्यहं लोकयात्रायाः प्रत्यक्षं स्त्री निबन्धनम् प्रत्यर्थं
9.e: The begetting of the child, the nourishing of the born, and the ordinary life of the world,—of each of these things the woman is clearly the main-spring.

9.s: apatyaṃ dharmakāryāṇi śuśrūṣā ratiruttamā dārā 'dhīnastathā svargaḥ pitr̥̄ṇāmātmanaśca ha
9.d: अपत्यं धर्मकार्याणि शुश्रूषा रतिरुत्तमा दारा ऽधीनस्तथा स्वर्गः पित्र्̥̄णामात्मनश्च ह
9.e: Off-spring, religious acts, faithful service, highest happiness,—all this is dependent on the wife; as also the attainment of heaven by oneself as well as by his forefathers.

9.s: patiṃ yā nābhicarati manovāgdehasaṃyatā sā bhartṛlokānāpnoti sadbhiḥ sādhvīiti caucyate
9.d: पतिं या नाभिचरति मनोवाग्देहसंयता सा भर्तृलोकानाप्नोति सद्भिः साध्वीइति चौच्यते
9.e: The woman, who, through failure in her duty to her husband, becomes an object of contempt in the world, comes to be born as a jackal and is tormented by foul diseases.

9.s: vyabhicārāt tu bhartuḥ strī loke prāpnoti nindyatām sṛgālayoniṃ cāpnoti pāparogaiśca pīḍyate śṛgālayoniṃ
9.d: व्यभिचारात् तु भर्तुः स्त्री लोके प्राप्नोति निन्द्यताम् सृगालयोनिं चाप्नोति पापरोगैश्च पीड्यते शृगालयोनिं
9.e: The woman, who, through failure in her duty to her husband, becomes an object of contempt in the world, comes to be born as a jackal and is tormented by foul diseases.

9.s: putraṃ pratyuditaṃ sadbhiḥ pūrvajaiśca maharṣibhiḥ viśvajanyamimaṃ puṇyamupanyāsaṃ nibodhata
9.d: पुत्रं प्रत्युदितं सद्भिः पूर्वजैश्च महर्षिभिः विश्वजन्यमिमं पुण्यमुपन्यासं निबोधत
9.e: Listen to the following disquisition regarding the son, propitious and salutary to the world, set forth by the wise patriarchs and the great sages.

9.s: bhartari putraṃ vijānanti śrutidvaidhaṃ tu kartari bhartuḥ āhurutpādakaṃ ke cidapare kṣetriṇaṃ viduḥ
9.d: भर्तरि पुत्रं विजानन्ति श्रुतिद्वैधं तु कर्तरि भर्तुः आहुरुत्पादकं के चिदपरे क्षेत्रिणं विदुः
9.e: They recognise the son to be the husband’s; but in regard to one who is only the progenitor, there is diversity of opinion; some people declare the begetter, while others the owner of the soil (to be the owner of the child).

9.s: kṣetrabhūtā smṛtā nārī bījabhūtaḥ smṛtaḥ pumān kṣetrabījasamāyogāt saṃbhavaḥ sarvadehinām
9.d: क्षेत्रभूता स्मृता नारी बीजभूतः स्मृतः पुमान् क्षेत्रबीजसमायोगात् संभवः सर्वदेहिनाम्
9.e: The woman has been declared to be like the ‘soil,’ and the man has been declared to be like the seed; and the production of all corporeal beings proceeds from the union of the soil and the seed.

9.s: viśiṣṭaṃ kutra cidbījaṃ strīyonistveva kutra cit ubhayaṃ tu samaṃ yatra sā prasūtiḥ praśasyate
9.d: विशिष्टं कुत्र चिद्बीजं स्त्रीयोनिस्त्वेव कुत्र चित् उभयं तु समं यत्र सा प्रसूतिः प्रशस्यते
9.e: In some cases the seed is prominent; but in others it is the female womb; when both are equal, the offspring is highly commended.

9.s: bījasya caiva yonyāśca bījamutkṛṣṭamucyate sarvabhūtaprasūtirhi bījalakṣaṇalakṣitā
9.d: बीजस्य चैव योन्याश्च बीजमुत्कृष्टमुच्यते सर्वभूतप्रसूतिर्हि बीजलक्षणलक्षिता
9.e: [Prima-facie argument]—“As between the seed and the womb, the seed is declared to be superior; because the production of all things is marked by the characteristics of the seed.”

9.s: yādṛśaṃ tūpyate bījaṃ kṣetre kālaupapādite tādṛg rohati tat tasmin bījaṃ svairvyañjitaṃ guṇaiḥ
9.d: यादृशं तूप्यते बीजं क्षेत्रे कालौपपादिते तादृग् रोहति तत् तस्मिन् बीजं स्वैर्व्यञ्जितं गुणैः
9.e: “As is the seed which is sown in the soil prepared in season, so does the seed spring forth, marked by its own qualities.”

9.s: iyaṃ bhūmirhi bhūtānāṃ śāśvatī yonirucyate na ca yoniguṇān kāṃścidbījaṃ puṣyati puṣṭiṣu
9.d: इयं भूमिर्हि भूतानां शाश्वती योनिरुच्यते न च योनिगुणान् कांश्चिद्बीजं पुष्यति पुष्टिषु
9.e: “This earth is called the primeval womb of things; and yet, in its development, the seed does not develop any qualities of the womb.”

9.s: bhūmāvapyekakedāre kālauptāni kṛṣīvalaiḥ nānārūpāṇi jāyante bījānīha svabhāvataḥ
9.d: भूमावप्येककेदारे कालौप्तानि कृषीवलैः नानारूपाणि जायन्ते बीजानीह स्वभावतः
9.e: “In this world, seeds sown in season by the cultivators even in one and the same plot of land spring-forth in various forms, according to their nature”.

9.s: vrīhayaḥ śālayo mudgāstilā māṣāstathā yavāḥ yathābījaṃ prarohanti laśunānīkṣavastathā
9.d: व्रीहयः शालयो मुद्गास्तिला माषास्तथा यवाः यथाबीजं प्ररोहन्ति लशुनानीक्षवस्तथा
9.e: “Vrīhi-corn, rice, mudga-beans, sesamum,māṣa-beans, barley, leeks and sugar-cane are produced in accordance with the seeds.”

9.s: anyaduptaṃ jātamanyadityetatnaupapadyate upyate yaddhi yadbījaṃ tat tadeva prarohati
9.d: अन्यदुप्तं जातमन्यदित्येतत्नौपपद्यते उप्यते यद्धि यद्बीजं तत् तदेव प्ररोहति
9.e: “It is not possible that what is sown is of one kind and what is produced is of a different kind; the seed that is produced is the same that is sown.”

9.s: tat prājñena vinītena jñānavijñānavedinā āyuṣkāmena vaptavyaṃ na jātu parayoṣiti
9.d: तत् प्राज्ञेन विनीतेन ज्ञानविज्ञानवेदिना आयुष्कामेन वप्तव्यं न जातु परयोषिति
9.e: [The established conclusion]—for this reason he who is intelligent, well-trained, and conversant with the sciences and the arts, should never, if he desires longevity, sow in another’s wife.

9.s: atra gāthā vāyugītāḥ kīrtayanti purāvidaḥ yathā bījaṃ na vaptavyaṃ puṃsā paraparigrahe
9.d: अत्र गाथा वायुगीताः कीर्तयन्ति पुराविदः यथा बीजं न वप्तव्यं पुंसा परपरिग्रहे
9.e: On this point, persons conversant with ancient lore recite some ‘Gāthās’ sung byVāyu, to the effect that man should not sow his seed in what belongs to another.

9.s: naśyatīṣuryathā viddhaḥ khe viddhamanuvidhyataḥ tathā naśyati vai kṣipraṃ bījaṃ paraparigrahe kṣiptaṃ
9.d: नश्यतीषुर्यथा विद्धः खे विद्धमनुविध्यतः तथा नश्यति वै क्षिप्रं बीजं परपरिग्रहे क्षिप्तं
9.e: ‘As the arrow shot by an after-shooter hitting a wounded animal in a hole (already made) is wasted, so does the seed become wasted when sown in what belongs to another.’

9.s: pṛthorapīmāṃ pṛthivīṃ bhāryāṃ pūrvavido viduḥ sthāṇucchedasya kedāramāhuḥ śālyavato mṛgam
9.d: पृथोरपीमां पृथिवीं भार्यां पूर्वविदो विदुः स्थाणुच्छेदस्य केदारमाहुः शाल्यवतो मृगम्
9.e: People learned in ancient lore have regarded thisPṛthvī(earth) to be the wife ofPṛthu; they declare the field to belong to him who has cleared off the stalks, and the deer to him who struck the dart.

9.s: etāvāneva puruṣo yatjāyā 'tmā prajaiti ha viprāḥ prāhustathā caitadyo bhartā sā smṛtāṅganā
9.d: एतावानेव पुरुषो यत्जाया ऽत्मा प्रजैति ह विप्राः प्राहुस्तथा चैतद्यो भर्ता सा स्मृताङ्गना
9.e: The man is a man only in so far as he consists of himself, his wife and his progeny. thus it is that theBrāhmaṇashave declared that ‘the husband is declared to be the same as the wife.’

9.s: na niṣkrayavisargābhyāṃ bharturbhāryā vimucyate evaṃ dharmaṃ vijānīmaḥ prāk prajāpatinirmitam
9.d: न निष्क्रयविसर्गाभ्यां भर्तुर्भार्या विमुच्यते एवं धर्मं विजानीमः प्राक् प्रजापतिनिर्मितम्
9.e: Either by sale or by repudiation the wife is not released from her husband; such is the law that we know, as originally propounded by prajapati.

9.s: sakṛdaṃśo nipatati sakṛt kanyā pradīyate sakṛdāha dadānīti trīṇyetāni satāṃ sakṛt dadāmīti
9.d: सकृदंशो निपतति सकृत् कन्या प्रदीयते सकृदाह ददानीति त्रीण्येतानि सतां सकृत् ददामीति
9.e: Once does the share fall to a man; once is a maiden given away; once does one say ‘I give’; each of these three comes only once.

9.s: yathā go 'śvauṣṭradāsīṣu mahiṣy 'jā 'vikāsu ca nautpādakaḥ prajābhāgī tathaivānyāṅganāsvapi
9.d: यथा गो ऽश्वौष्ट्रदासीषु महिष्य् ऽजा ऽविकासु च नौत्पादकः प्रजाभागी तथैवान्याङ्गनास्वपि
9.e: As with cows, mares, she-camels, slave-girls, buffaloes, she-goats and ewes, it is not the begetter who obtains the offspring,—even thus it is with the wives of others

9.s: ye 'kṣetriṇo bījavantaḥ parakṣetrapravāpiṇaḥ te vai sasyasya jātasya na labhante phalaṃ kva cit
9.d: ये ऽक्षेत्रिणो बीजवन्तः परक्षेत्रप्रवापिणः ते वै सस्यस्य जातस्य न लभन्ते फलं क्व चित्
9.e: If persons, possessing no fields, but having seeds, sow these in fields belonging to others,—they never obtain the grain of the crop that is produced.

9.s: yadanyagoṣu vṛṣabho vatsānāṃ janayetśatam gomināmeva te vatsā moghaṃ skanditamārṣabham
9.d: यदन्यगोषु वृषभो वत्सानां जनयेत्शतम् गोमिनामेव ते वत्सा मोघं स्कन्दितमार्षभम्
9.e: If a bull were to beget a hundred calves on others’ cows, those calves would belong to the owners of the cows, and the bull’s emissions would be in vain.

9.s: tathaivākṣetriṇo bījaṃ parakṣetrapravāpiṇaḥ kurvanti kṣetriṇāmarthaṃ na bījī labhate phalam
9.d: तथैवाक्षेत्रिणो बीजं परक्षेत्रप्रवापिणः कुर्वन्ति क्षेत्रिणामर्थं न बीजी लभते फलम्
9.e: Similarly persons who have no ‘soil’ of their own—if they sow in the ‘soil’ belonging to another man, they confer benefit upon the owner of the ‘soil,’ and the owner of the seed reaps no fruit.

9.s: phalaṃ tvanabhisaṃdhāya kṣetriṇāṃ bījināṃ tathā pratyakṣaṃ kṣetriṇāmartho bījādyonirgalīyasī barīyasī
9.d: फलं त्वनभिसंधाय क्षेत्रिणां बीजिनां तथा प्रत्यक्षं क्षेत्रिणामर्थो बीजाद्योनिर्गलीयसी बरीयसी
9.e: If between the owner of the soil and the owner of the seed, there has been no compact regarding the produce, then the chops belong clearly to the owner of the soil;—the receptacle being more important than the seed.

9.s: kriyābhyupagamāt tvetadbījārthaṃ yat pradīyate tasyaiha bhāginau dṛṣṭau bījī kṣetrika eva ca
9.d: क्रियाभ्युपगमात् त्वेतद्बीजार्थं यत् प्रदीयते तस्यैह भागिनौ दृष्टौ बीजी क्षेत्रिक एव च
9.e: If however the seed is given for the purpose of sowing, after the acceptance of a compact,—in that case both, the owner of the soil and the owner of the seed, are considered to be sharers of the produce.—(r>3)

9.s: oghavātāhṛtaṃ bījaṃ yasya kṣetre prarohati kṣetrikasyaiva tadbījaṃ na vaptā labhate phalam na bījī labhate phalam
9.d: ओघवाताहृतं बीजं यस्य क्षेत्रे प्ररोहति क्षेत्रिकस्यैव तद्बीजं न वप्ता लभते फलम् न बीजी लभते फलम्
9.e: If seed, carried away by rain or wind, germinates in a soil,—that seed belongs to the owner of the soil, and the owner of the seed does not receive the produce.

9.s: eṣa dharmo gavāśvasya dāsyuṣṭrājāvikasya ca vihaṅgamahiṣīṇāṃ ca vijñeyaḥ prasavaṃ prati
9.d: एष धर्मो गवाश्वस्य दास्युष्ट्राजाविकस्य च विहङ्गमहिषीणां च विज्ञेयः प्रसवं प्रति
9.e: This same law should be understood as applying to the offspring of cows, mares, slave-girls, she-camels, she-goats and ewes; as also of birds and buffaloes.

9.s: etadvaḥ sāraphalgutvaṃ bījayonyoḥ prakīrtitam ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi yoṣitāṃ dharmamāpadi
9.d: एतद्वः सारफल्गुत्वं बीजयोन्योः प्रकीर्तितम् अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि योषितां धर्ममापदि
9.e: Thus has been explained to you the comparative importance and non-importance of the seed and the womb; after this i am going to expound the duties of women during times of distress.

9.s: bhrāturjyeṣṭhasya bhāryā yā gurupatnyanujasya sā yavīyasastu yā bhāryā snuṣā jyeṣṭhasya sā smṛtā
9.d: भ्रातुर्ज्येष्ठस्य भार्या या गुरुपत्न्यनुजस्य सा यवीयसस्तु या भार्या स्नुषा ज्येष्ठस्य सा स्मृता
9.e: The wife of the elder brother is, for the younger, a ‘wife of the preceptor’; and the wife of the younger brother has been declared to be a ‘daughter-in-law’ for the elder.

9.s: jyeṣṭho yavīyaso bhāryāṃ yavīyān vā 'grajastriyam patitau bhavato gatvā niyuktāvapyanāpadi
9.d: ज्येष्ठो यवीयसो भार्यां यवीयान् वा ऽग्रजस्त्रियम् पतितौ भवतो गत्वा नियुक्तावप्यनापदि
9.e: If the elder brother has recourse to the wife of the younger, or the younger brother to the wife of the elder, they become outcasts, even though ‘authorised,’—except in times of distress.

9.s: devarādvā sapiṇḍādvā striyā samyakniyuktayā prajaipsitā ''dhigantavyā saṃtānasya parikṣaye
9.d: देवराद्वा सपिण्डाद्वा स्त्रिया सम्यक्नियुक्तया प्रजैप्सिता 'ऽधिगन्तव्या संतानस्य परिक्षये
9.e: On failure of issue, the woman, on being authorised, may obtain, in the proper manner, the desired offspring, either from her younger brother-in-law or from a ‘Sapiṇḍa’.

9.s: vidhavāyāṃ niyuktastu ghṛtākto vāgyato niśi ekamutpādayet putraṃ na dvitīyaṃ kathaṃ cana
9.d: विधवायां नियुक्तस्तु घृताक्तो वाग्यतो निशि एकमुत्पादयेत् पुत्रं न द्वितीयं कथं चन
9.e: He who has been authorised in regard to a widow shall, annointed with clarified butter and with speech controlled, beget, at night, one son,—and on no account a second one.

9.s: dvitīyameke prajanaṃ manyante strīṣu tadvidaḥ anirvṛtaṃ niyogārthaṃ paśyanto dharmatastayoḥ 'nirvṛttaṃ
9.d: द्वितीयमेके प्रजनं मन्यन्ते स्त्रीषु तद्विदः अनिर्वृतं नियोगार्थं पश्यन्तो धर्मतस्तयोः ऽनिर्वृत्तं
9.e: Some people, learned in the subject, admit, on the basis of propriety, of a second procreation on women,—perceiving, as they do, that the couple’s purpose of authorisation’ is not (otherwise) accomplished.

9.s: vidhavāyāṃ niyogārthe nirvṛtte tu yathāvidhi nivṛtte guruvatca snuṣāvatca varteyātāṃ parasparam
9.d: विधवायां नियोगार्थे निर्वृत्ते तु यथाविधि निवृत्ते गुरुवत्च स्नुषावत्च वर्तेयातां परस्परम्
9.e: But when the purpose of the ‘authorisation’ in regard to the widow has been duly accomplished, the two should behave towards each other like an elder and like a daughter-in-law.

9.s: niyuktau yau vidhiṃ hitvā varteyātāṃ tu kāmataḥ tāvubhau patitau syātāṃ snuṣāgagurutalpagau
9.d: नियुक्तौ यौ विधिं हित्वा वर्तेयातां तु कामतः तावुभौ पतितौ स्यातां स्नुषागगुरुतल्पगौ
9.e: If the two persons thus ‘authorised’ renounce the law and act from carnal desire, both would become outcasts,—being like one who has intercourse with his daughter-in-law and one who defiles the bed of his elder.

9.s: nānyasmin vidhavā nārī niyoktavyā dvijātibhiḥ anyasmin hi niyuñjānā dharmaṃ hanyuḥ sanātanam
9.d: नान्यस्मिन् विधवा नारी नियोक्तव्या द्विजातिभिः अन्यस्मिन् हि नियुञ्जाना धर्मं हन्युः सनातनम्
9.e: By twice-born persons the widow shall not be ‘authorised’ in regard to another person; by ‘authorising’ her in regard to another, they would violate the eternal law.

9.s: naudvāhikeṣu mantreṣu niyogaḥ kīrtyate kva cit na vivāhavidhāvuktaṃ vidhavāvedanaṃ punaḥ
9.d: नौद्वाहिकेषु मन्त्रेषु नियोगः कीर्त्यते क्व चित् न विवाहविधावुक्तं विधवावेदनं पुनः
9.e: Nowhere in the mantra-texts bearing upon marriage is ‘authorisation’ mentioned; nor again is the marriage of the widow mentioned in the injunction of marriage.

9.s: ayaṃ dvijairhi vidvadbhiḥ paśudharmo vigarhitaḥ manuṣyāṇāmapi prokto vene rājyaṃ praśāsati
9.d: अयं द्विजैर्हि विद्वद्भिः पशुधर्मो विगर्हितः मनुष्याणामपि प्रोक्तो वेने राज्यं प्रशासति
9.e: During the time that King Vena was ruling over his kingdom, this reprehensible bestial practice was introduced by ignorant twice-born men among men also.

9.s: sa mahīmakhilāṃ bhuñjan rājarṣipravaraḥ purā varṇānāṃ saṅkaraṃ cakre kāmaupahatacetanaḥ
9.d: स महीमखिलां भुञ्जन् राजर्षिप्रवरः पुरा वर्णानां सङ्करं चक्रे कामौपहतचेतनः
9.e: In ancient times that chief of royal sages, possessing the whole world, brought about the confusion of castes, having his mind beset with lust.

9.s: tataḥ prabhṛti yo mohāt pramītapatikāṃ striyam niyojayatyapatyārthaṃ taṃ vigarhanti sādhavaḥ
9.d: ततः प्रभृति यो मोहात् प्रमीतपतिकां स्त्रियम् नियोजयत्यपत्यार्थं तं विगर्हन्ति साधवः
9.e: Since then, whenever any one, through folly, ‘authorises’ a woman whose husband is dead, to beget children,—him the good men censure.

9.s: yasyā mriyeta kanyāyā vācā satye kṛte patiḥ tāmanena vidhānena nijo vindeta devaraḥ
9.d: यस्या म्रियेत कन्याया वाचा सत्ये कृते पतिः तामनेन विधानेन निजो विन्देत देवरः
9.e: If the husband of a maiden dies after the troth has been verbally plighted,—shall her then own younger brother-in-law espouse in the following manner.

9.s: yathāvidhiadhigamyaināṃ śuklavastrāṃ śucivratām mitho bhajetā prasavāt sakṛtsakṛdṛtāvṛtau
9.d: यथाविधिअधिगम्यैनां शुक्लवस्त्रां शुचिव्रताम् मिथो भजेता प्रसवात् सकृत्सकृदृतावृतौ
9.e: When he has, according to rule, espoused her, clad in white garments and pure in her observances, they shall approach each other once in each season, until issue.

9.s: na dattvā kasya cit kanyāṃ punardadyādvicakṣaṇaḥ dattvā punaḥ prayacchan hi prāpnoti puruṣānṛtam
9.d: न दत्त्वा कस्य चित् कन्यां पुनर्दद्याद्विचक्षणः दत्त्वा पुनः प्रयच्छन् हि प्राप्नोति पुरुषानृतम्
9.e: Having given away his daughter to one man, the wise man should not give her away again. Having given her away once, if he gives her again, he incurs the guilt of ‘fraud towards men.’—‘(7l)

9.s: vidhivat pratigṛhyāpi tyajet kanyāṃ vigarhitām vyādhitāṃ vipraduṣṭāṃ vā chadmanā caupapāditām
9.d: विधिवत् प्रतिगृह्यापि त्यजेत् कन्यां विगर्हिताम् व्याधितां विप्रदुष्टां वा छद्मना चौपपादिताम्
9.e: Even after having accepted the maiden in due form, one mat repudiate her, if she be blemished, or diseased, or corrupted, or betrothed by deception.

9.s: yastu doṣavatīṃ kanyāmanākhyāyaupapādayet tasya tadvitathaṃ kuryāt kanyādāturdurātmanaḥ
9.d: यस्तु दोषवतीं कन्यामनाख्यायौपपादयेत् तस्य तद्वितथं कुर्यात् कन्यादातुर्दुरात्मनः
9.e: If a man gives away a defective maiden, without declaring the defects, one may annul that act of the wicked girl-betrother.

9.s: vidhāya vṛttiṃ bhāryāyāḥ pravaset kāryavānnaraḥ avṛttikarśitā hi strī praduṣyet sthitimatyapi
9.d: विधाय वृत्तिं भार्यायाः प्रवसेत् कार्यवान्नरः अवृत्तिकर्शिता हि स्त्री प्रदुष्येत् स्थितिमत्यपि
9.e: A man having business may go abroad, after having provided for the maintenance of his wife; for a wife, even though virtuous, may become corrupt, when distressed by want of subsistence.

9.s: vidhāya proṣite vṛttiṃ jīvenniyamamāsthitā proṣite tvavidhāyaiva jīvetśilpairagarhitaiḥ
9.d: विधाय प्रोषिते वृत्तिं जीवेन्नियममास्थिता प्रोषिते त्वविधायैव जीवेत्शिल्पैरगर्हितैः
9.e: When the husband has gone abroad after having provided for her subsistence, she shall live on, firmly devoted to restraint. When however he has gone without providing for it, she shall subsist by unobjectionable industries.

9.s: proṣito dharmakāryārthaṃ pratīkṣyo 'ṣṭau naraḥ samāḥ vidyārthaṃ ṣaḍ yaśo 'rthaṃ vā kāmārthaṃ trīṃstu vatsarān
9.d: प्रोषितो धर्मकार्यार्थं प्रतीक्ष्यो ऽष्टौ नरः समाः विद्यार्थं षड् यशो ऽर्थं वा कामार्थं त्रींस्तु वत्सरान्
9.e: If the husband went abroad for some sacred duty, he should be awaited for eight years; if for learning, or for fame, six years; but three years, if for pleasure.

9.s: saṃvatsaraṃ pratīkṣeta dviṣantīṃ yoṣitaṃ patiḥ dviṣāṇāṃ ūrdhvaṃ saṃvatsarāt tvenāṃ dāyaṃ hṛtvā na saṃvaset
9.d: संवत्सरं प्रतीक्षेत द्विषन्तीं योषितं पतिः द्विषाणां ऊर्ध्वं संवत्सरात् त्वेनां दायं हृत्वा न संवसेत्
9.e: For one year the husband shall bear with a hating wife; after the year he shall wrest her property and cease to co-habit with her.

9.s: atikrāmet pramattaṃ yā mattaṃ rogārtameva vā sā trīn māsān parityājyā vibhūṣaṇaparicchadā
9.d: अतिक्रामेत् प्रमत्तं या मत्तं रोगार्तमेव वा सा त्रीन् मासान् परित्याज्या विभूषणपरिच्छदा
9.e: If the wife disregards her husband who is mad, or intoxicated, or afflicted by disease, she should be deprived of ornaments and appurtenances and abandoned for three months.

9.s: unmattaṃ patitaṃ klībamabījaṃ pāparogiṇam na tyāgo 'sti dviṣantyāśca na ca dāyāpavartanam
9.d: उन्मत्तं पतितं क्लीबमबीजं पापरोगिणम् न त्यागो ऽस्ति द्विषन्त्याश्च न च दायापवर्तनम्
9.e: If, however, she shows aversion to one who is mad, or an outcast, or impotent, or seedless, or afflicted with foul disease, there shall be no desertion, nor the wresting of her property.

9.s: madyapā 'sādhuvṛttā ca pratikūlā ca yā bhavet madyapāsatyavṛttā vyādhitā vā 'dhivettavyā hiṃsrā 'rthaghnī ca sarvadā
9.d: मद्यपा ऽसाधुवृत्ता च प्रतिकूला च या भवेत् मद्यपासत्यवृत्ता व्याधिता वा ऽधिवेत्तव्या हिंस्रा ऽर्थघ्नी च सर्वदा
9.e: If the wife is a drunkard, or false in conduct, or rebellious, or diseased or mischievous, or wasteful,—she should be superseded.

9.s: vandhyāṣṭame 'dhivedyā'abde daśame tu mṛtaprajā ekādaśe strījananī sadyastvapriyavādinī
9.d: वन्ध्याष्टमे ऽधिवेद्याऽअब्दे दशमे तु मृतप्रजा एकादशे स्त्रीजननी सद्यस्त्वप्रियवादिनी
9.e: The barren wife shall be superseded in the eighth year; in the tenth she whose children die off; in the eleventh she who bears only daughters; but immediately she who talks harshly.

9.s: yā rogiṇī syāt tu hitā saṃpannā caiva śīlataḥ sā 'nujñāpyādhivettavyā nāvamānyā ca karhi cit
9.d: या रोगिणी स्यात् तु हिता संपन्ना चैव शीलतः सा ऽनुज्ञाप्याधिवेत्तव्या नावमान्या च कर्हि चित्
9.e: But if a wife, who is an invalid, is well-disposed and endowed with modesty, she may be superseded after her consent has been obtained; and in no case is she to be disgraced.

9.s: adhivinnā tu yā nārī nirgacchedruṣitā gṛhāt sā sadyaḥ saṃniroddhavyā tyājyā vā kulasaṃnidhau
9.d: अधिविन्ना तु या नारी निर्गच्छेद्रुषिता गृहात् सा सद्यः संनिरोद्धव्या त्याज्या वा कुलसंनिधौ
9.e: On being superseded, if a wife, in anger, should go away from the house, she shall be either immediately confined, or cast off in the presence of the family.

9.s: pratiṣiddhā 'pi cedyā tu madyamabhyudayeṣvapi pratiṣedhe pibedyā tu prekṣāsamājaṃ gacchedvā sā daṇḍyā kṛṣṇalāni ṣaṭ
9.d: प्रतिषिद्धा ऽपि चेद्या तु मद्यमभ्युदयेष्वपि प्रतिषेधे पिबेद्या तु प्रेक्षासमाजं गच्छेद्वा सा दण्ड्या कृष्णलानि षट्
9.e: If the wife, though forbidden, drinks wine even at festivals or visits, shows and assemblies, she shall be fined six ‘Kṛṣṇalas’.

9.s: yadi svāścāparāścaiva vinderan yoṣito dvijāḥ tāsāṃ varṇakrameṇa syāj jyeṣṭhyaṃ pūjā ca veśma ca
9.d: यदि स्वाश्चापराश्चैव विन्देरन् योषितो द्विजाः तासां वर्णक्रमेण स्याज् ज्येष्ठ्यं पूजा च वेश्म च
9.e: When twice-born men wed women of their own as well as other castes, their seniority, honour and habitation shall be according to the order of their castes.

9.s: bhartuḥ śarīraśuśrūṣāṃ dharmakāryaṃ ca naityakam svā caiva kuryāt sarveṣāṃ nāsvajātiḥ kathaṃ cana svā svaiva
9.d: भर्तुः शरीरशुश्रूषां धर्मकार्यं च नैत्यकम् स्वा चैव कुर्यात् सर्वेषां नास्वजातिः कथं चन स्वा स्वैव
9.e: Of all wives, the wife of the man’s own caste, and never that of a different caste, shall attend to the husband’s personal service, as also to his daily sacred rites.

9.s: yastu tat kārayen mohāt sajātyā sthitayā 'nyayā yathā brāhmaṇacāṇḍālaḥ pūrvadṛṣṭastathaiva saḥ
9.d: यस्तु तत् कारयेन् मोहात् सजात्या स्थितया ऽन्यया यथा ब्राह्मणचाण्डालः पूर्वदृष्टस्तथैव सः
9.e: While the wife of the same caste is alive, if through folly, one causes these duties to be performed by another wife, he is a ‘Brāhmaṇa-Cāṇḍāla’, as has been held by the ancients.

9.s: utkṛṣṭāyābhirūpāya varāya sadṛśāya ca aprāptāmapi tāṃ tasmai kanyāṃ dadyādyathāvidhi
9.d: उत्कृष्टायाभिरूपाय वराय सदृशाय च अप्राप्तामपि तां तस्मै कन्यां दद्याद्यथाविधि
9.e: One shall give his daughter in the proper form, even though she may not have attained (the age), to a bridegroom who is of exceptionally distinguished appearance, and her equal.

9.s: kāmamā maraṇāt tiṣṭhedgṛhe kanyāṛtumatyapi na caivaināṃ prayaccet tu guṇahīnāya karhi cit
9.d: काममा मरणात् तिष्ठेद्गृहे कन्याऋतुमत्यपि न चैवैनां प्रयच्चेत् तु गुणहीनाय कर्हि चित्
9.e: Well might the maiden, even though she may have reached puberty, remain in the house till her death; but the father shall never give her to a man destitute of good qualities.

9.s: trīṇi varṣāṇyudīkṣeta kumāry ṛtumatī satī ūrdhvaṃ tu kālādetasmādvindeta sadṛśaṃ patim
9.d: त्रीणि वर्षाण्युदीक्षेत कुमार्य् ऋतुमती सती ऊर्ध्वं तु कालादेतस्माद्विन्देत सदृशं पतिम्
9.e: Having reached puberty, the maiden may wait for three years; after that time, she shall procure a suitable husband.

9.s: adīyamānā bhartāramadhigacchedyadi svayam nainaḥ kiṃ cidavāpnoti na ca yaṃ sā 'dhigacchati
9.d: अदीयमाना भर्तारमधिगच्छेद्यदि स्वयम् नैनः किं चिदवाप्नोति न च यं सा ऽधिगच्छति
9.e: When a maiden, when not given away, herself procures a husband, she incurs no sort of sin; nor does the man whom she weds.

9.s: alaṅkāraṃ nādadīta pitryaṃ kanyā svayaṃvarā mātṛkaṃ bhrātṛdattaṃ vā stenā syādyadi taṃ haret
9.d: अलङ्कारं नाददीत पित्र्यं कन्या स्वयंवरा मातृकं भ्रातृदत्तं वा स्तेना स्याद्यदि तं हरेत्
9.e: When the girl chooses her own husband, she should not take away any ornaments given to her either by her father, or mother or brother; if she did take them, she would be a thief.

9.s: pitre na dadyātśulkaṃ tu kanyāṃ ṛtumatīṃ haran sa ca svāmyādatikrāmedṛtūnāṃ pratirodhanāt
9.d: पित्रे न दद्यात्शुल्कं तु कन्यां ऋतुमतीं हरन् स च स्वाम्यादतिक्रामेदृतूनां प्रतिरोधनात्
9.e: When a man takes away a maiden who has reached puberty, he shall pay no nuptial fee to the father,—who would fall off from his ownership by reason of thwarting her menses.

9.s: triṃśadvarṣo vahet kanyāṃ hṛdyāṃ dvādaśavārṣikīm tryaṣṭavarṣo 'ṣṭavarṣāṃ vā dharme sīdati satvaraḥ
9.d: त्रिंशद्वर्षो वहेत् कन्यां हृद्यां द्वादशवार्षिकीम् त्र्यष्टवर्षो ऽष्टवर्षां वा धर्मे सीदति सत्वरः
9.e: A man thirty years old shall marry a charming maiden twelve years old; or one twenty four years old, a damsel eight years old; in the event of his duties suffering, he may do it sooner.

9.s: devadattāṃ patirbhāryāṃ vindate naicchayā 'tmanaḥ tāṃ sādhvīṃ bibhṛyānnityaṃ devānāṃ priyamācaran
9.d: देवदत्तां पतिर्भार्यां विन्दते नैच्छया ऽत्मनः तां साध्वीं बिभृयान्नित्यं देवानां प्रियमाचरन्
9.e: The husband obtains his wife as a present from the gods, and not by his own wish; hence he should always support the faithful wife, thereby doing what is agreeable to the gods.

9.s: prajanārthaṃ striyaḥ sṛṣṭāḥ saṃtānārthaṃ ca mānavaḥ tasmāt sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ śrutau patnyā sahauditaḥ
9.d: प्रजनार्थं स्त्रियः सृष्टाः संतानार्थं च मानवः तस्मात् साधारणो धर्मः श्रुतौ पत्न्या सहौदितः
9.e: Women were created for the purpose of child-bearing, and men for the furfose of procreation. hence it is that Religious Rites have been ordained in the Veda as common between the man and his wife.

9.s: kanyāyāṃ dattaśulkāyāṃ mriyeta yadi śulkadaḥ devarāya pradātavyā yadi kanyā 'numanyate
9.d: कन्यायां दत्तशुल्कायां म्रियेत यदि शुल्कदः देवराय प्रदातव्या यदि कन्या ऽनुमन्यते
9.e: After the nuptial fee for a girl has been paid, if the man who paid the fee dies, the girl should be given to the younger brother-in-law, in case she consents.

9.s: ādadīta na śūdro 'pi śulkaṃ duhitaraṃ dadan śulkaṃ hi gṛhṇan kurute channaṃ duhitṛvikrayam
9.d: आददीत न शूद्रो ऽपि शुल्कं दुहितरं ददन् शुल्कं हि गृह्णन् कुरुते छन्नं दुहितृविक्रयम्
9.e: Even a Śūdra should not take a nuptial fee, when he is giving away his daughter; by accepting a fee, what he does is disguised bartering.

9.s: etat tu na pare cakrurnāpare jātu sādhavaḥ yadanyasya pratijñāya punaranyasya dīyate
9.d: एतत् तु न परे चक्रुर्नापरे जातु साधवः यदन्यस्य प्रतिज्ञाय पुनरन्यस्य दीयते
9.e: Good men, both ancient and modern, have never committed the act, that having promised to one they gave her to another.

9.s: nānuśuśruma jātvetat pūrveṣvapi hi janmasu śulkasaṃjñena mūlyena channaṃ duhitṛvikrayam
9.d: नानुशुश्रुम जात्वेतत् पूर्वेष्वपि हि जन्मसु शुल्कसंज्ञेन मूल्येन छन्नं दुहितृविक्रयम्
9.e: Nor indeed have we heard, even in former Cycles, of the covert sale of a daughter, for a price styled “nuptial fee.”

9.s: anyonyasyāvyabhicāro bhavedāmaraṇāntikaḥ eṣa dharmaḥ samāsena jñeyaḥ strīpuṃsayoḥ paraḥ
9.d: अन्योन्यस्याव्यभिचारो भवेदामरणान्तिकः एष धर्मः समासेन ज्ञेयः स्त्रीपुंसयोः परः
9.e: ‘May mutual fidelity continue till death’,—this, in brief should be understood as the highest duty between husband and wife.

9.s: tathā nityaṃ yateyātāṃ strīpuṃsau tu kṛtakriyau yathā nābhicaretāṃ tau viyuktāvitaretaram nāticaretāṃ
9.d: तथा नित्यं यतेयातां स्त्रीपुंसौ तु कृतक्रियौ यथा नाभिचरेतां तौ वियुक्तावितरेतरम् नातिचरेतां
9.e: Man and wife, after they have passed through the rites, should always so exert themselves that they may not become separated and be unfaithful to each other.

9.s: eṣa strīpuṃsayorukto dharmo vo ratisaṃhitaḥ āpadyapatyaprāptiśca dāyadharmaṃ nibodhata
9.d: एष स्त्रीपुंसयोरुक्तो धर्मो वो रतिसंहितः आपद्यपत्यप्राप्तिश्च दायधर्मं निबोधत
9.e: Thus has been expounded to you the law relating to husband and wife, which is conducive to conjugal happiness,—as also the manner of obtaining children in times of distress; learn now the partition of inheritance.

9.s: ūrdhvaṃ pituśca mātuśca sametya bhrātaraḥ samam bhajeran paitṛkaṃ rikthamanīśāste hi jīvatoḥ
9.d: ऊर्ध्वं पितुश्च मातुश्च समेत्य भ्रातरः समम् भजेरन् पैतृकं रिक्थमनीशास्ते हि जीवतोः
9.e: After the death of the father and of the mother, the brothers, being assembled, shall divide equally the paternal property; while the parents are alive, they have no power.

9.s: jyeṣṭha eva tu gṛhṇīyāt pitryaṃ dhanamaśeṣataḥ śeṣāstamupajīveyuryathaiva pitaraṃ tathā
9.d: ज्येष्ठ एव तु गृह्णीयात् पित्र्यं धनमशेषतः शेषास्तमुपजीवेयुर्यथैव पितरं तथा
9.e: The eldest brother alone may take the entire paternal property; the rest shall live under him, just as under their father.

9.s: jyeṣṭhena jātamātreṇa putrī bhavati mānavaḥ pitr̥̄ṇāmanṛṇaścaiva sa tasmāt sarvamarhati
9.d: ज्येष्ठेन जातमात्रेण पुत्री भवति मानवः पित्र्̥̄णामनृणश्चैव स तस्मात् सर्वमर्हति
9.e: By the mere birth of the eldest son, a man becomes ‘with son,’ and (hence) free from the debt toPitṛs; it is for this reason that he deserves the whole.

9.s: yasminn ṛṇaṃ saṃnayati yena cānantyamaśnute sa eva dharmajaḥ putraḥ kāmajānitarān viduḥ
9.d: यस्मिन्न् ऋणं संनयति येन चानन्त्यमश्नुते स एव धर्मजः पुत्रः कामजानितरान् विदुः
9.e: That son alone to whom the man transfers his debt, and through whom he attains immortality, is the ‘duty-born son;’ others are known as ‘lust-born.’

9.s: pitaiva pālayet pūtrān jyeṣṭho bhrātr̥̄ṇ yavīyasaḥ putravatcāpi varteran jyeṣṭhe bhrātari dharmataḥ
9.d: पितैव पालयेत् पूत्रान् ज्येष्ठो भ्रात्र्̥̄ण् यवीयसः पुत्रवत्चापि वर्तेरन् ज्येष्ठे भ्रातरि धर्मतः
9.e: The eldest brother shall support his younger brothers, just as the father supports his sons; and the younger brothers, in duty bound, shall behave towards the eldest brother, like sons.

9.s: jyeṣṭhaḥ kulaṃ vardhayati vināśayati vā punaḥ jyeṣṭhaḥ pūjyatamo loke jyeṣṭhaḥ sadbhiragarhitaḥ
9.d: ज्येष्ठः कुलं वर्धयति विनाशयति वा पुनः ज्येष्ठः पूज्यतमो लोके ज्येष्ठः सद्भिरगर्हितः
9.e: It is the eldest brother who advances the family, or ruins it; the eldest brother is worthy of the highest honour; the eldest brother is never ill-treated by good men.

9.s: yo jyeṣṭho jyeṣṭhavṛttiḥ syān mātaiva sa pitaiva saḥ ajyeṣṭhavṛttiryastu syāt sa saṃpūjyastu bandhuvat
9.d: यो ज्येष्ठो ज्येष्ठवृत्तिः स्यान् मातैव स पितैव सः अज्येष्ठवृत्तिर्यस्तु स्यात् स संपूज्यस्तु बन्धुवत्
9.e: If the eldest brother behaves as the eldest brother, he is like a mother, and like a father. If however he does not behave like the eldest brother, he shall be honoured simply as a kinsman.

9.s: evaṃ saha vaseyurvā pṛthag vā dharmakāmyayā pṛthag vivardhate dharmastasmāddharmyā pṛthakkriyā
9.d: एवं सह वसेयुर्वा पृथग् वा धर्मकाम्यया पृथग् विवर्धते धर्मस्तस्माद्धर्म्या पृथक्क्रिया
9.e: Thus may they live either together, or separately, with a view to spiritual merit; by separate living merit prospers; hence separation is meritorious.

9.s: jyeṣṭhasya viṃśa uddhāraḥ sarvadravyācca yadvaram tato 'rdhaṃ madhyamasya syāt turīyaṃ tu yavīyasaḥ
9.d: ज्येष्ठस्य विंश उद्धारः सर्वद्रव्याच्च यद्वरम् ततो ऽर्धं मध्यमस्य स्यात् तुरीयं तु यवीयसः
9.e: For the eldest, the additional portion shall consist of the twentieth part of the property, as also the best of all the chattels; half of that for the middlemost, and the fourth of that for the youngest.

9.s: jyeṣṭhaścaiva kaniṣṭhaśca saṃharetāṃ yathauditam ye 'nye jyeṣṭhakaniṣṭhābhyāṃ teṣāṃ syān madhyamaṃ dhanam
9.d: ज्येष्ठश्चैव कनिष्ठश्च संहरेतां यथौदितम् ये ऽन्ये ज्येष्ठकनिष्ठाभ्यां तेषां स्यान् मध्यमं धनम्
9.e: The eldest and the youngest shall receive their property according to the rule just stated; to those other than the eldest and the youngest, would belong the middlemost share.

9.s: sarveṣāṃ dhanajātānāmādadītāgryamagrajaḥ yacca sātiśayaṃ kiṃ ciddaśataścāpnuyādvaram
9.d: सर्वेषां धनजातानामाददीताग्र्यमग्रजः यच्च सातिशयं किं चिद्दशतश्चाप्नुयाद्वरम्
9.e: Among the goods of every kind, the first-born shall take the best; as also anything that may be particularly good; as well as the best of ten animals.

9.s: uddhāro na daśasvasti saṃpannānāṃ svakarmasu yat kiṃ cideva deyaṃ tu jyāyase mānavardhanam
9.d: उद्धारो न दशस्वस्ति संपन्नानां स्वकर्मसु यत् किं चिदेव देयं तु ज्यायसे मानवर्धनम्
9.e: But there is to be no additional share ‘out of ten,’ if all the brothers are efficient in their occupations; some little thing however shall be given to the eldest, as a mark of respect.

9.s: evaṃ samuddhṛtauddhāre samānaṃśān prakalpayet uddhāre 'nuddhṛte tveṣāmiyaṃ syādaṃśakalpanā
9.d: एवं समुद्धृतौद्धारे समानंशान् प्रकल्पयेत् उद्धारे ऽनुद्धृते त्वेषामियं स्यादंशकल्पना
9.e: After the ‘additional share’ has been thus deducted, equal shares shall be allotted. But if no additional share has been deducted, the allotment of shares shall be in this (following) manner,

9.s: ekādhikaṃ harej jyeṣṭhaḥ putro 'dhyardhaṃ tato 'nujaḥ aṃśamaṃśaṃ yavīyāṃsa iti dharmo vyavasthitaḥ
9.d: एकाधिकं हरेज् ज्येष्ठः पुत्रो ऽध्यर्धं ततो ऽनुजः अंशमंशं यवीयांस इति धर्मो व्यवस्थितः
9.e: The eldest son shall take one share in excess; the one born next to him a share and a half; and the younger ones one share each; such is the settled law.

9.s: svebhyo 'ṃśebhyastu kanyābhyaḥ pradadyurbhrātaraḥ pṛthak svābhyaḥ svābhyastu svāt svādaṃśāccaturbhāgaṃ patitāḥ syuraditsavaḥ
9.d: स्वेभ्यो ऽंशेभ्यस्तु कन्याभ्यः प्रदद्युर्भ्रातरः पृथक् स्वाभ्यः स्वाभ्यस्तु स्वात् स्वादंशाच्चतुर्भागं पतिताः स्युरदित्सवः
9.e: To the maidens of the same caste, the brothers shall each severally give the fourth part of his share; those not inclined to give would be outcasts

9.s: ajāvikaṃ sekaśaphaṃ na jātu viṣamaṃ bhajet 'jāvikaṃ caikaśaphaṃ ajāvikaṃ tu viṣamaṃ jyeṣṭhasyaiva vidhīyate
9.d: अजाविकं सेकशफं न जातु विषमं भजेत् ऽजाविकं चैकशफं अजाविकं तु विषमं ज्येष्ठस्यैव विधीयते
9.e: One shall not divide an odd goat, or sheep, or an animal with uncleft hoofs; the odd goat or sheep is declared to belong to the eldest.

9.s: yavīyānjyeṣṭhabhāryāyāṃ putramutpādayedyadi samastatra vibhāgaḥ syāditi dharmo vyavasthitaḥ
9.d: यवीयान्ज्येष्ठभार्यायां पुत्रमुत्पादयेद्यदि समस्तत्र विभागः स्यादिति धर्मो व्यवस्थितः
9.e: If the younger brother begets a son on the wife of the elder, the division in that case shall be equal; such is the settled law.

9.s: upasarjanaṃ pradhānasya dharmato naupapadyate pitā pradhānaṃ prajane tasmāddharmeṇa taṃ bhajet
9.d: उपसर्जनं प्रधानस्य धर्मतो नौपपद्यते पिता प्रधानं प्रजने तस्माद्धर्मेण तं भजेत्
9.e: The Secondary cannot rightly be (equal to) the primary; because in procreation, the father is the primary, therefore he (the secondary) should be treated accordinc, to the law (stated before).

9.s: putraḥ kaniṣṭho jyeṣṭhāyāṃ kaniṣṭhāyāṃ ca pūrvajaḥ kathaṃ tatra vibhāgaḥ syāditi cet saṃśayo bhavet
9.d: पुत्रः कनिष्ठो ज्येष्ठायां कनिष्ठायां च पूर्वजः कथं तत्र विभागः स्यादिति चेत् संशयो भवेत्
9.e: ‘In case the younger son is born of the elder wife, and the elder one of the younger wife,—how would the partition be made?’—If such a doubt arises,—the son born of the elder wife shall take one bull as his ‘preferential share;’ the other bulls, which are not so good, shall belong to those who are junior to him, on account of the position of their mothers.

9.s: ekaṃ vṛṣabhamuddhāraṃ saṃhareta sa pūrvajaḥ tato 'pare jyeṣṭhavṛṣāstadūnānāṃ svamātṛtaḥ
9.d: एकं वृषभमुद्धारं संहरेत स पूर्वजः ततो ऽपरे ज्येष्ठवृषास्तदूनानां स्वमातृतः
9.e: ‘In case the younger son is born of the elder wife, and the elder one of the younger wife,—how would the partition be made?’—If such a doubt arises,—the son born of the elder wife shall take one bull as his ‘preferential share;’ the other bulls, which are not so good, shall belong to those who are junior to him, on account of the position of their mothers.

9.s: jyeṣṭhastu jāto jyeṣṭhāyāṃ haredvṛṣabhaṣoḍaśāḥ tataḥ svamātṛtaḥ śeṣā bhajeranniti dhāraṇā
9.d: ज्येष्ठस्तु जातो ज्येष्ठायां हरेद्वृषभषोडशाः ततः स्वमातृतः शेषा भजेरन्निति धारणा
9.e: The elder son born of the younger wife may take (fifteen cows with) a bull as the sixteenth; the others may take shares according to the seniority of their mothers; such is the settled rule.

9.s: sadṛśastrīṣu jātānāṃ putrāṇāmaviśeṣataḥ na mātṛto jyaiṣṭhyamasti janmato jyaiṣṭhyamucyate
9.d: सदृशस्त्रीषु जातानां पुत्राणामविशेषतः न मातृतो ज्यैष्ठ्यमस्ति जन्मतो ज्यैष्ठ्यमुच्यते
9.e: Among sons born of equal wives,—if there is no other distinction,—there is no seniority on account of their mothers; seniority is declared to be by birth only.

9.s: janmajyeṣṭhena cāhvānaṃ subrahmaṇyāsvapi smṛtam yamayoścaiva garbheṣu janmato jyeṣṭhatā smṛtā
9.d: जन्मज्येष्ठेन चाह्वानं सुब्रह्मण्यास्वपि स्मृतम् यमयोश्चैव गर्भेषु जन्मतो ज्येष्ठता स्मृता
9.e: In theSubrahmaṇyātext also, the invocation has been declared as to be done by the son who is eldest by birth. Between sons conceived as twins, seniority has been declared to be dependent upon birth.

9.s: aputro 'nena vidhinā sutāṃ kurvīta putrikām yadapatyaṃ bhavedasyāṃ tan mama syāt svadhākaram
9.d: अपुत्रो ऽनेन विधिना सुतां कुर्वीत पुत्रिकाम् यदपत्यं भवेदस्यां तन् मम स्यात् स्वधाकरम्
9.e: He who has no son may make his daughter an ‘appointed daughter’ in the following manner: [He shall mark the declaration]—‘The child that may bk born of her shall be the performer of my funeral rites’.

9.s: anena tu vidhānena purā cakre 'tha putrikāḥ vivṛddhyarthaṃ svavaṃśasya svayaṃ dakṣaḥ prajāpatiḥ
9.d: अनेन तु विधानेन पुरा चक्रे ऽथ पुत्रिकाः विवृद्ध्यर्थं स्ववंशस्य स्वयं दक्षः प्रजापतिः
9.e: In ancient timesDakṣa Prajāpatihimself made ‘appointed daughters’ in this same manner, for the purpose of multiplying his race.

9.s: dadau sa daśa dharmāya kaśyapāya trayodaśa somāya rājñe satkṛtya prītātmā saptaviṃśatim
9.d: ददौ स दश धर्माय कश्यपाय त्रयोदश सोमाय राज्ञे सत्कृत्य प्रीतात्मा सप्तविंशतिम्
9.e: He gave ten to Dharma, thirteen to Kaśyapa, and twenty-seven to King Soma,—having honoured them with an affectionate heart.

9.s: yathaivātmā tathā putraḥ putreṇa duhitā samā tasyāmātmani tiṣṭhantyāṃ kathamanyo dhanaṃ haret
9.d: यथैवात्मा तथा पुत्रः पुत्रेण दुहिता समा तस्यामात्मनि तिष्ठन्त्यां कथमन्यो धनं हरेत्
9.e: The son is as one’s own self, and the daughter is equal to the son; hence so long as she is there in her own real character, how can anyone else take his property?

9.s: mātustu yautakaṃ yat syāt kumārībhāga eva saḥ dauhitra eva ca haredaputrasyākhilaṃ dhanam
9.d: मातुस्तु यौतकं यत् स्यात् कुमारीभाग एव सः दौहित्र एव च हरेदपुत्रस्याखिलं धनम्
9.e: Whatever may be the separate property of the mother is the share of the unmarried daughter alone; and the daughter’s son shall inherit the entire property of the man who has no son.

9.s: dauhitro hyakhilaṃ rikthamaputrasya piturharet sa eva dadyāddvau piṇḍau pitre mātāmahāya ca
9.d: दौहित्रो ह्यखिलं रिक्थमपुत्रस्य पितुर्हरेत् स एव दद्याद्द्वौ पिण्डौ पित्रे मातामहाय च
9.e: The daughter’s son should inherit the entire property of the sonless father; he shall also offer two cakes—to the ‘father’ and to the ‘maternal grandfather.’

9.s: pautradauhitrayorloke na viśeṣo 'sti dharmataḥ tayorhi mātāpitarau saṃbhūtau tasya dehataḥ
9.d: पौत्रदौहित्रयोर्लोके न विशेषो ऽस्ति धर्मतः तयोर्हि मातापितरौ संभूतौ तस्य देहतः
9.e: In this world, between the son’s son and the daughter’s son there is no difference, in law; for the father and mother of each of them were both born of h is own body.

9.s: putrikāyāṃ kṛtāyāṃ tu yadi putro 'nujāyate samastatra vibhāgaḥ syātjyeṣṭhatā nāsti hi striyāḥ
9.d: पुत्रिकायां कृतायां तु यदि पुत्रो ऽनुजायते समस्तत्र विभागः स्यात्ज्येष्ठता नास्ति हि स्त्रियाः
9.e: But if a son happen to be born after the daughter has been ‘appointed,’ the division must be equal; as there is no seniority for the woman.

9.s: aputrāyāṃ mṛtāyāṃ tu putrikāyāṃ kathaṃ cana dhanaṃ tat putrikābhartā haretaivāvicārayan
9.d: अपुत्रायां मृतायां तु पुत्रिकायां कथं चन धनं तत् पुत्रिकाभर्ता हरेतैवाविचारयन्
9.e: If the appointed daughter happen to die without a son, the husband of that appointed daughter may, without hesitation, take that property.

9.s: akṛtā vā kṛtā vā 'pi yaṃ vindet sadṛśāt sutam pautrī mātāmahastena dadyāt piṇḍaṃ hareddhanam
9.d: अकृता वा कृता वा ऽपि यं विन्देत् सदृशात् सुतम् पौत्री मातामहस्तेन दद्यात् पिण्डं हरेद्धनम्
9.e: Either appointed on not appointed, if a daughter bears a son to a husband of equal status, through that son does the maternal grandfather become endowed with a ‘son’s son’; he shall offer the funeral cake and inherit his property.

9.s: putreṇa lokānjayati pautreṇānantyamaśnute atha putrasya pautreṇa bradhnasyāpnoti viṣṭapam
9.d: पुत्रेण लोकान्जयति पौत्रेणानन्त्यमश्नुते अथ पुत्रस्य पौत्रेण ब्रध्नस्याप्नोति विष्टपम्
9.e: Through the son one conquers the worlds, through the grandson he obtains immortality, and through the son’s grandson he attains the regions of the Sun.

9.s: putnāmno narakādyasmāt trāyate pitaraṃ sutaḥ tasmāt putra iti proktaḥ svayameva svayaṃbhuvā
9.d: पुत्नाम्नो नरकाद्यस्मात् त्रायते पितरं सुतः तस्मात् पुत्र इति प्रोक्तः स्वयमेव स्वयंभुवा
9.e: Because the Son delivers his father from the hell called ‘Put,’ therefore has he been called ‘Putra,’ ‘Deliverer from Put,’ by the Self-existent One Himself.

9.s: pautradauhitrayorloke viśeṣo naupapadyate dauhitro 'pi hyamutrainaṃ saṃtārayati pautravat
9.d: पौत्रदौहित्रयोर्लोके विशेषो नौपपद्यते दौहित्रो ऽपि ह्यमुत्रैनं संतारयति पौत्रवत्
9.e: Between the Son’s son and the Daughter’s son there is no difference in the world; since the daughter’s son also, like the son’s son, saves the man in the next world.

9.s: mātuḥ prathamataḥ piṇḍaṃ nirvapet putrikāsutaḥ dvitīyaṃ tu pitustasyāstṛtīyaṃ tatpituḥ pituḥ
9.d: मातुः प्रथमतः पिण्डं निर्वपेत् पुत्रिकासुतः द्वितीयं तु पितुस्तस्यास्तृतीयं तत्पितुः पितुः
9.e: The son of the Appointed Daughter shall offer the first cake to his mother, the second to her father and the third to his father’s father.

9.s: upapanno guṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ putro yasya tu dattrimaḥ sa haretaiva tadrikthaṃ saṃprāpto 'pyanyagotrataḥ
9.d: उपपन्नो गुणैः सर्वैः पुत्रो यस्य तु दत्त्रिमः स हरेतैव तद्रिक्थं संप्राप्तो ऽप्यन्यगोत्रतः
9.e: If one has an adopted son endowed with all good qualities, he shall inherit his property, even though he may have come from another family.

9.s: gotrarikthe janayiturna hareddattrimaḥ kva cit gotrarikthānugaḥ piṇḍo vyapaiti dadataḥ svadhā
9.d: गोत्ररिक्थे जनयितुर्न हरेद्दत्त्रिमः क्व चित् गोत्ररिक्थानुगः पिण्डो व्यपैति ददतः स्वधा
9.e: The adopted son shall not take the family-name or the property of his progenitor; the cake follows the family-name and the property; for him therefore who gives away his son the funeral offerings cease.

9.s: aniyuktāsutaścaiva putriṇyā 'ptaśca devarāt ubhau tau nārhato bhāgaṃ jārajātakakāmajau
9.d: अनियुक्तासुतश्चैव पुत्रिण्या ऽप्तश्च देवरात् उभौ तौ नार्हतो भागं जारजातककामजौ
9.e: The offspring of a wife not ‘authorised,’ and the offspring obtained from her younger brother-in-law by a woman who has already got a son,—both of these are undeserving of a share; one being born of an adulterer, and the other being the product of lust.

9.s: niyuktāyāmapi pumānnāryāṃ jāto 'vidhānataḥ naivārhaḥ paitṛkaṃ rikthaṃ patitautpādito hi saḥ
9.d: नियुक्तायामपि पुमान्नार्यां जातो ऽविधानतः नैवार्हः पैतृकं रिक्थं पतितौत्पादितो हि सः
9.e: The made child of an ‘authorised’ woman, if not begotten in the prescribed manner, is not entitled to the paternal property; as he is procreated by outcasts.

9.s: haret tatra niyuktāyāṃ jātaḥ putro yathā 'urasaḥ kṣetrikasya tu tadbījaṃ dharmataḥ prasavaśca saḥ
9.d: हरेत् तत्र नियुक्तायां जातः पुत्रो यथा ऽउरसः क्षेत्रिकस्य तु तद्बीजं धर्मतः प्रसवश्च सः
9.e: The son born of the ‘authorised’ woman shall inherit, like the ‘legitimate’ son; as legally that seed is of the owner of the soil and the offspring belongs to him.

9.s: dhanaṃ yo bibhṛyādbhrāturmṛtasya striyameva ca so 'patyaṃ bhrāturutpādya dadyāt tasyaiva taddhanam
9.d: धनं यो बिभृयाद्भ्रातुर्मृतस्य स्त्रियमेव च सो ऽपत्यं भ्रातुरुत्पाद्य दद्यात् तस्यैव तद्धनम्
9.e: This rule refers to the case where the dead brother was one who had separated from the surviving brother; while the preceding verse was meant for that where the two brothers lived together. This is the only difference between this and the foregoing rules.

9.s: yā niyuktā 'nyataḥ putraṃ devarādvā 'pyavāpnuyāt taṃ kāmajamarikthīyaṃ vṛthautpannaṃ pracakṣate mithyautpannaṃ
9.d: या नियुक्ता ऽन्यतः पुत्रं देवराद्वा ऽप्यवाप्नुयात् तं कामजमरिक्थीयं वृथौत्पन्नं प्रचक्षते मिथ्यौत्पन्नं
9.e: If a woman, without being ‘authorised,’ bears a son either to her broth er-in-law or to some other person, that son they declare to be‘lust-born,’ ‘incapable of inheritance’ and‘born in vain.’

9.s: etadvidhānaṃ vijñeyaṃ vibhāgasyaikayoniṣu bahvīṣu caikajātānāṃ nānāstrīṣu nibodhata
9.d: एतद्विधानं विज्ञेयं विभागस्यैकयोनिषु बह्वीषु चैकजातानां नानास्त्रीषु निबोधत
9.e: This rule should be understood as applying to partition among sons born of wives of the same caste; listen to that applying to that among sons born to one man of several and diverse wives.

9.s: brāhmaṇasyānupūrvyeṇa catasrastu yadi striyaḥ tāsāṃ putreṣu jāteṣu vibhāge 'yaṃ vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
9.d: ब्राह्मणस्यानुपूर्व्येण चतस्रस्तु यदि स्त्रियः तासां पुत्रेषु जातेषु विभागे ऽयं विधिः स्मृतः
9.e: If to aBrāhmaṇathere be four wives in due order,—for partition among the sons born of these, the rule has been declared to be as follows.

9.s: kīnāśo govṛṣo yānamalaṅkāraśca veśma ca viprasyauddhārikaṃ deyamekāṃśaśca pradhānataḥ
9.d: कीनाशो गोवृषो यानमलङ्कारश्च वेश्म च विप्रस्यौद्धारिकं देयमेकांशश्च प्रधानतः
9.e: The ploughman, the breeding bull, the conveyance, the ornament, and the house shall be given as the ‘preferential share’ to theBrāhmaṇa, as also one principal share.

9.s: tryaṃśaṃ dāyāddharedvipro dvāvaṃśau kṣatriyāsutaḥ vaiśyājaḥ sārdhamevāṃśamaṃśaṃ śūdrāsuto haret
9.d: त्र्यंशं दायाद्धरेद्विप्रो द्वावंशौ क्षत्रियासुतः वैश्याजः सार्धमेवांशमंशं शूद्रासुतो हरेत्
9.e: Out of the estate theBrāhmaṇashall take three shares; the son of theKṣatriyamother two shares; the son of theVaiśyamother a share and a half; and the son of theŚūdramother one share.

9.s: sarvaṃ vā rikthajātaṃ taddaśadhā parikalpya ca dharmyaṃ vibhāgaṃ kurvīta vidhinā 'nena dharmavit
9.d: सर्वं वा रिक्थजातं तद्दशधा परिकल्प्य च धर्म्यं विभागं कुर्वीत विधिना ऽनेन धर्मवित्
9.e: The man knowing the law shall divide the entire estate into ten parts, and then make an equitable division according to the following rule.

9.s: caturo 'ṃśān haredviprastrīnaṃśān kṣatriyāsutaḥ vaiśyāputro hareddvyaṃśamaṃśaṃ śūdrāsuto haret
9.d: चतुरो ऽंशान् हरेद्विप्रस्त्रीनंशान् क्षत्रियासुतः वैश्यापुत्रो हरेद्द्व्यंशमंशं शूद्रासुतो हरेत्
9.e: TheBrāhmaṇashall take four shares, and the son of theKṣatriyamother three shares; the son of theVaiśyamother shall take two shares, and the son of theŚūdramother shall take one share.

9.s: yadyapi syāt tu satputro 'pyasatputro 'pi vā bhavet yadyapi syāt tu satputro yadyaputro 'pi vā bhavet nādhikaṃ daśamāddadyātśūdrāputrāya dharmataḥ
9.d: यद्यपि स्यात् तु सत्पुत्रो ऽप्यसत्पुत्रो ऽपि वा भवेत् यद्यपि स्यात् तु सत्पुत्रो यद्यपुत्रो ऽपि वा भवेत् नाधिकं दशमाद्दद्यात्शूद्रापुत्राय धर्मतः
9.e: Whether aBrāhmaṇahas a son or no son, he shall not, according to law, allot more than the tenth part to the son of theŚūdrawife.

9.s: brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāputro na rikthabhāk yadevāsya pitā dadyāt tadevāsya dhanaṃ bhavet
9.d: ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्रापुत्रो न रिक्थभाक् यदेवास्य पिता दद्यात् तदेवास्य धनं भवेत्
9.e: Of theBrāhmaṇa, theKṣatriyaand theVaiśya, the son born of aŚūdrawife is not an inheritor of property; his property shall consist of whatever his father may give to him.

9.s: samavarṇāsu vā jātāḥ sarve putrā dvijanmanām uddhāraṃ jyāyase dattvā bhajerannitare samam
9.d: समवर्णासु वा जाताः सर्वे पुत्रा द्विजन्मनाम् उद्धारं ज्यायसे दत्त्वा भजेरन्नितरे समम्
9.e: Or, all the sons of twice-born men, born of wives of the same caste, shall divide the property equally, after the others have given to the eldest his ‘preferential share.’

9.s: śūdrasya tu savarṇaiva nānyā bhāryā vidhīyate tasyāṃ jātāḥ samāṃśāḥ syuryadi putraśataṃ bhavet
9.d: शूद्रस्य तु सवर्णैव नान्या भार्या विधीयते तस्यां जाताः समांशाः स्युर्यदि पुत्रशतं भवेत्
9.e: For theŚūdrais ordained a wife of his own caste only, and no other; and all the sons born of her shall be entitled to equal shares, even if there be a hundred sons.

9.s: putrān dvādaśa yānāha nr̥̄ṇāṃ svāyaṃbhuvo manuḥ teṣāṃ ṣaḍ bandhudāyādāḥ ṣaḍadāyādabāndhavāḥ
9.d: पुत्रान् द्वादश यानाह न्र्̥̄णां स्वायंभुवो मनुः तेषां षड् बन्धुदायादाः षडदायादबान्धवाः
9.e: Among the twelve kinds of sons that Manu sprung from the Self-existent one has mentioned,—six are kinsmen as well as heirs, and six are kinsmen, not heirs.

9.s: aurasaḥ kṣetrajaścaiva dattaḥ kṛtrima eva ca gūḍhautpanno 'paviddhaśca dāyādā bāndhavāśca ṣaṭ
9.d: औरसः क्षेत्रजश्चैव दत्तः कृत्रिम एव च गूढौत्पन्नो ऽपविद्धश्च दायादा बान्धवाश्च षट्
9.e: (1) The ‘Kānīna,’ ‘maiden-born,’ (2) the ‘Sahoḍha,’ ‘received along with the wife,’ (3) the ‘Krīta,’ ‘bought,’ (4) the ‘Paunarbhava’ ‘begotten on a remarried woman,’ (5) the ‘Svayandatta,’ ‘self-offered’ and (6) the ‘Śaudra,’ ‘Śūdra-born,’—these six are only kinsmen, not heirs.

9.s: kānīnaśca sahoḍhaśca krītaḥ paunarbhavastathā svayaṃdattaśca śaudraśca ṣaḍadāyādabāndhavāḥ
9.d: कानीनश्च सहोढश्च क्रीतः पौनर्भवस्तथा स्वयंदत्तश्च शौद्रश्च षडदायादबान्धवाः
9.e: (1) The ‘Kānīna,’ ‘maiden-born,’ (2) the ‘Sahoḍha,’ ‘received along with the wife,’ (3) the ‘Krīta,’ ‘bought,’ (4) the ‘Paunarbhava’ ‘begotten on a remarried woman,’ (5) the ‘Svayandatta,’ ‘self-offered’ and (6) the ‘Śaudra,’ ‘Śūdra-born,’—these six are only kinsmen, not heirs.

9.s: yādṛśaṃ phalamāpnoti kuplavaiḥ saṃtaranjalam tādṛśaṃ phalamāpnoti kuputraiḥ saṃtaraṃstamaḥ
9.d: यादृशं फलमाप्नोति कुप्लवैः संतरन्जलम् तादृशं फलमाप्नोति कुपुत्रैः संतरंस्तमः
9.e: The man who tries to cross the gloom with the help of bad sons obtains results similar to those obtained by one who tries to cross the water with the help of unsound boats.

9.s: yadyekarikthinau syātāmaurasakṣetrajau sutau yasya yat paitṛkaṃ rikthaṃ sa tadgṛhṇīta naitaraḥ
9.d: यद्येकरिक्थिनौ स्यातामौरसक्षेत्रजौ सुतौ यस्य यत् पैतृकं रिक्थं स तद्गृह्णीत नैतरः
9.e: If the ‘Soil-born’ and the ‘body-born’ sons are both entitled to inherit the same property, each shall receive that property which belongs to his own father, and not the other.

9.s: eka evaurasaḥ putraḥ pitryasya vasunaḥ prabhuḥ śeṣāṇāmānṛśaṃsyārthaṃ pradadyāt tu prajīvanam
9.d: एक एवौरसः पुत्रः पित्र्यस्य वसुनः प्रभुः शेषाणामानृशंस्यार्थं प्रदद्यात् तु प्रजीवनम्
9.e: The ‘legitimate’ (body-born) son is alone the owner of the paternal estate; but in order toavoid unkindness, he shall provide subsistence for the rest.

9.s: ṣaṣṭhaṃ tu kṣetrajasyāṃśaṃ pradadyāt paitṛkāddhanāt auraso vibhajan dāyaṃ pitryaṃ pañcamameva vā
9.d: षष्ठं तु क्षेत्रजस्यांशं प्रदद्यात् पैतृकाद्धनात् औरसो विभजन् दायं पित्र्यं पञ्चममेव वा
9.e: When the legitimate son is dividing the paternal estate, he shall give to the ‘Kṣetraja’ son one-sixth or one-fifth part of the father’s property.

9.s: aurasakṣetrajau putrau pitṛrikthasya bhāginau daśāpare tu kramaśo gotrarikthāṃśabhāginaḥ
9.d: औरसक्षेत्रजौ पुत्रौ पितृरिक्थस्य भागिनौ दशापरे तु क्रमशो गोत्ररिक्थांशभागिनः
9.e: The ‘body-born’ and the ‘soil-born’ are entitled to inherit the father’s property; while the other ten inherit the ‘family-title’ and a share in the property, according to their order

9.s: svakṣetre saṃskṛtāyāṃ tu svayamutpādayeddhi yam tamaurasaṃ vijānīyāt putraṃ prāthamakalpikam
9.d: स्वक्षेत्रे संस्कृतायां तु स्वयमुत्पादयेद्धि यम् तमौरसं विजानीयात् पुत्रं प्राथमकल्पिकम्
9.e: Him whom a man himself begets in his own sanctified ‘soil,’—one shall know as the ‘body-born’ (legitimate) son, (declared) to be the first in order.

9.s: yastalpajaḥ pramītasya klībasya vyādhitasya vā svadharmeṇa niyuktāyāṃ sa putraḥ kṣetrajaḥ smṛtaḥ
9.d: यस्तल्पजः प्रमीतस्य क्लीबस्य व्याधितस्य वा स्वधर्मेण नियुक्तायां स पुत्रः क्षेत्रजः स्मृतः
9.e: If a son is born of the wife of a man, either dead or impotent or diseased, by one who has been duly ‘authorised,’—that son is declared to be ‘kṣetraja’ ‘soil-born.’

9.s: mātā pitā vā dadyātāṃ yamadbhiḥ putramāpadi sadṛśaṃ prītisaṃyuktaṃ sa jñeyo dattrimaḥ sutaḥ
9.d: माता पिता वा दद्यातां यमद्भिः पुत्रमापदि सदृशं प्रीतिसंयुक्तं स ज्ञेयो दत्त्रिमः सुतः
9.e: When in times of distress, the mother or the father affectionately gives away, with water-libations, a worthy son,—that son is called ‘given’ (adopted).

9.s: sadṛśaṃ tu prakuryādyaṃ guṇadoṣavicakṣaṇam putraṃ putraguṇairyuktaṃ sa vijñeyaśca kṛtrimaḥ
9.d: सदृशं तु प्रकुर्याद्यं गुणदोषविचक्षणम् पुत्रं पुत्रगुणैर्युक्तं स विज्ञेयश्च कृत्रिमः
9.e: When one appoints a son who is worthy, capable of discerning right and wrong, and endowed with filial virtues,—that son is to be known as “appointed.’

9.s: utpadyate gṛhe yastu na ca jñāyeta kasya saḥ sa gṛhe gūḍha utpannastasya syādyasya talpajaḥ
9.d: उत्पद्यते गृहे यस्तु न च ज्ञायेत कस्य सः स गृहे गूढ उत्पन्नस्तस्य स्याद्यस्य तल्पजः
9.e: If a son is born in a man’s house, and it is not known whose he is,—this son ‘secretly born’ in the house shall belong to him of whose wife he is born.

9.s: mātāpitṛbhyāmutsṛṣṭaṃ tayoranyatareṇa vā yaṃ putraṃ parigṛhṇīyādapaviddhaḥ sa ucyate
9.d: मातापितृभ्यामुत्सृष्टं तयोरन्यतरेण वा यं पुत्रं परिगृह्णीयादपविद्धः स उच्यते
9.e: If a man takes up a son deserted by his parents, or by either of them, he is called the ‘cast off son.’

9.s: pitṛveśmani kanyā tu yaṃ putraṃ janayedrahaḥ taṃ kānīnaṃ vadennāmnā voḍhuḥ kanyāsamudbhavam
9.d: पितृवेश्मनि कन्या तु यं पुत्रं जनयेद्रहः तं कानीनं वदेन्नाम्ना वोढुः कन्यासमुद्भवम्
9.e: If a maiden secretly bears a son in her father’s house, that son, born of a maiden, should be declared as ‘maiden-born’ by name, and to belong to the man who marries her.

9.s: yā garbhiṇī saṃskriyate jñātā 'jñātā 'pi vā satī voḍhuḥ sa garbho bhavati sahoḍha iti caucyate
9.d: या गर्भिणी संस्क्रियते ज्ञाता ऽज्ञाता ऽपि वा सती वोढुः स गर्भो भवति सहोढ इति चौच्यते
9.e: If one marries, knowingly or unknowingly, a pregnant maiden, the child in her womb belongs to him who marries her, and is called ‘received along with the wife.’

9.s: krīṇīyādyastvapatyārthaṃ mātāpitroryamantikāt sa krītakaḥ sutastasya sadṛśo 'sadṛśo 'pi vā
9.d: क्रीणीयाद्यस्त्वपत्यार्थं मातापित्रोर्यमन्तिकात् स क्रीतकः सुतस्तस्य सदृशो ऽसदृशो ऽपि वा
9.e: If a man buys a boy, worthy or unworthy, from his father and mother, with a view to making him his son, that son is called ‘bought.’

9.s: yā patyā vā parityaktā vidhavā vā svayaicchayā utpādayet punarbhūtvā sa paunarbhava ucyate
9.d: या पत्या वा परित्यक्ता विधवा वा स्वयैच्छया उत्पादयेत् पुनर्भूत्वा स पौनर्भव उच्यते
9.e: If a woman abandoned by her husband, or a widow, of her own accord, marries again and bears a son, that son is called ‘the son of a re-married woman.’

9.s: sā cedakṣatayoniḥ syādgatapratyāgatā 'pi vā paunarbhavena bhartrā sā punaḥ saṃskāramarhati
9.d: सा चेदक्षतयोनिः स्याद्गतप्रत्यागता ऽपि वा पौनर्भवेन भर्त्रा सा पुनः संस्कारमर्हति
9.e: In case she be still a virgin, or having gone away comes back,—she is fit to undergo re-marriage with her second husband.

9.s: mātāpitṛvihīno yastyakto vā syādakāraṇāt ātmānamarpayedyasmai svayaṃdattastu sa smṛtaḥ
9.d: मातापितृविहीनो यस्त्यक्तो वा स्यादकारणात् आत्मानमर्पयेद्यस्मै स्वयंदत्तस्तु स स्मृतः
9.e: If a boy, being deprived of his parents, or being abandoned by them without cause, offers himself to a man,—he is called the‘self-offered son.’

9.s: yaṃ brāhmaṇastu śūdrāyāṃ kāmādutpādayet sutam sa pārayanneva śavastasmāt pāraśavaḥ smṛtaḥ
9.d: यं ब्राह्मणस्तु शूद्रायां कामादुत्पादयेत् सुतम् स पारयन्नेव शवस्तस्मात् पारशवः स्मृतः
9.e: If aBrāhmaṇa, through lust, begets a son on aŚūdrawoman, he is as a corpse, even though living, and hence called the ‘living corpse.’

9.s: dāsyāṃ vā dāsadāsyāṃ vā yaḥ śūdrasya suto bhavet so 'nujñāto haredaṃśamiti dharmo vyavasthitaḥ
9.d: दास्यां वा दासदास्यां वा यः शूद्रस्य सुतो भवेत् सो ऽनुज्ञातो हरेदंशमिति धर्मो व्यवस्थितः
9.e: If a son is born to aŚūdrafrom a female slave, or from the female slave of a slave, he shall, when permitted, receive a share; such is the settled law.

9.s: kṣetrajādīn sutānetānekādaśa yathauditān putrapratinidhīnāhuḥ kriyālopān manīṣiṇaḥ
9.d: क्षेत्रजादीन् सुतानेतानेकादश यथौदितान् पुत्रप्रतिनिधीनाहुः क्रियालोपान् मनीषिणः
9.e: These eleven, the ‘soil-born’ and the rest, as here described, the wise ones call ‘substitutes of a son,’—taken with a view to the failure of a religious duty.

9.s: ya ete 'bhihitāḥ putrāḥ prasaṅgādanyabījajāḥ yasya te bījato jātāstasya te naitarasya tu
9.d: य एते ऽभिहिताः पुत्राः प्रसङ्गादन्यबीजजाः यस्य ते बीजतो जातास्तस्य ते नैतरस्य तु
9.e: Those sons born of the seed of strangers that have been described here by the way, belong to him from whose seed they are born, and not to any other person.

9.s: bhrātr̥̄ṇāmekajātānāmekaścet putravān bhavet sarvāṃstāṃstena putreṇa putriṇo manurabravīt
9.d: भ्रात्र्̥̄णामेकजातानामेकश्चेत् पुत्रवान् भवेत् सर्वांस्तांस्तेन पुत्रेण पुत्रिणो मनुरब्रवीत्
9.e: Among brothers, born of the same father, if even one have a son, Manu has declared all of them to be ‘with son,’ through that son.

9.s: sarvāsāmekapatnīnāmekā cet putriṇī bhavet sarvāstāstena putreṇa prāha putravatīrmanuḥ
9.d: सर्वासामेकपत्नीनामेका चेत् पुत्रिणी भवेत् सर्वास्तास्तेन पुत्रेण प्राह पुत्रवतीर्मनुः
9.e: Among all the wives of one man, if one have a son, Manu has declared all of them to be ‘with son,’ through that son.

9.s: śreyasaḥ śreyaso 'lābhe pāpīyān rikthamarhati bahavaścet tu sadṛśāḥ sarve rikthasya bhāginaḥ
9.d: श्रेयसः श्रेयसो ऽलाभे पापीयान् रिक्थमर्हति बहवश्चेत् तु सदृशाः सर्वे रिक्थस्य भागिनः
9.e: On the failure of each superior kind of son, each next inferior one is entitled to inheritance; if there be several of the same class, all shall share the property.

9.s: na bhrātaro na pitaraḥ putrā rikthaharāḥ pituḥ pitā haredaputrasya rikthaṃ bhrātara eva ca
9.d: न भ्रातरो न पितरः पुत्रा रिक्थहराः पितुः पिता हरेदपुत्रस्य रिक्थं भ्रातर एव च
9.e: Sons alone shall inherit the father’s property, not brothers or fathers; but the father and brothers shall inherit the property of one who dies sonless.

9.s: trayāṇāmudakaṃ kāryaṃ triṣu piṇḍaḥ pravartate caturthaḥ saṃpradātaiṣāṃ pañcamo naupapadyate
9.d: त्रयाणामुदकं कार्यं त्रिषु पिण्डः प्रवर्तते चतुर्थः संप्रदातैषां पञ्चमो नौपपद्यते
9.e: To three should water-libation be offered; to three is the cake offered; the fourth is the giver of these offerings; there can be no fifth.

9.s: anantaraḥ sapiṇḍādyastasya tasya dhanaṃ bhavet ata ūrdhvaṃ sakulyaḥ syādācāryaḥ śiṣya eva vā
9.d: अनन्तरः सपिण्डाद्यस्तस्य तस्य धनं भवेत् अत ऊर्ध्वं सकुल्यः स्यादाचार्यः शिष्य एव वा
9.e: The property shall always devolve upon him who is nearest to the (deceased) ‘Sapiṇḍa’; after these either a ‘Sakulya’; or the Spiritual Preceptor, or the pupil.

9.s: sarveṣāmapyabhāve tu brāhmaṇā rikthabhāginaḥ traividyāḥ śucayo dāntāstathā dharmo na hīyate
9.d: सर्वेषामप्यभावे तु ब्राह्मणा रिक्थभागिनः त्रैविद्याः शुचयो दान्तास्तथा धर्मो न हीयते
9.e: But, on the failure of all, the property shall be taken byBrāhmaṇas, learned in the Vedas, pure and self-controlled; in this manner the law would not be violated.

9.s: ahāryaṃ brāhmaṇadravyaṃ rājñā nityamiti sthitiḥ itareṣāṃ tu varṇānāṃ sarvābhāve harennṛpaḥ
9.d: अहार्यं ब्राह्मणद्रव्यं राज्ञा नित्यमिति स्थितिः इतरेषां तु वर्णानां सर्वाभावे हरेन्नृपः
9.e: The property of theBrāhmaṇashoved never be taken by the King,—such is the law; but in the case of other castes, the king shall take the property, in the absence of all heirs.

9.s: saṃsthitasyānapatyasya sagotrāt putramāharet tatra yadrikthajātaṃ syāt tat tasmin pratipādayet
9.d: संस्थितस्यानपत्यस्य सगोत्रात् पुत्रमाहरेत् तत्र यद्रिक्थजातं स्यात् तत् तस्मिन् प्रतिपादयेत्
9.e: In the case of a man dying childless, if an issue is raised from a member of the same family, all the property that there may be shall be delivered to that child.

9.s: dvau tu yau vivadeyātāṃ dvābhyāṃ jātau striyā dhane tayoryadyasya pitryaṃ syāt tat sa gṛhṇīta naitaraḥ
9.d: द्वौ तु यौ विवदेयातां द्वाभ्यां जातौ स्त्रिया धने तयोर्यद्यस्य पित्र्यं स्यात् तत् स गृह्णीत नैतरः
9.e: But if two sons, born of two men, contend for the property in the mother’s possession, each shall take, to the exclusion of the other, what belonged to his own father.

9.s: jananyāṃ saṃsthitāyāṃ tu samaṃ sarve sahaudarāḥ bhajeran mātṛkaṃ rikthaṃ bhaginyaśca sanābhayaḥ
9.d: जनन्यां संस्थितायां तु समं सर्वे सहौदराः भजेरन् मातृकं रिक्थं भगिन्यश्च सनाभयः
9.e: When the mother has died, all the uterine brothers and uterine sisters shall divide the mother’s property equally.

9.s: yāstāsāṃ syurduhitarastāsāmapi yathārhataḥ tasyāṃ mātāmahyā dhanāt kiṃ cit pradeyaṃ prītipūrvakam
9.d: यास्तासां स्युर्दुहितरस्तासामपि यथार्हतः तस्यां मातामह्या धनात् किं चित् प्रदेयं प्रीतिपूर्वकम्
9.e: Even to the daughters of those daughters something shall be lovingly given, as is quite proper, out of the property of their maternal grandmother.

9.s: adhyagniadhyāvāhanikaṃ dattaṃ ca prītikarmaṇi bhrātṛmātṛpitṛprāptaṃ ṣaḍvidhaṃ strīdhanaṃ smṛtam
9.d: अध्यग्निअध्यावाहनिकं दत्तं च प्रीतिकर्मणि भ्रातृमातृपितृप्राप्तं षड्विधं स्त्रीधनं स्मृतम्
9.e: (1) What is given before the fire, (2) what is given at the time of departure, (3) what is given in token of love, and what is received from (4) the brother, (5) the mother and (6) the father,—has been declared to be ‘Strīdhana’ (the exclusive property of the woman).

9.s: anvādheyaṃ ca yaddattaṃ patyā prītena caiva yat patyau jīvati vṛttāyāḥ prajāyāstaddhanaṃ bhavet
9.d: अन्वाधेयं च यद्दत्तं पत्या प्रीतेन चैव यत् पत्यौ जीवति वृत्तायाः प्रजायास्तद्धनं भवेत्
9.e: Also the gift that is subsequently made to her by her loving husband, shall go to her offspring, if she dies while her husband is living.

9.s: brāhmadaivārṣagāndharvaprājāpatyeṣu yadvasu aprajāyāmatītāyāṃ bhartureva tadiṣyate
9.d: ब्राह्मदैवार्षगान्धर्वप्राजापत्येषु यद्वसु अप्रजायामतीतायां भर्तुरेव तदिष्यते
9.e: But the property given to a woman on the ‘Āsura’ or other (inferior) forms of marriage, has been held to belong to her parents, upon her dying childless.

9.s: yat tvasyāḥ syāddhanaṃ dattaṃ vivāheṣvāsurādiṣu aprajāyāmatītāyāṃ mātāpitrostadiṣyate
9.d: यत् त्वस्याः स्याद्धनं दत्तं विवाहेष्वासुरादिषु अप्रजायामतीतायां मातापित्रोस्तदिष्यते
9.e: But the property given to a woman on the ‘Āsura’ or other (inferior) forms of marriage, has been held to belong to her parents, upon her dying childless.

9.s: striyāṃ tu yadbhavedvittaṃ pitrā dattaṃ kathaṃ cana brāhmaṇī taddharet kanyā tadapatyasya vā bhavet
9.d: स्त्रियां तु यद्भवेद्वित्तं पित्रा दत्तं कथं चन ब्राह्मणी तद्धरेत् कन्या तदपत्यस्य वा भवेत्
9.e: The property that may have been given to a woman by her father shall be taken by the daughter of theBrāhamaṇa-caste; or it shall belong to the child of that daughter.

9.s: na nirhāraṃ striyaḥ kuryuḥ kuṭumbādbahumadhyagāt kṣ svakādapi ca vittāddhi svasya bharturanājñayā
9.d: न निर्हारं स्त्रियः कुर्युः कुटुम्बाद्बहुमध्यगात् क्ष् स्वकादपि च वित्ताद्धि स्वस्य भर्तुरनाज्ञया
9.e: Women shall never make a hoard out of the family-property common to many, nor out of their own property, without the husband’s permission.

9.s: patyau jīvati yaḥ strībhiralaṅkāro dhṛto bhavet na taṃ bhajeran dāyādā bhajamānāḥ patanti te
9.d: पत्यौ जीवति यः स्त्रीभिरलङ्कारो धृतो भवेत् न तं भजेरन् दायादा भजमानाः पतन्ति ते
9.e: The ornament worn by the woman during her husband’s life-time, her heirs shall not divide; if they divide it, they become outcasts.

9.s: anaṃśau klībapatitau jātyandhabadhirau tathā unmattajaḍamūkāśca ye ca ke cinnirindriyāḥ
9.d: अनंशौ क्लीबपतितौ जात्यन्धबधिरौ तथा उन्मत्तजडमूकाश्च ये च के चिन्निरिन्द्रियाः
9.e: Eunuchs and outcasts, those born blind or deaf, idiots and the dumb, as well as those deficient in any organ, are entitled to no shares.

9.s: sarveṣāmapi tu nyāyyaṃ dātuṃ śaktyā manīṣiṇā grāsācchādanamatyantaṃ patito hyadadadbhavet
9.d: सर्वेषामपि तु न्याय्यं दातुं शक्त्या मनीषिणा ग्रासाच्छादनमत्यन्तं पतितो ह्यददद्भवेत्
9.e: But it is fair that the wise man shall give even to all these food and clothing to the best of his ability; if he does not give it at all, he becomes an outcast.

9.s: yadyarthitā tu dāraiḥ syāt klībādīnāṃ kathaṃ cana teṣāmutpannatantūnāmapatyaṃ dāyamarhati
9.d: यद्यर्थिता तु दारैः स्यात् क्लीबादीनां कथं चन तेषामुत्पन्नतन्तूनामपत्यं दायमर्हति
9.e: If the eunuch and the rest should somehow happen to have longing for a wife, the child of such of them as have issue is entitled to inheritance.

9.s: yat kiṃ cit pitari prete dhanaṃ jyeṣṭho 'dhigacchati bhāgo yavīyasāṃ tatra yadi vidyānupālinaḥ
9.d: यत् किं चित् पितरि प्रेते धनं ज्येष्ठो ऽधिगच्छति भागो यवीयसां तत्र यदि विद्यानुपालिनः
9.e: Whatever property the eldest brother acquires after the death of the father, a share of that shall belong to the younger brothers, if they are devoted to learning.

9.s: avidyānāṃ tu sarveṣāmīhātaśceddhanaṃ bhavet samastatra vibhāgaḥ syādapitrya iti dhāraṇā
9.d: अविद्यानां तु सर्वेषामीहातश्चेद्धनं भवेत् समस्तत्र विभागः स्यादपित्र्य इति धारणा
9.e: But if all of them are unlearned, and the property is acquired by their labour,—the division in that case shall be equal, the property being not ancestral. such is the settled rule.

9.s: vidyādhanaṃ tu yadyasya tat tasyaiva dhanaṃ bhavet maitryamaudvāhikaṃ caiva mādhuparkikameva ca
9.d: विद्याधनं तु यद्यस्य तत् तस्यैव धनं भवेत् मैत्र्यमौद्वाहिकं चैव माधुपर्किकमेव च
9.e: The gains of learning shall be the sole property of the man by whom they have been acquired; as also friendly presents, marriage.—presents, and presents received in connection with the ‘honey—mixture.’

9.s: bhrātr̥̄ṇāṃ yastu naiheta dhanaṃ śaktaḥ svakarmaṇā sa nirbhājyaḥ svakādaṃśāt kiṃ ciddattvaupajīvanam
9.d: भ्रात्र्̥̄णां यस्तु नैहेत धनं शक्तः स्वकर्मणा स निर्भाज्यः स्वकादंशात् किं चिद्दत्त्वौपजीवनम्
9.e: Among brothers, if any one, being quite competent through his own profession, does not desire the property, he shall be debarred from his share, after a little has been given to him by way of maintenance.

9.s: anupaghnan pitṛdravyaṃ śrameṇa yadupārjitam svayamīhitalabdhaṃ tannākāmo dātumarhati
9.d: अनुपघ्नन् पितृद्रव्यं श्रमेण यदुपार्जितम् स्वयमीहितलब्धं तन्नाकामो दातुमर्हति
9.e: If one of them acquires something by his own effort, without interfering with the patrimony,—that property, being acquired by his own labour, he need not give to others, unless he himself wishes it.

9.s: paitṛkaṃ tu pitā dravyamanavāptaṃ yadāpnuyāt na tat putrairbhajet sārdhamakāmaḥ svayamarjitam
9.d: पैतृकं तु पिता द्रव्यमनवाप्तं यदाप्नुयात् न तत् पुत्रैर्भजेत् सार्धमकामः स्वयमर्जितम्
9.e: If the father recovers a lost ancestral property, he shall not, unless he so wishes, share it with his sons,—being, as it is his self-acquired property.

9.s: vibhaktāḥ saha jīvanto vibhajeran punaryadi samastatra vibhāgaḥ syāj jyaiṣṭhyaṃ tatra na vidyate
9.d: विभक्ताः सह जीवन्तो विभजेरन् पुनर्यदि समस्तत्र विभागः स्याज् ज्यैष्ठ्यं तत्र न विद्यते
9.e: If brothers, living together, after having divided once, happen to make a second partition, the division in that case shall be equal; in such cases there is no ‘primogeniture.’

9.s: yeṣāṃ jyeṣṭhaḥ kaniṣṭho vā hīyetāṃśapradānataḥ mriyetānyataro vā 'pi tasya bhāgo na lupyate
9.d: येषां ज्येष्ठः कनिष्ठो वा हीयेतांशप्रदानतः म्रियेतान्यतरो वा ऽपि तस्य भागो न लुप्यते
9.e: If the eldest or the youngest of the brothers should be deprived of his shares,—or if either of them dies,—his share does not become lost.

9.s: sodaryā vibhajeraṃstaṃ sametya sahitāḥ samam bhrātaro ye ca saṃsṛṣṭā bhāginyaśca sanābhayaḥ
9.d: सोदर्या विभजेरंस्तं समेत्य सहिताः समम् भ्रातरो ये च संसृष्टा भागिन्यश्च सनाभयः
9.e: His uterine brothers, coming together, shall divide it equally; as also the united brothers and consanguineous sisters.

9.s: yo jyeṣṭho vinikurvīta lobhādbhrātr̥̄n yavīyasaḥ so 'jyeṣṭhaḥ syādabhāgaśca niyantavyaśca rājabhiḥ
9.d: यो ज्येष्ठो विनिकुर्वीत लोभाद्भ्रात्र्̥̄न् यवीयसः सो ऽज्येष्ठः स्यादभागश्च नियन्तव्यश्च राजभिः
9.e: If an eldest brother, through avarice, defrauds the younger ones, he shall lose his ‘seniority’ and his share, and shall also be punished by the king.

9.s: sarva eva vikarmasthā nārhanti bhrātaro dhanam na cādattvā kaniṣṭhebhyo jyeṣṭhaḥ kurvīta yautakam
9.d: सर्व एव विकर्मस्था नार्हन्ति भ्रातरो धनम् न चादत्त्वा कनिष्ठेभ्यो ज्येष्ठः कुर्वीत यौतकम्
9.e: All brothers addicted to evil deeds are unworthy of having property; and the elder brother shall not have a separate hoard without making a contribution to his younger brothers.

9.s: bhrātr̥̄ṇāmavibhaktānāṃ yadyutthānaṃ bhavet saha na putrabhāgaṃ viṣamaṃ pitā dadyāt kathaṃ cana
9.d: भ्रात्र्̥̄णामविभक्तानां यद्युत्थानं भवेत् सह न पुत्रभागं विषमं पिता दद्यात् कथं चन
9.e: Among undivided brothers, if there is a joint concern,—the father shall, on no account, make an unequal division among his sons.

9.s: ūrdhvaṃ vibhāgātjātastu pitryameva hareddhanam saṃsṛṣṭāstena vā ye syurvibhajeta sa taiḥ saha
9.d: ऊर्ध्वं विभागात्जातस्तु पित्र्यमेव हरेद्धनम् संसृष्टास्तेन वा ये स्युर्विभजेत स तैः सह
9.e: If a son is born after partition, he shall receive the property of the father alone; or if any other sons be reunited, he would share it with them.

9.s: anapatyasya putrasya mātā dāyamavāpnuyāt mātaryapi ca vṛttāyāṃ piturmātā hareddhanam
9.d: अनपत्यस्य पुत्रस्य माता दायमवाप्नुयात् मातर्यपि च वृत्तायां पितुर्माता हरेद्धनम्
9.e: The property of a childless son shall be inherited by his mother; and if the mother also is dead, his father’s mother shall receive that property.

9.s: ṛṇe dhane ca sarvasmin pravibhakte yathāvidhi paścāddṛśyeta yat kiṃ cit tat sarvaṃ samatāṃ nayet
9.d: ऋणे धने च सर्वस्मिन् प्रविभक्ते यथाविधि पश्चाद्दृश्येत यत् किं चित् तत् सर्वं समतां नयेत्
9.e: After all the assets and liabilities have been duly distributed, if something be discovered afterwards,—all this must be divided equally.

9.s: vastraṃ patramalaṅkāraṃ kṛtānnamudakaṃ striyaḥ yogakṣemaṃ pracāraṃ ca na vibhājyaṃ pracakṣate
9.d: वस्त्रं पत्रमलङ्कारं कृतान्नमुदकं स्त्रियः योगक्षेमं प्रचारं च न विभाज्यं प्रचक्षते
9.e: A cloth, a conveyance, an ornament, cooked food, water, women, what is conducive to welfare and pasture-ground,—these they declare to be impartible.

9.s: ayamukto vibhāgo vaḥ putrāṇāṃ ca kriyāvidhiḥ kramaśaḥ kṣetrajādīnāṃ dyūtadharmaṃ nibodhata
9.d: अयमुक्तो विभागो वः पुत्राणां च क्रियाविधिः क्रमशः क्षेत्रजादीनां द्यूतधर्मं निबोधत
9.e: Thus has been expounded to you Partition, and the appointing of the ‘soil-born’ and other kinds of sons in due order. Now learn the law relating to Gambling.

9.s: dyūtaṃ samāhvayaṃ caiva rājā rāṣṭrātnivārayet rājāntakaraṇāvetau dvau doṣau pṛthivīkṣitām
9.d: द्यूतं समाह्वयं चैव राजा राष्ट्रात्निवारयेत् राजान्तकरणावेतौ द्वौ दोषौ पृथिवीक्षिताम्
9.e: The King shall exclude from his realm Gambling and Betting; these two evils bring about the destruction of the kingdoms of princes.
