9.s: prakāśametat tāskaryaṃ yaddevanasamāhvayau tayornityaṃ pratīghāte nṛpatiryatnavān bhavet
9.d: प्रकाशमेतत् तास्कर्यं यद्देवनसमाह्वयौ तयोर्नित्यं प्रतीघाते नृपतिर्यत्नवान् भवेत्
9.e: Gambling and Betting are open theft; the King shall always be careful in suppressing them.

9.s: aprāṇibhiryat kriyate tatloke dyūtamucyate prāṇibhiḥ kriyate yastu sa vijñeyaḥ samāhvayaḥ
9.d: अप्राणिभिर्यत् क्रियते तत्लोके द्यूतमुच्यते प्राणिभिः क्रियते यस्तु स विज्ञेयः समाह्वयः
9.e: That which is done through inanimate things is called ‘Gambling’; while what is done through animate things is to be known as ‘Betting.’

9.s: dyūtaṃ samāhvayaṃ caiva yaḥ kuryāt kārayeta vā tān sarvān ghātayedrājā śūdrāṃśca dvijaliṅginaḥ
9.d: द्यूतं समाह्वयं चैव यः कुर्यात् कारयेत वा तान् सर्वान् घातयेद्राजा शूद्रांश्च द्विजलिङ्गिनः
9.e: He who either does the gambling or betting himself, or helps others to do them,—all these the King shall strike; as also those Śūdras who assume the guise of twice-born men.

9.s: kitavān kuśīlavān krūrān pāṣaṇḍasthāṃśca mānavān vikarmasthān śauṇḍikāṃśca kṣipraṃ nirvāsayet purāt
9.d: कितवान् कुशीलवान् क्रूरान् पाषण्डस्थांश्च मानवान् विकर्मस्थान् शौण्डिकांश्च क्षिप्रं निर्वासयेत् पुरात्
9.e: Gamblers, dancers, cruel men, men belonging to heretical sects, men addicted to evil deeds, dealers in wine,—these the King shall instantly banish from his town.

9.s: ete rāṣṭre vartamānā rājñaḥ prachannataskarāḥ vikarmakriyayā nityaṃ bādhante bhadrikāḥ prajāḥ
9.d: एते राष्ट्रे वर्तमाना राज्ञः प्रछन्नतस्कराः विकर्मक्रियया नित्यं बाधन्ते भद्रिकाः प्रजाः
9.e: These disguised thieves, living in the King’s realm, constantly harass the well-behaved people by their evil deeds.

9.s: dyūtametat purā kalpe dṛṣṭaṃ vairakaraṃ mahat tasmāddyūtaṃ na seveta hāsyārthamapi buddhimān
9.d: द्यूतमेतत् पुरा कल्पे दृष्टं वैरकरं महत् तस्माद्द्यूतं न सेवेत हास्यार्थमपि बुद्धिमान्
9.e: In former cycles gambling has been seen to be the great source of enmity; the wise man shall therefore not have recourse to gambling, even in joke.

9.s: pracchannaṃ vā prakāśaṃ vā tatniṣeveta yo naraḥ tasya daṇḍavikalpaḥ syādyathaiṣṭaṃ nṛpatestathā
9.d: प्रच्छन्नं वा प्रकाशं वा तत्निषेवेत यो नरः तस्य दण्डविकल्पः स्याद्यथैष्टं नृपतेस्तथा
9.e: If a man has recourse, either openly or secretly, to this (vice), the form of punishment inflicted upon him shall be in accordance with the King’s discretion.

9.s: kṣatraviśśūdrayonistu daṇḍaṃ dātumaśaknuvan ānṛṇyaṃ karmaṇā gacchedvipro dadyātśanaiḥ śanaiḥ
9.d: क्षत्रविश्शूद्रयोनिस्तु दण्डं दातुमशक्नुवन् आनृण्यं कर्मणा गच्छेद्विप्रो दद्यात्शनैः शनैः
9.e: TheKṣatriya, theVaiśyaand theŚūdra, when unable to pay a fine, shall discharge the liability by labour; theBrāhmaṇamay pay it by instalments.

9.s: strībālaunmattavṛddhānāṃ daridrāṇāṃ ca rogiṇām śiphāvidalarajjuādyairvidadhyātnṛpatirdamam
9.d: स्त्रीबालौन्मत्तवृद्धानां दरिद्राणां च रोगिणाम् शिफाविदलरज्जुआद्यैर्विदध्यात्नृपतिर्दमम्
9.e: On women, boys, men out of their minds, the old, the poor and the sick, the king shall inflict punishment with creepers, barks, ropes and so forth.

9.s: ye niyuktāstu kāryeṣu hanyuḥ kāryāṇi kāryiṇām dhanauṣmaṇā pacyamānāstānnissvān kārayennṛpaḥ
9.d: ये नियुक्तास्तु कार्येषु हन्युः कार्याणि कार्यिणाम् धनौष्मणा पच्यमानास्तान्निस्स्वान् कारयेन्नृपः
9.e: If the officers deputed to look after the business of suitors should, fired by the heat of wealth, hamper that business,—these the King shall render penniless.

9.s: kūṭaśāsanakartr̥̄ṃśca prakṛtīnāṃ ca dūṣakān strībālabrāhmaṇaghnāṃśca hanyāddviṣsevinastathā
9.d: कूटशासनकर्त्र्̥̄ंश्च प्रकृतीनां च दूषकान् स्त्रीबालब्राह्मणघ्नांश्च हन्याद्द्विष्सेविनस्तथा

9.s: tīritaṃ cānuśiṣṭaṃ ca yatra kva cana yadbhavet kṛtaṃ taddharmato vidyātna tadbhūyo nivartayet
9.d: तीरितं चानुशिष्टं च यत्र क्व चन यद्भवेत् कृतं तद्धर्मतो विद्यात्न तद्भूयो निवर्तयेत्
9.e: Whatever has been finally settled and whatever punishment has been inflicted,—he shall accept as lawfully done, and shall not annul it

9.s: amātyāḥ prāḍvivāko vā yat kuryuḥ kāryamanyathā tat svayaṃ nṛpatiḥ kuryāt tān sahasraṃ ca daṇḍayet taṃ
9.d: अमात्याः प्राड्विवाको वा यत् कुर्युः कार्यमन्यथा तत् स्वयं नृपतिः कुर्यात् तान् सहस्रं च दण्डयेत् तं
9.e: If the councillors or the judge decide a case unfairly, that case the King himself shall revise and fine them one thousand.

9.s: brahmahā ca surāpaśca steyī ca gurutalpagaḥ taskaro gurutalpagaḥ ete sarve pṛthag jñeyā mahāpātakino narāḥ
9.d: ब्रह्महा च सुरापश्च स्तेयी च गुरुतल्पगः तस्करो गुरुतल्पगः एते सर्वे पृथग् ज्ञेया महापातकिनो नराः
9.e: The slayer of aBrāhmaṇa, the drinker of wine, the thief and the violator of the preceptor’s bed,—all these individually should be known as men who have committed heinous crimes.

9.s: caturṇāmapi caiteṣāṃ prāyaścittamakurvatām śārīraṃ dhanasaṃyuktaṃ daṇḍaṃ dharmyaṃ prakalpayet
9.d: चतुर्णामपि चैतेषां प्रायश्चित्तमकुर्वताम् शारीरं धनसंयुक्तं दण्डं धर्म्यं प्रकल्पयेत्
9.e: Even on all these four, if they do not perform the expiatory penance, the king shall inflict corporal punishment along with fine, in accordance with the law.

9.s: gurutalpe bhagaḥ kāryaḥ surāpāne surādhvajaḥ steye ca śvapadaṃ kāryaṃ brahmahaṇyaśirāḥ pumān taskare śvapadaṃ kāryaṃ
9.d: गुरुतल्पे भगः कार्यः सुरापाने सुराध्वजः स्तेये च श्वपदं कार्यं ब्रह्महण्यशिराः पुमान् तस्करे श्वपदं कार्यं
9.e: For violating the preceptor’s bed the sign of the female organ shall be branded; for drinking wine that of the tavern; for theft that of the dog’s foot; and for killing aBrāhmaṇathat of a headless man.

9.s: asaṃbhojyā hyasaṃyājyā asaṃpāṭhyā 'vivāhinaḥ careyuḥ pṛthivīṃ dīnāḥ sarvadharmabahiṣkṛtāḥ
9.d: असंभोज्या ह्यसंयाज्या असंपाठ्या ऽविवाहिनः चरेयुः पृथिवीं दीनाः सर्वधर्मबहिष्कृताः
9.e: Debarred from entertainments, debarred from sacrifices, debarred from education, excluded from all religious acts, these shall wander over the earth; abject and despised.

9.s: jñātisaṃbandhibhistvete tyaktavyāḥ kṛtalakṣaṇāḥ nirdayā nirṃamaskārāstan manoranuśāsanam
9.d: ज्ञातिसंबन्धिभिस्त्वेते त्यक्तव्याः कृतलक्षणाः निर्दया निर्ंअमस्कारास्तन् मनोरनुशासनम्
9.e: Being branded, these shall be abandoned by Kinsmen and relations, deprived of all sympathy and greetings;—such is the teaching of manu.

9.s: prāyaścittaṃ tu kurvāṇāḥ sarvavarṇā yathoditam pūrve varṇā yathauditam nāṅkyā rājñā lalāṭe syurdāpyāstūttamasāhasam
9.d: प्रायश्चित्तं तु कुर्वाणाः सर्ववर्णा यथोदितम् पूर्वे वर्णा यथौदितम् नाङ्क्या राज्ञा ललाटे स्युर्दाप्यास्तूत्तमसाहसम्
9.e: But men of the senior castes, who perform the expiatory penances, as prescribed, shall not be branded on the forehead by the king; they shall be made to pay the highest amercement.

9.s: āgaḥsu brāhmaṇasyaiva kāryo madhyamasāhasaḥ vivāsyo vā bhavedrāṣṭrāt sadravyaḥ saparicchadaḥ
9.d: आगःसु ब्राह्मणस्यैव कार्यो मध्यमसाहसः विवास्यो वा भवेद्राष्ट्रात् सद्रव्यः सपरिच्छदः
9.e: For offences committed by theBrāhmaṇathe middle-most amercement shall be inflicted on him; or he shall be banished from the kingdom, along with his goods and chattels.

9.s: itare kṛtavantastu pāpānyetānyakāmataḥ sarvasvahāramarhanti kāmatastu pravāsanam
9.d: इतरे कृतवन्तस्तु पापान्येतान्यकामतः सर्वस्वहारमर्हन्ति कामतस्तु प्रवासनम्
9.e: But others who have committed these offences unintentionally, deserve to have the entire property confiscated; and death, in the case of their being intentional.

9.s: nādadīta nṛpaḥ sādhurmahāpātakino dhanam ādadānastu tatlobhāt tena doṣeṇa lipyate
9.d: नाददीत नृपः साधुर्महापातकिनो धनम् आददानस्तु तत्लोभात् तेन दोषेण लिप्यते
9.e: The righteous King shall not appropriate the property of the man guilty of a heinous crime; if, through greed, he takes it, he becomes tainted with that guilt.

9.s: apsu praveśya taṃ daṇḍaṃ varuṇāyaupapādayet śrutavṛttaupapanne vā brāhmaṇe pratipādayet
9.d: अप्सु प्रवेश्य तं दण्डं वरुणायौपपादयेत् श्रुतवृत्तौपपन्ने वा ब्राह्मणे प्रतिपादयेत्
9.e: He shall deposit such property in the water and offer it toVaruṇa, or bestow it on aBrāhmaṇaendowed with learning and character.

9.s: īśo daṇḍasya varuṇo rājñāṃ daṇḍadharo hi saḥ īśaḥ sarvasya jagato brāhmaṇo vedapāragaḥ
9.d: ईशो दण्डस्य वरुणो राज्ञां दण्डधरो हि सः ईशः सर्वस्य जगतो ब्राह्मणो वेदपारगः
9.e: Varuṇai s the lord of punishment, as he holds the sceptre over the King; while theBrāhmaṇa, well versed in the Veda, is the lord of the whole world.

9.s: yatra varjayate rājā pāpakṛdbhyo dhanāgamam tatra kālena jāyante mānavā dīrghajīvinaḥ
9.d: यत्र वर्जयते राजा पापकृद्भ्यो धनागमम् तत्र कालेन जायन्ते मानवा दीर्घजीविनः
9.e: In a country where the King avoids the income of wealth from sinners, men are, in time, born to be long-lived—(246) the crops of husbandmen grow, according as they are sown; children do not die, and no mis-shaped child is born.

9.s: niṣpadyante ca sasyāni yathauptāni viśāṃ pṛthak bālāśca na pramīyante vikṛtaṃ ca na jāyate
9.d: निष्पद्यन्ते च सस्यानि यथौप्तानि विशां पृथक् बालाश्च न प्रमीयन्ते विकृतं च न जायते
9.e: In a country where the King avoids the income of wealth from sinners, men are, in time, born to be long-lived—(246) the crops of husbandmen grow, according as they are sown; children do not die, and no mis-shaped child is born.

9.s: brāhmaṇān bādhamānaṃ tu kāmādavaravarṇajam hanyāccitrairvadhaupāyairudvejanakarairnṛpaḥ
9.d: ब्राह्मणान् बाधमानं तु कामादवरवर्णजम् हन्याच्चित्रैर्वधौपायैरुद्वेजनकरैर्नृपः
9.e: If a low-born person intentionally harasses aBrāhmaṇa, the King shall strike him with various terror-striking forms of corporal punishment.

9.s: yāvānavadhyasya vadhe tāvān vadhyasya mokṣaṇe adharmo nṛpaterdṛṣṭo dharmastu viniyacchataḥ
9.d: यावानवध्यस्य वधे तावान् वध्यस्य मोक्षणे अधर्मो नृपतेर्दृष्टो धर्मस्तु विनियच्छतः
9.e: The sin incurred by the king in striking one who does not deserve it, is the same as that in acquitting one who deserves to be struck; but merit accrues to him if he chastises justly.

9.s: udito 'yaṃ vistaraśo mitho vivādamānayoḥ aṣṭādaśasu mārgeṣu vyavahārasya nirṇayaḥ
9.d: उदितो ऽयं विस्तरशो मिथो विवादमानयोः अष्टादशसु मार्गेषु व्यवहारस्य निर्णयः
9.e: This has been expounded at length-investigation of suits between two litigants, bearing upon the eighteen titles of dispute.

9.s: evaṃ dharmyāṇi kāryāṇi samyak kurvan mahīpatiḥ deśānalabdhānlipseta labdhāṃśca paripālayet
9.d: एवं धर्म्याणि कार्याणि सम्यक् कुर्वन् महीपतिः देशानलब्धान्लिप्सेत लब्धांश्च परिपालयेत्
9.e: The king thus duly doing his lawful work, may seek to acquire tracts of land not already acquired, and settle those already acquired.

9.s: samyakniviṣṭadeśastu kṛtadurgaśca śāstrataḥ kaṇṭakauddharaṇe nityamātiṣṭhedyatnamuttamam
9.d: सम्यक्निविष्टदेशस्तु कृतदुर्गश्च शास्त्रतः कण्टकौद्धरणे नित्यमातिष्ठेद्यत्नमुत्तमम्
9.e: Having duly settled his kingdom, and having built forts according to the institutes, he shall apply his best efforts to the ‘removal of thorns.’

9.s: rakṣanādāryavṛttānāṃ kaṇṭakānāṃ ca śodhanāt narendrāstridivaṃ yānti prajāpālanatatparāḥ
9.d: रक्षनादार्यवृत्तानां कण्टकानां च शोधनात् नरेन्द्रास्त्रिदिवं यान्ति प्रजापालनतत्पराः
9.e: Kings, intent upon protecting the people, go to heaven, by protecting the Well-behaved and by removing the ‘thorns’

9.s: aśāsaṃstaskarān yastu baliṃ gṛhṇāti pārthivaḥ tasya prakṣubhyate rāṣṭraṃ svargācca parihīyate
9.d: अशासंस्तस्करान् यस्तु बलिं गृह्णाति पार्थिवः तस्य प्रक्षुभ्यते राष्ट्रं स्वर्गाच्च परिहीयते
9.e: If a king does not repress thieves and yet receives his taxes, his kingdom becomes perturbed and he falls off from heaven.

9.s: nirbhayaṃ tu bhavedyasya rāṣṭraṃ bāhubalāśritam tasya tadvardhate nityaṃ sicyamāna iva drumaḥ
9.d: निर्भयं तु भवेद्यस्य राष्ट्रं बाहुबलाश्रितम् तस्य तद्वर्धते नित्यं सिच्यमान इव द्रुमः
9.e: If however his kingdom, resting on the strength of his arms, is secure from danger,—it flourishes constantly, like a well-watered tree.

9.s: dvividhāṃstaskarān vidyāt paradravyāpahārakān prakāśāṃścāprakāśāṃśca cāracakṣurmahīpatiḥ
9.d: द्विविधांस्तस्करान् विद्यात् परद्रव्यापहारकान् प्रकाशांश्चाप्रकाशांश्च चारचक्षुर्महीपतिः
9.e: The spy-eyed king shall discover the two kinds of thieves who take away the property of other men, those that are ‘open’ and those ‘concealed’

9.s: prakāśavañcakāsteṣāṃ nānāpaṇyaupajīvinaḥ pracchannavañcakāstvete ye stenāṭavikādayaḥ
9.d: प्रकाशवञ्चकास्तेषां नानापण्यौपजीविनः प्रच्छन्नवञ्चकास्त्वेते ये स्तेनाटविकादयः
9.e: Of these, the ‘open’ cheats are those who make a living by dealing in various commodities, and the ‘concealed’ cheats are burglars, robbers in forests and so forth.

9.s: utkocakāścaupadhikā vañcakāḥ kitavāstathā maṅgalādeśavṛttāśca bhadrāścaikṣaṇikaiḥ saha bhadraprekṣaṇikaiḥ saha
9.d: उत्कोचकाश्चौपधिका वञ्चकाः कितवास्तथा मङ्गलादेशवृत्ताश्च भद्राश्चैक्षणिकैः सह भद्रप्रेक्षणिकैः सह
9.e: Those who take bribes, dissemblers, cheats and gamblers, fortune-tellers and palmists.

9.s: asamyakkāriṇaścaiva mahāmātrāścikitsakāḥ śilpaupacārayuktāśca nipuṇāḥ paṇyayoṣitaḥ
9.d: असम्यक्कारिणश्चैव महामात्राश्चिकित्सकाः शिल्पौपचारयुक्ताश्च निपुणाः पण्ययोषितः
9.e: Misbehaving High officials and physicians, art-exhibitors, and clever harlots.

9.s: evamādīn vijānīyāt prakāśāṃllokakaṇṭakān evamādyān nigūḍhacāriṇaścānyānanāryānāryaliṅginaḥ
9.d: एवमादीन् विजानीयात् प्रकाशांल्लोककण्टकान् एवमाद्यान् निगूढचारिणश्चान्याननार्यानार्यलिङ्गिनः
9.e: These and others of the same kind one should know as the open ‘thorns’ of the people; and others, who are rogues in the guise of gentlemen, as ‘dissemblers.’

9.s: tān viditvā sucaritairgūḍhaistatkarmakāribhiḥ cāraiścānekasaṃsthānaiḥ protsādya vaśamānayet
9.d: तान् विदित्वा सुचरितैर्गूढैस्तत्कर्मकारिभिः चारैश्चानेकसंस्थानैः प्रोत्साद्य वशमानयेत्
9.e: Having discovered them through well-behaved and disguised men following the same occupations, as also through spies variously disguised, he shall exterminate them and bring them under his control.

9.s: teṣāṃ doṣānabhikhyāpya sve sve karmaṇi tattvataḥ kurvīta śāsanaṃ rājā samyak sārāparādhataḥ
9.d: तेषां दोषानभिख्याप्य स्वे स्वे कर्मणि तत्त्वतः कुर्वीत शासनं राजा सम्यक् सारापराधतः
9.e: Having truly proclaimed their crimes in connection with their respective acts, the king shall duly inflict punishment on them, in accordance with their crimes and capacities.

9.s: na hi daṇḍādṛte śakyaḥ kartuṃ pāpavinigrahaḥ stenānāṃ pāpabuddhīnāṃ nibhṛtaṃ caratāṃ kṣitau
9.d: न हि दण्डादृते शक्यः कर्तुं पापविनिग्रहः स्तेनानां पापबुद्धीनां निभृतं चरतां क्षितौ
9.e: The crimes of evil-minded thieves secretly prowling over the earth cannot be suppressed without punishment.

9.s: sabhāprapā 'pūpaśālāveśamadyānnavikrayāḥ catuṣpathāṃścaityavṛkṣāḥ samājāḥ prekṣaṇāni ca
9.d: सभाप्रपा ऽपूपशालावेशमद्यान्नविक्रयाः चतुष्पथांश्चैत्यवृक्षाः समाजाः प्रेक्षणानि च
9.e: Old gardens, forests, shops of artisans, uninhabited houses, groves and gardens;—(265)—these and similar places the king shall cause to be guarded by companies of soldiers, stationary as well as patrolling, and also by spies,—in order to keep away thieves.

9.s: jīrṇaudyānānyaraṇyāni kārukāveśanāni ca śūnyāni cāpyagārāṇi vanānyupavanāni ca
9.d: जीर्णौद्यानान्यरण्यानि कारुकावेशनानि च शून्यानि चाप्यगाराणि वनान्युपवनानि च
9.e: Old gardens, forests, shops of artisans, uninhabited houses, groves and gardens;—(265)—these and similar places the king shall cause to be guarded by companies of soldiers, stationary as well as patrolling, and also by spies,—in order to keep away thieves.

9.s: evaṃvidhānnṛpo deśān gulmaiḥ sthāvarajaṅgamaiḥ taskarapratiṣedhārthaṃ cāraiścāpyanucārayet
9.d: एवंविधान्नृपो देशान् गुल्मैः स्थावरजङ्गमैः तस्करप्रतिषेधार्थं चारैश्चाप्यनुचारयेत्
9.e: Old gardens, forests, shops of artisans, uninhabited houses, groves and gardens;—(265)—these and similar places the king shall cause to be guarded by companies of soldiers, stationary as well as patrolling, and also by spies,—in order to keep away thieves.

9.s: tatsahāyairanugatairnānākarmapravedibhiḥ vidyādutsādayeccaiva nipuṇaiḥ pūrvataskaraiḥ
9.d: तत्सहायैरनुगतैर्नानाकर्मप्रवेदिभिः विद्यादुत्सादयेच्चैव निपुणैः पूर्वतस्करैः
9.e: He shall detect and exterminate them by means of clever reformed thieves, who associate with them, follow them and become apprised of their machinations.

9.s: bhakṣyabhojyaupadeśaiśca brāhmaṇānāṃ ca darśanaiḥ śauryakarmāpadeśaiśca kuryusteṣāṃ samāgamam
9.d: भक्ष्यभोज्यौपदेशैश्च ब्राह्मणानां च दर्शनैः शौर्यकर्मापदेशैश्च कुर्युस्तेषां समागमम्
9.e: They shall bring them together by means of offers of food and drink, by introducing toBrāhmaṇas, and by exhibition of martial feats.

9.s: ye tatra naupasarpeyurmūlapraṇihitāśca ye tān prasahya nṛpo hanyāt samitrajñātibāndhavān
9.d: ये तत्र नौपसर्पेयुर्मूलप्रणिहिताश्च ये तान् प्रसह्य नृपो हन्यात् समित्रज्ञातिबान्धवान्
9.e: Those among them who do not come, and those who are careful in their dealings with the older men,—these the king shall attack by force and destroy, along with their friends, kinsmen and relations.

9.s: na hauḍhena vinā cauraṃ ghātayeddhārmiko nṛpaḥ sahauḍhaṃ saupakaraṇaṃ ghātayedavicārayan
9.d: न हौढेन विना चौरं घातयेद्धार्मिको नृपः सहौढं सौपकरणं घातयेदविचारयन्
9.e: The righteous king shall not put a thief to death unless caught with the stolen goods; when however one is caught with the stolen goods, and the implements of burglary, he may, without hesitation, put him to death.

9.s: grāmeṣvapi ca ye ke ciccaurāṇāṃ bhaktadāyakāḥ bhāṇḍāvakāśadāścaiva sarvāṃstānapi ghātayet
9.d: ग्रामेष्वपि च ये के चिच्चौराणां भक्तदायकाः भाण्डावकाशदाश्चैव सर्वांस्तानपि घातयेत्
9.e: He shall also strike all those in a village who supply food for thieves or provide room for the goods.

9.s: rāṣṭreṣu rakṣādhikṛtān sāmantāṃścaiva coditān abhyāghāteṣu madhyasthāñ śiṣyāccaurāniva drutam
9.d: राष्ट्रेषु रक्षाधिकृतान् सामन्तांश्चैव चोदितान् अभ्याघातेषु मध्यस्थाञ् शिष्याच्चौरानिव द्रुतम्
9.e: If those persons who are entrusted with the work of guarding the realm, and those vassals who have been ordered to assist, should remain neutral during the raids (against thieves), the king shall punish them speedily, like thieves.

9.s: yaścāpi dharmasamayāt pracyuto dharmajīvanaḥ daṇḍenaiva tamapyoṣet svakāddharmāddhi vicyutam
9.d: यश्चापि धर्मसमयात् प्रच्युतो धर्मजीवनः दण्डेनैव तमप्योषेत् स्वकाद्धर्माद्धि विच्युतम्
9.e: If one who subsists on religion deviates from religious ordinances, he shall punish him severely by a fine,—fallen as he is from his duty.

9.s: grāmaghāte hitābhaṅge pathi moṣābhidarśane śaktito nābhidhāvanto nirvāsyāḥ saparicchadāḥ
9.d: ग्रामघाते हिताभङ्गे पथि मोषाभिदर्शने शक्तितो नाभिधावन्तो निर्वास्याः सपरिच्छदाः
9.e: If people do not hasten to assist, to the best of their power, whenever a village is attacked, or a dyke is breaking, or a highway robbery is being committed,—they should be banished along with their chattels.

9.s: rājñaḥ kośāpahartr̥̄ṃśca pratikūleṣu ca sthitān prātikūlyeṣvavasthitān ghātayedvividhairdaṇḍairarīṇāṃ caupajāpakān
9.d: राज्ञः कोशापहर्त्र्̥̄ंश्च प्रतिकूलेषु च स्थितान् प्रातिकूल्येष्ववस्थितान् घातयेद्विविधैर्दण्डैररीणां चौपजापकान्
9.e: Those who rob the king’s treasuries and those who are disaffected towards him, as also those who conspire with his enemies,—the king shall strike with various forms of punishment.

9.s: saṃdhiṃ chittvā tu ye cauryaṃ rātrau kurvanti taskarāḥ saṃdhiṃ bhittvā teṣāṃ chittvā nṛpo hastau tīkṣṇe śūle niveśayet
9.d: संधिं छित्त्वा तु ये चौर्यं रात्रौ कुर्वन्ति तस्कराः संधिं भित्त्वा तेषां छित्त्वा नृपो हस्तौ तीक्ष्णे शूले निवेशयेत्
9.e: If thieves commit thefts at night, after breaking into a house, the king shall cut off their hands and have them impaled on a pointed stake;—(276) on the first conviction he should have two fingers of the cut-purse amputated; on the second a hand and a foot; and on the third he should be put to death.

9.s: aṅgulīrgranthibhedasya chedayet prathame grahe dvitīye hastacaraṇau tṛtīye vadhamarhati
9.d: अङ्गुलीर्ग्रन्थिभेदस्य छेदयेत् प्रथमे ग्रहे द्वितीये हस्तचरणौ तृतीये वधमर्हति
9.e: If thieves commit thefts at night, after breaking into a house, the king shall cut off their hands and have them impaled on a pointed stake;—(276) on the first conviction he should have two fingers of the cut-purse amputated; on the second a hand and a foot; and on the third he should be put to death.

9.s: agnidān bhaktadāṃścaiva tathā śastrāvakāśadān saṃnidhātr̥̄ṃśca moṣasya hanyāccauramivaiśvaraḥ
9.d: अग्निदान् भक्तदांश्चैव तथा शस्त्रावकाशदान् संनिधात्र्̥̄ंश्च मोषस्य हन्याच्चौरमिवैश्वरः
9.e: The king shall strike like thieves those who provide fire, offer food and supply arms and lodging, as also those who abet their escape.

9.s: taḍāgabhedakaṃ hanyādapsu śuddhavadhena vā yadvā 'pi pratisaṃskuryāddāpyastūttamasāhasam
9.d: तडागभेदकं हन्यादप्सु शुद्धवधेन वा यद्वा ऽपि प्रतिसंस्कुर्याद्दाप्यस्तूत्तमसाहसम्
9.e: If a man breaks open a tank, he shall be slain in the water, or by simple form of death; or, he may repair the damage and be made to fay the highest amercement.

9.s: koṣṭhāgārāyudhāgāradevatāgārabhedakān hastiaśvarathahartr̥̄ṃśca hanyādevāvicārayan
9.d: कोष्ठागारायुधागारदेवतागारभेदकान् हस्तिअश्वरथहर्त्र्̥̄ंश्च हन्यादेवाविचारयन्
9.e: Those who break into a storehouse, an armoury, or a temple, and those who steal elephants, horses and chariots,—he shall put to death without hesitation.

9.s: yastu pūrvaniviṣṭasya taḍāgasyaudakaṃ haret āgamaṃ vā 'pyapāṃ bhindyāt sa dāpyaḥ pūrvasāhasam
9.d: यस्तु पूर्वनिविष्टस्य तडागस्यौदकं हरेत् आगमं वा ऽप्यपां भिन्द्यात् स दाप्यः पूर्वसाहसम्
9.e: If a man take away the water of a tank dug in ancient times, or cut off the supply of water,—he shall be made to pay the lowest amercement.

9.s: samutsṛjedrājamārge yastvamedhyamanāpadi sa dvau kārṣāpaṇau dadyādamedhyaṃ cāśu śodhayet
9.d: समुत्सृजेद्राजमार्गे यस्त्वमेध्यमनापदि स द्वौ कार्षापणौ दद्यादमेध्यं चाशु शोधयेत्
9.e: If one throws filth upon the public road, except in dire necessity,—he shall pay twoKārṣāpaṇasand clean the filth immediately.

9.s: āpadgato 'tha vā vṛddhā garbhiṇī bāla eva vā paribhāṣaṇamarhanti tacca śodhyamiti sthitiḥ
9.d: आपद्गतो ऽथ वा वृद्धा गर्भिणी बाल एव वा परिभाषणमर्हन्ति तच्च शोध्यमिति स्थितिः
9.e: But a person in urgent necessity, an aged person, a pregnant woman, or a child should be reprimanded and the filth should be cleaned;—such is the law.

9.s: cikitsakānāṃ sarveṣāṃ mithyāpracaratāṃ damaḥ amānuṣeṣu prathamo mānuṣeṣu tu madhyamaḥ
9.d: चिकित्सकानां सर्वेषां मिथ्याप्रचरतां दमः अमानुषेषु प्रथमो मानुषेषु तु मध्यमः
9.e: All physicians dealing dishonestly are liable to punishment; in the case of patients other than human, the lowest, and in that of human patients, the middlemost amercement.

9.s: saṅkramadhvajayaṣṭīnāṃ pratimānāṃ ca bhedakaḥ pratikuryācca tat sarvaṃ pañca dadyātśatāni ca
9.d: सङ्क्रमध्वजयष्टीनां प्रतिमानां च भेदकः प्रतिकुर्याच्च तत् सर्वं पञ्च दद्यात्शतानि च
9.e: He who destroys a crossing, a flag, a pole or images, shall repair the whole of it and shall pay five hundred.

9.s: adūṣitānāṃ dravyāṇāṃ dūṣaṇe bhedane tathā maṇīnāmapavedhe ca daṇḍaḥ prathamasāhasaḥ
9.d: अदूषितानां द्रव्याणां दूषणे भेदने तथा मणीनामपवेधे च दण्डः प्रथमसाहसः
9.e: For adulterating unadulterated commodities, and for breaking or wrongly boring gems, the punishment shall be the first amercement.

9.s: samairhi viṣamaṃ yastu caredvai mūlyato 'pi vā samāpnuyāddamaṃ pūrvaṃ naro madhyamameva vā
9.d: समैर्हि विषमं यस्तु चरेद्वै मूल्यतो ऽपि वा समाप्नुयाद्दमं पूर्वं नरो मध्यममेव वा
9.e: The man who treats equals as unequals in value should receive the punishment of the first or the middlemost amercement.

9.s: bandhanāni ca sarvāṇi rājā mārge niveśayet rājamārge duḥkhitā yatra dṛśyeran vikṛtāḥ pāpakāriṇaḥ
9.d: बन्धनानि च सर्वाणि राजा मार्गे निवेशयेत् राजमार्गे दुःखिता यत्र दृश्येरन् विकृताः पापकारिणः
9.e: The king shall establish prisons all along the public road,—where the suffering and disfigured offenders might be seen.

9.s: prākārasya ca bhettāraṃ parikhāṇāṃ ca pūrakam dvārāṇāṃ caiva bhaṅktāraṃ kṣiprameva pravāsayet
9.d: प्राकारस्य च भेत्तारं परिखाणां च पूरकम् द्वाराणां चैव भङ्क्तारं क्षिप्रमेव प्रवासयेत्
9.e: Him in who breaks the wall, or fills up the ditch, or breaks the gate—he shall instantly banish.

9.s: abhicāreṣu sarveṣu kartavyo dviśato damaḥ mūlakarmaṇi cānāpteḥ kṛtyāsu vividhāsu ca cānāptaiḥ
9.d: अभिचारेषु सर्वेषु कर्तव्यो द्विशतो दमः मूलकर्मणि चानाप्तेः कृत्यासु विविधासु च चानाप्तैः
9.e: In all cases of malevolent rites, the fine shall be two hundred; as also in a case of magic spell by persons not related, or in those of various kinds of sorcery.

9.s: abījavikrayī caiva bījautkṛṣṭā tathaiva ca maryādābhedakaścaiva vikṛtaṃ prāpnuyādvadham
9.d: अबीजविक्रयी चैव बीजौत्कृष्टा तथैव च मर्यादाभेदकश्चैव विकृतं प्राप्नुयाद्वधम्
9.e: He who sells what is not-seed, or picks out the seed, or transgresses the bounds (of propriety) shall suffer ‘mutilation’ as the penalty.

9.s: sarvakaṇṭakapāpiṣṭhaṃ hemakāraṃ tu pārthivaḥ pravartamānamanyāye chedayetlavaśaḥ kṣuraiḥ chedayet khaṇḍaśaḥ kṣuraiḥ
9.d: सर्वकण्टकपापिष्ठं हेमकारं तु पार्थिवः प्रवर्तमानमन्याये छेदयेत्लवशः क्षुरैः छेदयेत् खण्डशः क्षुरैः
9.e: If the goldsmith, the worst of all ‘thorns,’ behaves dishonestly, the king shall have him cut to pieces with razors.

9.s: sītādravyāpaharaṇe śastrāṇāmauṣadhasya ca kālamāsādya kāryaṃ ca rājā daṇḍaṃ prakalpayet
9.d: सीताद्रव्यापहरणे शस्त्राणामौषधस्य च कालमासाद्य कार्यं च राजा दण्डं प्रकल्पयेत्
9.e: For the stealing of agricultural implements, of arms or of medicines, the king shall determine the punishment, after taking into consideration the time and uses.

9.s: svāmy 'mātyau puraṃ rāṣṭraṃ kośadaṇḍau suhṛt tathā sapta prakṛtayo hyetāḥ saptāṅgaṃ rājyamucyate
9.d: स्वाम्य् ऽमात्यौ पुरं राष्ट्रं कोशदण्डौ सुहृत् तथा सप्त प्रकृतयो ह्येताः सप्ताङ्गं राज्यमुच्यते
9.e: The master and the minister, the capital city, the people, the treasury and the army, and the ally,—these are the seven constituents; and the kingdom is described as having ‘seven limbs.’

9.s: saptānāṃ prakṛtīnāṃ tu rājyasyāsāṃ yathākramam pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ gurutaraṃ jānīyādvyasanaṃ mahat
9.d: सप्तानां प्रकृतीनां तु राज्यस्यासां यथाक्रमम् पूर्वं पूर्वं गुरुतरं जानीयाद्व्यसनं महत्
9.e: Among these seven constituents of the kingdom stated in due order, injury to each preceding one is to be regarded as more serious.

9.s: saptāṅgasyaiha rājyasya viṣṭabdhasya tridaṇḍavat anyonyaguṇavaiśeṣyātna kiṃ cidatiricyate
9.d: सप्ताङ्गस्यैह राज्यस्य विष्टब्धस्य त्रिदण्डवत् अन्योन्यगुणवैशेष्यात्न किं चिदतिरिच्यते
9.e: Yet in the kingdom consisting of the ‘seven limbs’ interlaced like the ‘triple staff,’—since their qualities are mutually helpful,—no one of them is superior.

9.s: teṣu teṣu tu kṛtyeṣu tat tadaṅgaṃ viśiṣyate yena yat sādhyate kāryaṃ tat tasmiṃśreṣṭhamucyate
9.d: तेषु तेषु तु कृत्येषु तत् तदङ्गं विशिष्यते येन यत् साध्यते कार्यं तत् तस्मिंश्रेष्ठमुच्यते
9.e: Each ‘limb’ is particularly qualified for the fulfilment of a distinct purpose; and hence each is declared to be the most important in reference to that purpose which is fulfilled by its means.

9.s: cāreṇautsāhayogena kriyayaiva ca karmaṇām svaśaktiṃ paraśaktiṃ ca nityaṃ vidyātmahīpatiḥ vidyāt parātmanoḥ
9.d: चारेणौत्साहयोगेन क्रिययैव च कर्मणाम् स्वशक्तिं परशक्तिं च नित्यं विद्यात्महीपतिः विद्यात् परात्मनोः
9.e: The king shall constantly ascertain his own and his enemy’s strength through spies, through display of energy and also through the actual carrying out of undertakings.

9.s: pīḍanāni ca sarvāṇi vyasanāni tathaiva ca ārabheta tataḥ kāryaṃ sañcintya gurulāghavam
9.d: पीडनानि च सर्वाणि व्यसनानि तथैव च आरभेत ततः कार्यं सञ्चिन्त्य गुरुलाघवम्
9.e: The king shall begin operations after having taken into consideration all calamities and vices, and their relative importance.

9.s: ārabhetaiva karmāṇi śrāntaḥ śrāntaḥ punaḥ punaḥ karmāṇyārabhamāṇaṃ hi puruṣaṃ śrīrniṣevate
9.d: आरभेतैव कर्माणि श्रान्तः श्रान्तः पुनः पुनः कर्माण्यारभमाणं हि पुरुषं श्रीर्निषेवते
9.e: Tired and tired, over again he should begin his operations; for fortune favours the man who undertakes operations.

9.s: kṛtaṃ tretāyugaṃ caiva dvāparaṃ kalireva ca rājño vṛttāni sarvāṇi rājā hi yugamucyate
9.d: कृतं त्रेतायुगं चैव द्वापरं कलिरेव च राज्ञो वृत्तानि सर्वाणि राजा हि युगमुच्यते
9.e: The actions of the king constitute the ‘Kṛta’, the ‘Tretā’, the ‘Dvāpara’ and the ‘Kali’ cycles; as it is the king that is called the ‘cycle.’

9.s: kaliḥ prasupto bhavati sa jāgraddvāparaṃ yugam karmasvabhyudyatastretā vicaraṃstu kṛtaṃ yugam
9.d: कलिः प्रसुप्तो भवति स जाग्रद्द्वापरं युगम् कर्मस्वभ्युद्यतस्त्रेता विचरंस्तु कृतं युगम्
9.e: Asleep, he represents ‘Kali;’ awake, the ‘Dvāpara’ cycle; ready to act, the ‘Tretā’; and actually acting, the ‘Kṛta’ cycle.

9.s: indrasyārkasya vāyośca yamasya varuṇasya ca candrasyāgneḥ pṛthivyāśca tejovṛttaṃ nṛpaścaret
9.d: इन्द्रस्यार्कस्य वायोश्च यमस्य वरुणस्य च चन्द्रस्याग्नेः पृथिव्याश्च तेजोवृत्तं नृपश्चरेत्
9.e: The king shall emulate the energetic activity ofIndra, ofArka, ofVāyu, ofYama, ofVaruṇa, ofChandra, ofAgniand ofPṛthvī.

9.s: vārṣikāṃścaturo māsān yathaindro 'bhipravarṣati tathā 'bhivarṣet svaṃ rāṣṭraṃ kāmairindravrataṃ caran
9.d: वार्षिकांश्चतुरो मासान् यथैन्द्रो ऽभिप्रवर्षति तथा ऽभिवर्षेत् स्वं राष्ट्रं कामैरिन्द्रव्रतं चरन्
9.e: As Indra showers rain during four months of the year, so shall the king, acting like Indra, shower benefits on his people.

9.s: aṣṭau māsān yathā 'dityastoyaṃ harati raśmibhiḥ tathā haret karaṃ rāṣṭrātnityamarkavrataṃ hi tat
9.d: अष्टौ मासान् यथा ऽदित्यस्तोयं हरति रश्मिभिः तथा हरेत् करं राष्ट्रात्नित्यमर्कव्रतं हि तत्
9.e: Just as during eight months,Ādityadraws up water with his rays, even so the king shall draw taxes from the people,—this being the function of arka.

9.s: praviśya sarvabhūtāni yathā carati mārutaḥ tathā cāraiḥ praveṣṭavyaṃ vratametaddhi mārutam
9.d: प्रविश्य सर्वभूतानि यथा चरति मारुतः तथा चारैः प्रवेष्टव्यं व्रतमेतद्धि मारुतम्
9.e: As Yama, at the approach of the proper time, restrains both friends and enemies, even so shall all men be restrained by the king; this is the function of Yama.

9.s: yathā yamaḥ priyadveṣyau prāpte kāle niyacchati tathā rājñā niyantavyāḥ prajāstaddhi yamavratam
9.d: यथा यमः प्रियद्वेष्यौ प्राप्ते काले नियच्छति तथा राज्ञा नियन्तव्याः प्रजास्तद्धि यमव्रतम्
9.e: As Yama, at the approach of the proper time, restrains both friends and enemies, even so shall all men be restrained by the king; this is the function of Yama.

9.s: varuṇena yathā pāśairbaddha evābhidṛśyate tathā pāpānnigṛhṇīyādvratametaddhi vāruṇam
9.d: वरुणेन यथा पाशैर्बद्ध एवाभिदृश्यते तथा पापान्निगृह्णीयाद्व्रतमेतद्धि वारुणम्
9.e: As one is always found bound up with ropes byVaruṇa, even so shall the king punish the wicked; this is the function ofVaruṇa.

9.s: paripūrṇaṃ yathā candraṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛṣyanti mānavāḥ tathā prakṛtayo yasmin sa cāndravratiko nṛpaḥ
9.d: परिपूर्णं यथा चन्द्रं दृष्ट्वा हृष्यन्ति मानवाः तथा प्रकृतयो यस्मिन् स चान्द्रव्रतिको नृपः
9.e: The people rejoice at seeing the full moon; the king at whose appearance the people rejoice in that manner is a king who fulfills the functions of the moon.

9.s: pratāpayuktastejasvī nityaṃ syāt pāpakarmasu duṣṭasāmantahiṃsraśca tadāgneyaṃ vrataṃ smṛtam
9.d: प्रतापयुक्तस्तेजस्वी नित्यं स्यात् पापकर्मसु दुष्टसामन्तहिंस्रश्च तदाग्नेयं व्रतं स्मृतम्
9.e: He shall always be endowed with brilliant energy and ardent in his wrath against offenders; he shall exterminate his disaffected vassals; this is the function of agni.

9.s: yathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni dharā dhārayate samam tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni bibhrataḥ pārthivaṃ vratam
9.d: यथा सर्वाणि भूतानि धरा धारयते समम् तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि बिभ्रतः पार्थिवं व्रतम्
9.e: As the earth sustains all beings equally, so does the king support all beings; and this is the function ofPṛthivī.

9.s: etairupāyairanyaiśca yukto nityamatandritaḥ stenān rājā nigṛhṇīyāt svarāṣṭre para eva ca
9.d: एतैरुपायैरन्यैश्च युक्तो नित्यमतन्द्रितः स्तेनान् राजा निगृह्णीयात् स्वराष्ट्रे पर एव च
9.e: Betaking himself to these and other methods, the king, ever alert, shall restrain thieves in his own realm as well as in that of others.

9.s: parāmapyāpadaṃ prāpto brāhmaṇānna prakopayet te hyenaṃ kupitā hanyuḥ sadyaḥ sabalavāhanam
9.d: परामप्यापदं प्राप्तो ब्राह्मणान्न प्रकोपयेत् ते ह्येनं कुपिता हन्युः सद्यः सबलवाहनम्
9.e: Even when fallen in the deepest distress, the king shall not provoke theBrāhmaṇas; for if provoked, they would ruin him, along with his army and conveyances.

9.s: yaiḥ kṛtaḥ sarvabhakṣyo 'gnirapeyaśca mahodadhiḥ sarvabhakṣo kṣayī cāpyāyitaḥ somaḥ ko na naśyet prakopya tān
9.d: यैः कृतः सर्वभक्ष्यो ऽग्निरपेयश्च महोदधिः सर्वभक्षो क्षयी चाप्यायितः सोमः को न नश्येत् प्रकोप्य तान्
9.e: Who could escape ruin after having provoked those by whom fire was rendered all-devouring, by whom the ocean was made undrinkable and by whom the moon was made to wax and wane?

9.s: lokānanyān sṛjeyurye lokapālāṃśca kopitāḥ devān kuryuradevāṃśca kaḥ kṣiṇvaṃstān samṛdhnuyāt
9.d: लोकानन्यान् सृजेयुर्ये लोकपालांश्च कोपिताः देवान् कुर्युरदेवांश्च कः क्षिण्वंस्तान् समृध्नुयात्
9.e: Who could prosper after injuring those who, on being provoked, would create other worlds and other guardians of the regions, and who would make the Gods cease to be Gods?

9.s: yānupāśritya tiṣṭhanti lokā devāśca sarvadā brahma caiva dhanaṃ yeṣāṃ ko hiṃsyāt tāñjijīviṣuḥ
9.d: यानुपाश्रित्य तिष्ठन्ति लोका देवाश्च सर्वदा ब्रह्म चैव धनं येषां को हिंस्यात् ताञ्जिजीविषुः
9.e: What man, desirous of living, would injure them, depending on whom the world and the gods exist, and whose wealth consists of the Veda?

9.s: avidvāṃścaiva vidvāṃśca brāhmaṇo daivataṃ mahat praṇītaścāpraṇītaśca yathā 'gnirdaivataṃ mahat
9.d: अविद्वांश्चैव विद्वांश्च ब्राह्मणो दैवतं महत् प्रणीतश्चाप्रणीतश्च यथा ऽग्निर्दैवतं महत्
9.e: Learned or unlearned, theBrāhmaṇais a great divinity; just as consecrated or unconsecrated, the fire is a great divinity.

9.s: śmaśāneṣvapi tejasvī pāvako naiva duṣyati hūyamānaśca yajñeṣu bhūya evābhivardhate
9.d: श्मशानेष्वपि तेजस्वी पावको नैव दुष्यति हूयमानश्च यज्ञेषु भूय एवाभिवर्धते
9.e: Even though in the cremation-ground, the brilliant fire is not defiled, and it flourishes again when libations are poured unto it at sacrifices.

9.s: evaṃ yadyapyaniṣṭeṣu vartante sarvakarmasu sarvathā brāhmaṇāḥ pūjyāḥ paramaṃ daivataṃ hi tat
9.d: एवं यद्यप्यनिष्टेषु वर्तन्ते सर्वकर्मसु सर्वथा ब्राह्मणाः पूज्याः परमं दैवतं हि तत्
9.e: Even though in the cremation-ground, the brilliant fire is not defiled, and it flourishes again when libations are poured unto it at sacrifices.

9.s: kṣatrasyātipravṛddhasya brāhmaṇān prati sarvaśaḥ brahmaiva saṃniyantṛ syāt kṣatraṃ hi brahmasaṃbhavam
9.d: क्षत्रस्यातिप्रवृद्धस्य ब्राह्मणान् प्रति सर्वशः ब्रह्मैव संनियन्तृ स्यात् क्षत्रं हि ब्रह्मसंभवम्
9.e: When theKṣatriyashall become too over-bearing in every way towardsBrāhmaṇas, theBrāhmaṇahimself shall be their restraining influence; as theKṣatriyahas his source in theBrāhmaṇa.—320

9.s: adbhyo 'gnirbrahmataḥ kṣatramaśmano lohamutthitam teṣāṃ sarvatragaṃ tejaḥ svāsu yoniṣu śāmyati
9.d: अद्भ्यो ऽग्निर्ब्रह्मतः क्षत्रमश्मनो लोहमुत्थितम् तेषां सर्वत्रगं तेजः स्वासु योनिषु शाम्यति
9.e: Fire sprang from water, theKṣatriyafrom theBrāhmaṇa, and iron from stone; the all-penetrating force of each of these becomes extinguished in its source.

9.s: nābrahma kṣatraṃ ṛdhnoti nākṣatraṃ brahma vardhate brahma kṣatraṃ ca saṃpṛktamiha cāmutra vardhate
9.d: नाब्रह्म क्षत्रं ऋध्नोति नाक्षत्रं ब्रह्म वर्धते ब्रह्म क्षत्रं च संपृक्तमिह चामुत्र वर्धते
9.e: TheKṣatriyaflourishes not without theBrāhmaṇa; theBrāhmaṇaprospers not without theKṣatriya; theBrāhmaṇaand theKṣatriya, when united, prosper here as also in the other world.

9.s: dattvā dhanaṃ tu viprebhyaḥ sarvadaṇḍasamutthitam putre rājyaṃ samāsṛjya kurvīta prāyaṇaṃ raṇe samāsādya
9.d: दत्त्वा धनं तु विप्रेभ्यः सर्वदण्डसमुत्थितम् पुत्रे राज्यं समासृज्य कुर्वीत प्रायणं रणे समासाद्य
9.e: Bestowing his wealth, obtained from all kinds of fines, uponBrāhmaṇas, and making over the kingdom to his son, the king shall bring about his departure in battle.

9.s: evaṃ caran sadā yukto rājadharmeṣu pārthivaḥ hiteṣu caiva lokasya sarvān bhṛtyānniyojayet iteṣu caiva lokebhyaḥ
9.d: एवं चरन् सदा युक्तो राजधर्मेषु पार्थिवः हितेषु चैव लोकस्य सर्वान् भृत्यान्नियोजयेत् इतेषु चैव लोकेभ्यः
9.e: Acting in this manner, and ever intent upon his Kingly Duties, the king shall order all his servants to work for the good of the people.

9.s: eṣo 'khilaḥ karmavidhirukto rājñaḥ sanātanaḥ imaṃ karmavidhiṃ vidyāt kramaśo vaiśyaśūdrayoḥ
9.d: एषो ऽखिलः कर्मविधिरुक्तो राज्ञः सनातनः इमं कर्मविधिं विद्यात् क्रमशो वैश्यशूद्रयोः
9.e: Thus has been expounded the whole of the eternal Law relating to the Duties of the King; the law relating to theVaiśyaand theŚūdrarespectively should be understood to be as follows.

9.s: vaiśyastu kṛtasaṃskāraḥ kṛtvā dāraparigraham vārtāyāṃ nityayuktaḥ syāt paśūnāṃ caiva rakṣaṇe
9.d: वैश्यस्तु कृतसंस्कारः कृत्वा दारपरिग्रहम् वार्तायां नित्ययुक्तः स्यात् पशूनां चैव रक्षणे
9.e: After having his sacraments performed, the Vaiśya shall take a wife and apply himself entirely to agriculture and the tending of catlle.

9.s: prajāpatirhi vaiśyāya sṛṣṭvā paridade paśūn brāhmaṇāya ca rājñe ca sarvāḥ paridade prajāḥ
9.d: प्रजापतिर्हि वैश्याय सृष्ट्वा परिददे पशून् ब्राह्मणाय च राज्ञे च सर्वाः परिददे प्रजाः
9.e: Prajāpati, having created cattle, made them over to the Vaiśya; while to theBrāhmaṇāand theKṣatriyahe made over all creatures.

9.s: na ca vaiśyasya kāmaḥ syānna rakṣeyaṃ paśūniti vaiśye caicchati nānyena rakṣitavyāḥ kathaṃ cana
9.d: न च वैश्यस्य कामः स्यान्न रक्षेयं पशूनिति वैश्ये चैच्छति नान्येन रक्षितव्याः कथं चन
9.e: The Vaiśya shall never conceive the wish—‘I will not tend cattle;’ and so long as the Vaiśya is willing, they should not be tended by any one else.

9.s: maṇimuktāpravālānāṃ lohānāṃ tāntavasya ca gandhānāṃ ca rasānāṃ ca vidyādarghabalābalam
9.d: मणिमुक्ताप्रवालानां लोहानां तान्तवस्य च गन्धानां च रसानां च विद्यादर्घबलाबलम्
9.e: He shall find out the relative value of gems, pearls, corals, metals, woven cloths, perfumes and condiments.

9.s: bījānāmuptividca syāt kṣetradoṣaguṇasya ca mānayogaṃ ca jānīyāt tulāyogāṃśca sarvaśaḥ
9.d: बीजानामुप्तिविद्च स्यात् क्षेत्रदोषगुणस्य च मानयोगं च जानीयात् तुलायोगांश्च सर्वशः
9.e: He should be acquainted with the manner of sowing seeds, with the good and bad qualities of the soil; he should know all kinds of weights and measures.

9.s: sārāsāraṃ ca bhāṇḍānāṃ deśānāṃ ca guṇāguṇān lābhālābhaṃ ca paṇyānāṃ paśūnāṃ parivardhanam
9.d: सारासारं च भाण्डानां देशानां च गुणागुणान् लाभालाभं च पण्यानां पशूनां परिवर्धनम्
9.e: Also the excellences and defects of commodities, the advantages and disadvantages relating to countries, the profit and loss on merchandise and also cattle-breeding.

9.s: bhṛtyānāṃ ca bhṛtiṃ vidyādbhāṣāśca vividhā nṛṇām dravyāṇāṃ sthānayogāṃśca krayavikrayameva ca
9.d: भृत्यानां च भृतिं विद्याद्भाषाश्च विविधा नृणाम् द्रव्याणां स्थानयोगांश्च क्रयविक्रयमेव च
9.e: He shall know also the wages of servants, the several languages of men, the manner of keeping goods, and also their purchase and sale.

9.s: dharmeṇa ca dravyavṛddhāvātiṣṭhedyatnamuttamam dadyācca sarvabhūtānāmannameva prayatnataḥ
9.d: धर्मेण च द्रव्यवृद्धावातिष्ठेद्यत्नमुत्तमम् दद्याच्च सर्वभूतानामन्नमेव प्रयत्नतः
9.e: He shall put forth his best efforts towards increasing his property in a righteous manner; and he shall zealously give food to all beings.

9.s: viprāṇāṃ vedaviduṣāṃ gṛhasthānāṃ yaśasvinām śuśrūṣaiva tu śūdrasya dharmo naiśreyasaḥ paraḥ param
9.d: विप्राणां वेदविदुषां गृहस्थानां यशस्विनाम् शुश्रूषैव तु शूद्रस्य धर्मो नैश्रेयसः परः परम्
9.e: For theŚūdrathe highest duty conducive to his best welfare is to attend upon suchBrāhmaṇahouse-holders as are learned in the Vedas and famous.

9.s: śucirutkṛṣṭaśuśrūṣurmṛduvāganahaṅkṛtaḥ brāhmaṇādiāśrayo nityamutkṛṣṭāṃ jātimaśnute brāhmaṇāpāśrayo
9.d: शुचिरुत्कृष्टशुश्रूषुर्मृदुवागनहङ्कृतः ब्राह्मणादिआश्रयो नित्यमुत्कृष्टां जातिमश्नुते ब्राह्मणापाश्रयो
9.e: If he is pure, attendant upon his superiors, of gentle speech, free from pride, and always dependent upon theBrāhmaṇa,—he attains a higher caste.

10.s: eṣo 'nāpadi varṇānāmuktaḥ karmavidhiḥ śubhaḥ āpadyapi hi yasteṣāṃ kramaśastannibodhata
10.d: एषो ऽनापदि वर्णानामुक्तः कर्मविधिः शुभः आपद्यपि हि यस्तेषां क्रमशस्तन्निबोधत

10.s: adhīyīraṃstrayo varṇāḥ svakarmasthā dvijātayaḥ prabrūyādbrāhmaṇastveṣāṃ naitarāviti niścayaḥ
10.d: अधीयीरंस्त्रयो वर्णाः स्वकर्मस्था द्विजातयः प्रब्रूयाद्ब्राह्मणस्त्वेषां नैतराविति निश्चयः
10.e: The three twice-born castes, devoted to their duties, shall study; but of these theBrāhmaṇaalone shall expound it, not the other two; such is the established law.

10.s: sarveṣāṃ brāhmaṇo vidyādvṛttyupāyān yathāvidhi prabrūyāditarebhyaśca svayaṃ caiva tathā bhavet
10.d: सर्वेषां ब्राह्मणो विद्याद्वृत्त्युपायान् यथाविधि प्रब्रूयादितरेभ्यश्च स्वयं चैव तथा भवेत्
10.e: TheBrāhmaṇashould know the means of livelihood for all men; he shall duly expound them to the others and himself do accordingly.

10.s: vaiśeṣyāt prakṛtiśraiṣṭhyātniyamasya ca dhāraṇāt saṃskārasya viśeṣācca varṇānāṃ brāhmaṇaḥ prabhuḥ
10.d: वैशेष्यात् प्रकृतिश्रैष्ठ्यात्नियमस्य च धारणात् संस्कारस्य विशेषाच्च वर्णानां ब्राह्मणः प्रभुः
10.e: TheBrāhmaṇais the lord of the castes, on account of his distinctive qualities, of the superiority of his origin, of his observance of restrictive rules, of the peculiar character of his sanctification.

10.s: brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyastrayo varṇā dvijātayaḥ caturtha ekajātistu śūdro nāsti tu pañcamaḥ
10.d: ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियो वैश्यस्त्रयो वर्णा द्विजातयः चतुर्थ एकजातिस्तु शूद्रो नास्ति तु पञ्चमः
10.e: TheBrāhmaṇa, theKṣatriyaand theVaiśyaare the three twice-born castes; the fourth is the one caste,Śūdra; there is no fifth.

10.s: sarvavarṇeṣu tulyāsu patnīṣvakṣatayoniṣu ānulomyena saṃbhūtā jātyā jñeyāsta eva te
10.d: सर्ववर्णेषु तुल्यासु पत्नीष्वक्षतयोनिषु आनुलोम्येन संभूता जात्या ज्ञेयास्त एव ते
10.e: Among all castes, those only who are born of consorts wedded in the natural order, as virgins of equal status, are to be regarded as the same (as their father).

10.s: strīṣvanantarajātāsu dvijairutpāditān sutān sadṛśāneva tānāhurmātṛdoṣavigarhitān
10.d: स्त्रीष्वनन्तरजातासु द्विजैरुत्पादितान् सुतान् सदृशानेव तानाहुर्मातृदोषविगर्हितान्
10.e: The sons begotten by twice-born men on wives of the next lower castes, they declare to be equal, tainted as they are by the defect of their mothers.

10.s: anantarāsu jātānāṃ vidhireṣa sanātanaḥ dvyekāntarāsu jātānāṃ dharmyaṃ vidyādimaṃ vidhim
10.d: अनन्तरासु जातानां विधिरेष सनातनः द्व्येकान्तरासु जातानां धर्म्यं विद्यादिमं विधिम्
10.e: Such is the eternal law relating to those born of wives of the next lower castes; know this (following) to be the right rule pertaining to those born of wives two or three degrees lower.

10.s: brāhmaṇādvaiśyakanyāyāmambaṣṭho nāma jāyate niṣādaḥ śūdrakanyāyāṃ yaḥ pāraśava ucyate
10.d: ब्राह्मणाद्वैश्यकन्यायामम्बष्ठो नाम जायते निषादः शूद्रकन्यायां यः पारशव उच्यते
10.e: From theBrāhmaṇaon aVaiśyamaiden is born the ‘Ambaṣṭha’ and on aŚūdramaiden the ‘Niṣāda,’ who is called ‘Pārośora.’

10.s: kṣatriyātśūdrakanyāyāṃ krūrācāravihāravān kṣatraśūdravapurjanturugro nāma prajāyate
10.d: क्षत्रियात्शूद्रकन्यायां क्रूराचारविहारवान् क्षत्रशूद्रवपुर्जन्तुरुग्रो नाम प्रजायते
10.e: From theKṣatriyaon aŚūdramaiden is born a being called ‘Ugra,’ of the stuff of theKṣatriyaandŚūdra, cruel in his deeds and dealings.

10.s: viprasya triṣu varṇeṣu nṛpatervarṇayordvayoḥ vaiśyasya varṇe caikasmin ṣaḍete 'pasadāḥ smṛtāḥ
10.d: विप्रस्य त्रिषु वर्णेषु नृपतेर्वर्णयोर्द्वयोः वैश्यस्य वर्णे चैकस्मिन् षडेते ऽपसदाः स्मृताः
10.e: Children of theBrāhmaṇafrom the three lower castes, of theKṣatriyafrom the two lower castes, and of the Vaiśya from the one lower caste,—these six have been declared to be ‘lowborn.’

10.s: kṣatriyādviprakanyāyāṃ sūto bhavati jātitaḥ vaiśyān māgadhavaidehau rājaviprāṅganāsutau
10.d: क्षत्रियाद्विप्रकन्यायां सूतो भवति जातितः वैश्यान् मागधवैदेहौ राजविप्राङ्गनासुतौ
10.e: One born from theKṣatriyaon theBrāhmaṇamaiden is ‘Sūta’ in caste; and the sons born on theKṣatriyaand theBrāhmaṇamaiden from the vaiśya are ‘Māgadha’ and ‘Vaideha’ respectively.

10.s: śūdrādāyogavaḥ kṣattā caṇḍālaścādhamo nṛṇām vaiśyarājanyaviprāsu jāyante varṇasaṅkarāḥ
10.d: शूद्रादायोगवः क्षत्ता चण्डालश्चाधमो नृणाम् वैश्यराजन्यविप्रासु जायन्ते वर्णसङ्कराः
10.e: From theŚūdraon theVaiśya, theKṣatriyaand theBrāhmaṇamaiden are born the mixed castes, ‘Āyogava,’Kṣattṛand the ‘Caṇḍāla,’ the lowest of men.

10.s: ekāntare tvānulomyādambaṣṭhaugrau yathā smṛtau kṣattṛvaidehakau tadvat prātilomye 'pi janmani
10.d: एकान्तरे त्वानुलोम्यादम्बष्ठौग्रौ यथा स्मृतौ क्षत्तृवैदेहकौ तद्वत् प्रातिलोम्ये ऽपि जन्मनि
10.e: As the ‘Ambaṣṭha’ and the ‘ugra’ are born in the ‘natural order’ from a woman two degrees removed,—even so have been declared to be the ‘Kṣattṛ’ and the ‘Vaideha,’ though born in the ‘inverse order.’

10.s: putrā ye 'nantarastrījāḥ krameṇauktā dvijanmanām tānanantaranāmnastu mātṛdoṣāt pracakṣate
10.d: पुत्रा ये ऽनन्तरस्त्रीजाः क्रमेणौक्ता द्विजन्मनाम् ताननन्तरनाम्नस्तु मातृदोषात् प्रचक्षते
10.e: The sons of twice-born men from women of the next lower caste, who have been enunciated in due order, are called by the name of the lower caste, on account of the taint attaching to their mothers.

10.s: brāhmaṇādugrakanyāyāmāvṛto nāma jāyate ābhīro 'mbaṣṭhakanyāyāmāyogavyāṃ tu dhigvaṇaḥ
10.d: ब्राह्मणादुग्रकन्यायामावृतो नाम जायते आभीरो ऽम्बष्ठकन्यायामायोगव्यां तु धिग्वणः
10.e: One born from the ‘Niṣāda’ on theŚūdrawoman is a ‘Pukkasa’ by caste; but one born from theŚūdraon the ‘Niṣāda’ woman is called the ‘Kukkaṭaka’.

10.s: āyogavaśca kṣattā ca caṇḍālaścādhamo nṛṇām prātilomyena jāyante śūdrādapasadāstrayaḥ
10.d: आयोगवश्च क्षत्ता च चण्डालश्चाधमो नृणाम् प्रातिलोम्येन जायन्ते शूद्रादपसदास्त्रयः
10.e: One born from the ‘Niṣāda’ on theŚūdrawoman is a ‘Pukkasa’ by caste; but one born from theŚūdraon the ‘Niṣāda’ woman is called the ‘Kukkaṭaka’.

10.s: vaiśyān māgadhavaidehau kṣatriyāt sūta eva tu pratīpamete jāyante pare 'pyapasadāstrayaḥ
10.d: वैश्यान् मागधवैदेहौ क्षत्रियात् सूत एव तु प्रतीपमेते जायन्ते परे ऽप्यपसदास्त्रयः
10.e: One born from the ‘Niṣāda’ on theŚūdrawoman is a ‘Pukkasa’ by caste; but one born from theŚūdraon the ‘Niṣāda’ woman is called the ‘Kukkaṭaka’.

10.s: jāto niṣādātśūdrāyāṃ jātyā bhavati pukkasaḥ śūdrāj jāto niṣādyāṃ tu sa vai kukkuṭakaḥ smṛtaḥ
10.d: जातो निषादात्शूद्रायां जात्या भवति पुक्कसः शूद्राज् जातो निषाद्यां तु स वै कुक्कुटकः स्मृतः
10.e: One born from the ‘Niṣāda’ on theŚūdrawoman is a ‘Pukkasa’ by caste; but one born from theŚūdraon the ‘Niṣāda’ woman is called the ‘Kukkaṭaka’.

10.s: kṣatturjātastathaugrāyāṃ śvapāka iti kīrtyate vaidehakena tvambaṣṭhyāmutpanno veṇa ucyate
10.d: क्षत्तुर्जातस्तथौग्रायां श्वपाक इति कीर्त्यते वैदेहकेन त्वम्बष्ठ्यामुत्पन्नो वेण उच्यते
10.e: One born from the ‘Kṣattṛ’ on the ‘Ugrā’ woman is called ‘Śvapāka;’ and one begotten by the ‘Vaideha’ on the ‘Ambaṣṭha’ woman is called ‘Veṇa.’

10.s: dvijātayaḥ savarṇāsu janayantyavratāṃstu yān tān sāvitrīparibhraṣṭān vrātyāniti vinirdiśet
10.d: द्विजातयः सवर्णासु जनयन्त्यव्रतांस्तु यान् तान् सावित्रीपरिभ्रष्टान् व्रात्यानिति विनिर्दिशेत्
10.e: The sons that the twice-born men beget on wives of equal caste, but who, not fulfilling their sacred duties, become excluded from theSāvitrī—should be designated as ‘Vrātyas’ (apostates).

10.s: vrātyāt tu jāyate viprāt pāpātmā bhūrjakaṇṭakaḥ bhṛjjakaṇṭakaḥ āvantyavāṭadhānau ca puṣpadhaḥ śaikha eva ca
10.d: व्रात्यात् तु जायते विप्रात् पापात्मा भूर्जकण्टकः भृज्जकण्टकः आवन्त्यवाटधानौ च पुष्पधः शैख एव च
10.e: From the ‘Apostate’Brāhmaṇais born the evil- natured ‘Bhṛjjakaṇṭaka,’ theĀvantya, the ‘Vāṭadhāna’ the ‘Puṣpadha,’ and the ‘Śaikha.’

10.s: jhallo mallaśca rājanyādvrātyātnicchivireva ca vrātyātlicchavireva ca naṭaśca karaṇaścaiva khaso draviḍa eva ca
10.d: झल्लो मल्लश्च राजन्याद्व्रात्यात्निच्छिविरेव च व्रात्यात्लिच्छविरेव च नटश्च करणश्चैव खसो द्रविड एव च
10.e: And from the ‘Apostate’ Vaiśya is born the ‘Sudhanvan’ the ‘Ācārya,’ the ‘Karuṣa,’ the ‘Vijanman,’ the ‘Maitra’ and the ‘Sāttvata.’

10.s: vaiśyāt tu jāyate vrātyāt sudhanvā 'cārya eva ca kāruṣaśca vijanmā ca maitraḥ sātvata eva ca
10.d: वैश्यात् तु जायते व्रात्यात् सुधन्वा ऽचार्य एव च कारुषश्च विजन्मा च मैत्रः सात्वत एव च
10.e: And from the ‘Apostate’ Vaiśya is born the ‘Sudhanvan’ the ‘Ācārya,’ the ‘Karuṣa,’ the ‘Vijanman,’ the ‘Maitra’ and the ‘Sāttvata.’

10.s: vyabhicāreṇa varṇānāmavedyāvedanena ca svakarmaṇāṃ ca tyāgena jāyante varṇasaṅkarāḥ
10.d: व्यभिचारेण वर्णानामवेद्यावेदनेन च स्वकर्मणां च त्यागेन जायन्ते वर्णसङ्कराः
10.e: ‘Confused castes’ are produced by infidelity among the castes, by the marrying of women unfit for marriage, and by the neglect of one’s duties.

10.s: saṅkīrṇayonayo ye tu pratilomānulomajāḥ anyonyavyatiṣaktāśca tān pravakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ
10.d: सङ्कीर्णयोनयो ये तु प्रतिलोमानुलोमजाः अन्योन्यव्यतिषक्ताश्च तान् प्रवक्ष्याम्यशेषतः
10.e: I am going to describe those persons of mixed origin who are born in the natural and in the inverse order and are mutually connected.

10.s: sūto vaidehakaścaiva caṇḍālaśca narādhamaḥ māgadhaḥ tathā 'yogava eva ca kṣatrajātiśca kṣattṛjātiśca
10.d: सूतो वैदेहकश्चैव चण्डालश्च नराधमः मागधः तथा ऽयोगव एव च क्षत्रजातिश्च क्षत्तृजातिश्च

10.s: ete ṣaṭ sadṛśān varṇāñjanayanti svayoniṣu mātṛjātyāṃ prasūyante pravārāsu ca yoniṣu mātṛjātyāḥ
10.d: एते षट् सदृशान् वर्णाञ्जनयन्ति स्वयोनिषु मातृजात्यां प्रसूयन्ते प्रवारासु च योनिषु मातृजात्याः
10.e: These six beget similar castes on women belonging to the same caste as themselves; so also those belonging to the mother’s caste procreate (on women of the same caste), as also on women of higher castes.

10.s: yathā trayāṇāṃ varṇānāṃ dvayorātmā 'sya jāyate ānantaryāt svayonyāṃ tu tathā bāhyeṣvapi kramāt kramaḥ
10.d: यथा त्रयाणां वर्णानां द्वयोरात्मा ऽस्य जायते आनन्तर्यात् स्वयोन्यां तु तथा बाह्येष्वपि क्रमात् क्रमः
10.e: As to one his own alter-ego is born from two out of the three nearest castes, as also from his own caste,—even so is the order among those out of the outer circle.

10.s: te cāpi bāhyān subahūṃstato 'pyadhikadūṣitān parasparasya dāreṣu janayanti vigarhitān
10.d: ते चापि बाह्यान् सुबहूंस्ततो ऽप्यधिकदूषितान् परस्परस्य दारेषु जनयन्ति विगर्हितान्
10.e: Those also beget on each other’s wives several ‘alien’ sons, greatly tainted and despised.

10.s: yathaiva śūdro brāhmaṇyāṃ bāhyaṃ jantuṃ prasūyate tathā bāhyataraṃ bāhyaścāturvarṇye prasūyate
10.d: यथैव शूद्रो ब्राह्मण्यां बाह्यं जन्तुं प्रसूयते तथा बाह्यतरं बाह्यश्चातुर्वर्ण्ये प्रसूयते
10.e: As theŚūdrabegets an ‘alien’ being on aBrāhmaṇawoman,—even so an alien propagates on females of the four castes, a still more alien being.

10.s: pratikūlaṃ vartamānā bāhyā bāhyatarān punaḥ hīnā hīnān prasūyante varṇān pañcadaśaiva tu
10.d: प्रतिकूलं वर्तमाना बाह्या बाह्यतरान् पुनः हीना हीनान् प्रसूयन्ते वर्णान् पञ्चदशैव तु
10.e: Aliens behaving discordantly, beget fifteen castes, still more alien, disgraced and not disgraced.

10.s: prasādhanaupacārajñamadāsaṃ dāsajīvanam dāsyajīvinaṃ sairindhraṃ vāgurāvṛttiṃ sūte dasyurayogave sairandhraṃ
10.d: प्रसाधनौपचारज्ञमदासं दासजीवनम् दास्यजीविनं सैरिन्ध्रं वागुरावृत्तिं सूते दस्युरयोगवे सैरन्ध्रं
10.e: The ‘Dasyu’ begets on the ‘Āyogava,’ the ‘Sairandhra,’ skilled in toilet and attendance, who, though not a slave, makes his living like a slave, and also lives by catching animals.

10.s: maitreyakaṃ tu vaideho mādhūkaṃ saṃprasūyate nr̥̄n praśaṃsatyajasraṃ yo ghaṇṭātāḍo 'ruṇaudaye
10.d: मैत्रेयकं तु वैदेहो माधूकं संप्रसूयते न्र्̥̄न् प्रशंसत्यजस्रं यो घण्टाताडो ऽरुणौदये
10.e: But the ‘Vaideha’ begets theMadhūka-like‘Maitreyaka,’ who constantly praises men, and serves as the bell-ringer at sunrise.

10.s: niṣādo mārgavaṃ sūte dāsaṃ naukarmajīvinam kaivartamiti yaṃ prāhurāryāvartanivāsinaḥ
10.d: निषादो मार्गवं सूते दासं नौकर्मजीविनम् कैवर्तमिति यं प्राहुरार्यावर्तनिवासिनः
10.e: The ‘Niṣāda’ begets the ‘Mārgava’ or ‘Dāsa,’ who subsists by working the boat, and whom the inhabitants ofĀryāvartacall ‘Kaivarta.’

10.s: mṛtavastrabhṛtsvnārīṣu garhitānnāśanāsu ca 'nāryāṣu bhavantyāyogavīṣvete jātihīnāḥ pṛthak trayaḥ
10.d: मृतवस्त्रभृत्स्व्नारीषु गर्हितान्नाशनासु च ऽनार्याषु भवन्त्यायोगवीष्वेते जातिहीनाः पृथक् त्रयः
10.e: These three, devoid of caste, are severally born from ‘Āyogava’ women, who wear the clothes of the dead, are ignoble, and eat despised food.

10.s: kārāvaro niṣādāt tu carmakāraḥ prasūyate carmakāraṃ vaidehikādandhramedau bahirgrāmapratiśrayau
10.d: कारावरो निषादात् तु चर्मकारः प्रसूयते चर्मकारं वैदेहिकादन्ध्रमेदौ बहिर्ग्रामप्रतिश्रयौ
10.e: From the ‘Niṣāda’ is born of the ‘Kārāvara,’ who works in leather; and from the ‘Vaiḍehaka’ the ‘Andhra’ and the ‘Meda,’ who have their dwellings outside the village.

10.s: caṇḍālāt pāṇḍusopākastvaksāravyavahāravān āhiṇḍiko niṣādena vaidehyāmeva jāyate
10.d: चण्डालात् पाण्डुसोपाकस्त्वक्सारव्यवहारवान् आहिण्डिको निषादेन वैदेह्यामेव जायते
10.e: On the ‘Vaideha’ woman from the ‘Caṇḍāla’ is born the ‘Paṇḍusopāka’ who deals in bamboos; as also the ‘Āhiṇḍika’ from the ‘Niṣāda.’

10.s: caṇḍālena tu sopāko mūlavyasanavṛttimān pukkasyāṃ jāyate pāpaḥ sadā sajjanagarhitaḥ pulkasyāṃ
10.d: चण्डालेन तु सोपाको मूलव्यसनवृत्तिमान् पुक्कस्यां जायते पापः सदा सज्जनगर्हितः पुल्कस्यां
10.e: By the ‘Caṇḍāla,’ on the ‘Pukkasa’ woman is begotten the ‘Sopāka,’ whose livelihood consists of death, and who are wicked and despised by good people.

10.s: niṣādastrī tu caṇḍālāt putramantyāvasāyinam śmaśānagocaraṃ sūte bāhyānāmapi garhitam
10.d: निषादस्त्री तु चण्डालात् पुत्रमन्त्यावसायिनम् श्मशानगोचरं सूते बाह्यानामपि गर्हितम्
10.e: The ‘Niṣāda’ woman bears to the ‘Caṇḍāla’ the son called ‘Antyāvasāyin,’ working in the cremation-ground, despised even by out-casts.

10.s: saṅkare jātayastvetāḥ pitṛmātṛpradarśitāḥ prachannā vā prakāśā vā veditavyāḥ svakarmabhiḥ
10.d: सङ्करे जातयस्त्वेताः पितृमातृप्रदर्शिताः प्रछन्ना वा प्रकाशा वा वेदितव्याः स्वकर्मभिः
10.e: These castes, proceeding from mixtures, have been described in relation to their fathers and mothers; and whether manifest or unmanifest, they may be known by their occupations.

10.s: svajātijānantarajāḥ ṣaṭ sutā dvijadharmiṇaḥ śūdrāṇāṃ tu sadharmāṇaḥ sarve 'padhvaṃsajāḥ smṛtāḥ
10.d: स्वजातिजानन्तरजाः षट् सुता द्विजधर्मिणः शूद्राणां तु सधर्माणः सर्वे ऽपध्वंसजाः स्मृताः
10.e: Six sons born or women of the same caste and of those of the next lower castes partake of the character of ‘twice-born’ persons. But all those born of violation have been declared to be of the nature ofŚūdras.

10.s: tapobījaprabhāvaistu te gacchanti yuge yuge utkarṣaṃ cāpakarṣaṃ ca manuṣyeṣviha janmataḥ
10.d: तपोबीजप्रभावैस्तु ते गच्छन्ति युगे युगे उत्कर्षं चापकर्षं च मनुष्येष्विह जन्मतः
10.e: By the force of austerities and the seed they attain higher or lower rank among men, through birth, cycle after cycle.

10.s: śanakaistu kriyālopādimāḥ kṣatriyajātayaḥ vṛṣalatvaṃ gatā loke brāhmaṇādarśanena ca brāhmaṇātikrameṇa ca
10.d: शनकैस्तु क्रियालोपादिमाः क्षत्रियजातयः वृषलत्वं गता लोके ब्राह्मणादर्शनेन च ब्राह्मणातिक्रमेण च
10.e: But by the omission of the sacred rites, and also by their neglect ofBrāhmaṇas, the followingKṣatriyacastes have gradually sunk to the position of the low-born.

10.s: pauṇḍrakāścauḍradraviḍāḥ kāmbojā yavanāḥ śakāḥ puṇḍrakāścoḍadraviḍāḥ pāradāpahlavāścīnāḥ kirātā daradāḥ khaśāḥ
10.d: पौण्ड्रकाश्चौड्रद्रविडाः काम्बोजा यवनाः शकाः पुण्ड्रकाश्चोडद्रविडाः पारदापह्लवाश्चीनाः किराता दरदाः खशाः
10.e: ThePuṇḍrakas, theCoḍas[=Cauḍras], theDraviḍas, theKāmbojas, the Yavanas, theŚākas, thePāradas, the Pahlavas, theCīnas, theKirātas, the Daradas and the Khaśas.

10.s: mukhabāhūrupadjānāṃ yā loke jātayo bahiḥ mlecchavācaścāryavācaḥ sarve te dasyavaḥ smṛtāḥ
10.d: मुखबाहूरुपद्जानां या लोके जातयो बहिः म्लेच्छवाचश्चार्यवाचः सर्वे ते दस्यवः स्मृताः
10.e: All those races of the world which are outside the pale of the people ‘born of the mouth, the arms, the thighs and the feet,’—speaking the ‘barbaric’ or the ‘refined’ language—are called ‘Dasyu.’

10.s: ye dvijānāmapasadā ye cāpadhvaṃsajāḥ smṛtāḥ te ninditairvartayeyurdvijānāmeva karmabhiḥ
10.d: ये द्विजानामपसदा ये चापध्वंसजाः स्मृताः ते निन्दितैर्वर्तयेयुर्द्विजानामेव कर्मभिः
10.e: The base-born sons of the ‘twice-born,’ as also those who have been declared to be ‘born of transgression,’ shall subsist by lowly services of ‘twice-born’ persons.

10.s: sūtānāmaśvasārathyamambaṣṭhānāṃ cikitsanam vaidehakānāṃ strīkāryaṃ māgadhānāṃ vaṇikpathaḥ
10.d: सूतानामश्वसारथ्यमम्बष्ठानां चिकित्सनम् वैदेहकानां स्त्रीकार्यं मागधानां वणिक्पथः
10.e: ForSūtas, the management of horses and chariots; forAmbaṣṭhas, the art of healing; forVaidehakas, the service of women; and forMāgadhas, trade.

10.s: matsyaghāto niṣādānāṃ tvaṣṭistvāyogavasya ca medāndhracuñcumadgūnāmāraṇyapaśuhiṃsanam
10.d: मत्स्यघातो निषादानां त्वष्टिस्त्वायोगवस्य च मेदान्ध्रचुञ्चुमद्गूनामारण्यपशुहिंसनम्
10.e: ForNiṣādas, the killing of fish; forĀyogavas, carpentry; and for medas, andhras,Cuñcusand Madgus, the killing of wild animals.

10.s: kṣattryugrapukkasānāṃ tu bilaukovadhabandhanam dhigvaṇānāṃ carmakāryaṃ veṇānāṃ bhāṇḍavādanam
10.d: क्षत्त्र्युग्रपुक्कसानां तु बिलौकोवधबन्धनम् धिग्वणानां चर्मकार्यं वेणानां भाण्डवादनम्
10.e: ForKṣattṛs, Ugras and Pukkasas, the killing and catching of animals living underground; forDhigvaṇas, work in leather; and forVeṇasthe beating of drums.

10.s: caityadrumaśmaśāneṣu śaileṣūpavaneṣu ca vaseyurete vijñātā vartayantaḥ svakarmabhiḥ
10.d: चैत्यद्रुमश्मशानेषु शैलेषूपवनेषु च वसेयुरेते विज्ञाता वर्तयन्तः स्वकर्मभिः
10.e: Near worshipped trees and cremation-grounds, on hills and in groves, these shall dwell, duly marked, subsisting by their respective occupations.

10.s: caṇḍālaśvapacānāṃ tu bahirgrāmāt pratiśrayaḥ apapātrāśca kartavyā dhanameṣāṃ śvagardabham
10.d: चण्डालश्वपचानां तु बहिर्ग्रामात् प्रतिश्रयः अपपात्राश्च कर्तव्या धनमेषां श्वगर्दभम्
10.e: The dwelling ofCaṇḍālasand Śvapacas shall be outside the village; they shall be made ‘Apapātra,’ and their wealth shall consist of dogs and donkeys.

10.s: vāsāṃsi mṛtacailāni bhinnabhāṇḍeṣu bhojanam kārṣṇāyasamalaṅkāraḥ parivrajyā ca nityaśaḥ
10.d: वासांसि मृतचैलानि भिन्नभाण्डेषु भोजनम् कार्ष्णायसमलङ्कारः परिव्रज्या च नित्यशः
10.e: The clothes of dead bodies shall be their dress; they shall eat in broken dishes; their ornaments shall be of iron, and they shall be constantly wandering.

10.s: na taiḥ samayamanvicchet puruṣo dharmamācaran vyavahāro mithasteṣāṃ vivāhaḥ sadṛśaiḥ saha
10.d: न तैः समयमन्विच्छेत् पुरुषो धर्ममाचरन् व्यवहारो मिथस्तेषां विवाहः सदृशैः सह
10.e: One who follows the law shall not seek intercourse with them; their transactions shall be among themselves and their marriages with their equals.

10.s: annameṣāṃ parādhīnaṃ deyaṃ syādbhinnabhājane rātrau na vicareyuste grāmeṣu nagareṣu ca
10.d: अन्नमेषां पराधीनं देयं स्याद्भिन्नभाजने रात्रौ न विचरेयुस्ते ग्रामेषु नगरेषु च
10.e: Their food should be given to them, through others, and in a broken dish; they shall not wander about in villages or cities during the night.

10.s: divā careyuḥ kāryārthaṃ cihnitā rājaśāsanaiḥ abāndhavaṃ śavaṃ caiva nirhareyuriti sthitiḥ
10.d: दिवा चरेयुः कार्यार्थं चिह्निता राजशासनैः अबान्धवं शवं चैव निर्हरेयुरिति स्थितिः
10.e: During the day they may go about on business distinguished by royal signs; they shall carry out corpses of people without relations; such is the law.

10.s: vadhyāṃśca hanyuḥ satataṃ yathāśāstraṃ nṛpājñayā vadhyavāsāṃsi gṛhṇīyuḥ śayyāścābharaṇāni ca
10.d: वध्यांश्च हन्युः सततं यथाशास्त्रं नृपाज्ञया वध्यवासांसि गृह्णीयुः शय्याश्चाभरणानि च
10.e: They shall always execute criminals, in accordance with law, under the orders of the king; and they shall take away the clothes, the beds and the ornaments of those executed.

10.s: varṇāpetamavijñātaṃ naraṃ kaluṣayonijam āryarūpamivānāryaṃ karmabhiḥ svairvibhāvayet
10.d: वर्णापेतमविज्ञातं नरं कलुषयोनिजम् आर्यरूपमिवानार्यं कर्मभिः स्वैर्विभावयेत्
10.e: The man of impure origin, who is devoid of caste, unknown, a non-Aryan, even though having the appearance of an Aryan,—one shall discover by his acts.

10.s: anāryatā niṣṭhuratā krūratā niṣkriyātmatā puruṣaṃ vyañjayantīha loke kaluṣayonijam
10.d: अनार्यता निष्ठुरता क्रूरता निष्क्रियात्मता पुरुषं व्यञ्जयन्तीह लोके कलुषयोनिजम्
10.e: Snobbishness, harshness, cruelty, and proneness to neglect duties, mark the man of impure origin in this world.

10.s: pitryaṃ vā bhajate śīlaṃ māturvaubhayameva vā na kathaṃ cana duryoniḥ prakṛtiṃ svāṃ niyacchati
10.d: पित्र्यं वा भजते शीलं मातुर्वौभयमेव वा न कथं चन दुर्योनिः प्रकृतिं स्वां नियच्छति
10.e: The base-born man bears the character or his father, or of his mother, or of both; he can never conceal his origin.

10.s: kule mukhye 'pi jātasya yasya syādyonisaṅkaraḥ saṃśrayatyeva tatśīlaṃ naro 'lpamapi vā bahu
10.d: कुले मुख्ये ऽपि जातस्य यस्य स्याद्योनिसङ्करः संश्रयत्येव तत्शीलं नरो ऽल्पमपि वा बहु
10.e: Even when one is born in a great family, if there be a confusion regarding his parentage, he surely imbibes the traits thereof, to a greater or less extent.

10.s: yatra tvete paridhvaṃsāj jāyante varṇadūṣakāḥ rāṣṭrikaiḥ saha tadrāṣṭraṃ kṣiprameva vinaśyati rāṣṭriyaiḥ
10.d: यत्र त्वेते परिध्वंसाज् जायन्ते वर्णदूषकाः राष्ट्रिकैः सह तद्राष्ट्रं क्षिप्रमेव विनश्यति राष्ट्रियैः
10.e: That kingdom in which such caste-defilers are born of criminal intercourses, speedily perishes, along with the people.

10.s: brāhmaṇārthe gavārthe vā dehatyāgo 'nupaskṛtaḥ strībālābhyupapattau ca bāhyānāṃ siddhikāraṇam strībālābhyavapattau ca
10.d: ब्राह्मणार्थे गवार्थे वा देहत्यागो ऽनुपस्कृतः स्त्रीबालाभ्युपपत्तौ च बाह्यानां सिद्धिकारणम् स्त्रीबालाभ्यवपत्तौ च
10.e: For aliens perfection is secured by unrequitedly giving up the body for the sake ofBrāhmaṇasand cows, and in defence of women and children.

10.s: ahiṃsā satyamasteyaṃ śaucamindriyanigrahaḥ etaṃ sāmāsikaṃ dharmaṃ cāturvarṇye 'bravīn manuḥ
10.d: अहिंसा सत्यमस्तेयं शौचमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः एतं सामासिकं धर्मं चातुर्वर्ण्ये ऽब्रवीन् मनुः
10.e: Abstention from injuring, truthfulness, abstention from unlawful appropriation, purity and control of the sense-organs,—this Manu has declared to be the sum and substance of duty for the four castes.

10.s: śūdrāyāṃ brāhmaṇāj jātaḥ śreyasā cet prajāyate aśreyān śreyasīṃ jātiṃ gacchatyā saptamādyugāt
10.d: शूद्रायां ब्राह्मणाज् जातः श्रेयसा चेत् प्रजायते अश्रेयान् श्रेयसीं जातिं गच्छत्या सप्तमाद्युगात्
10.e: If the child born from aŚūdrawoman to aBrāhmaṇagoes on being wedded to a superior person,—the inferior attains the superior caste, within the seventh generation.

10.s: śūdro brāhmaṇatāmeti brāhmaṇaścaiti śūdratām kṣatriyāj jātamevaṃ tu vidyādvaiśyāt tathaiva ca
10.d: शूद्रो ब्राह्मणतामेति ब्राह्मणश्चैति शूद्रताम् क्षत्रियाज् जातमेवं तु विद्याद्वैश्यात् तथैव च
10.e: TheŚūdraattains the position of theBrāhmaṇaand theBrāhmaṇasinks to the position of theŚūdra; the same should be understood to be the case with the offspring of theKṣatriyaor of the vaiśya.

10.s: anāryāyāṃ samutpanno brāhmaṇāt tu yadṛcchayā brāhmaṇyāmapyanāryāt tu śreyastvaṃ kvaiti cedbhavet) kasya cidbhavet
10.d: अनार्यायां समुत्पन्नो ब्राह्मणात् तु यदृच्छया ब्राह्मण्यामप्यनार्यात् तु श्रेयस्त्वं क्वैति चेद्भवेत्) कस्य चिद्भवेत्
10.e: (question).—If a child is somehow born to aBrāhmaṇafrom a non-Aryan woman, and another is born to a non-Aryan from aBrāhmaṇawoman,—with which of these would the ‘superiority’ lie?

10.s: jāto nāryāmanāryāyāmāryādāryo bhavedguṇaiḥ jāto 'pyanāryādāryāyāmanārya iti niścayaḥ
10.d: जातो नार्यामनार्यायामार्यादार्यो भवेद्गुणैः जातो ऽप्यनार्यादार्यायामनार्य इति निश्चयः
10.e: The decision is that—‘one born to anĀryafrom aNon-Āryawoman may be anĀryain quality; but one born to aNon-āryaeven from anĀryawoman is alwaysNon-Ārya’

10.s: tāvubhāvapyasaṃskāryāviti dharmo vyavasthitaḥ vaiguṇyāj janmanaḥ pūrva uttaraḥ pratilomataḥ janmataḥ
10.d: तावुभावप्यसंस्कार्याविति धर्मो व्यवस्थितः वैगुण्याज् जन्मनः पूर्व उत्तरः प्रतिलोमतः जन्मतः
10.e: The settled law is that both these are unfit for the sacraments:—the former on account of the defect in his birth and the latter by reason of his being horn ‘in the inverse order.’

10.s: subījaṃ caiva sukṣetre jātaṃ saṃpadyate yathā tathā 'ryāj jāta āryāyāṃ sarvaṃ saṃskāramarhati
10.d: सुबीजं चैव सुक्षेत्रे जातं संपद्यते यथा तथा ऽर्याज् जात आर्यायां सर्वं संस्कारमर्हति
10.e: Just as good seed grown in a good soil turns out well, so is the child born to anĀryafrom anĀryawoman worthy of all sacraments.

10.s: bījameke praśaṃsanti kṣetramanye manīṣiṇaḥ bījakṣetre tathaivānye tatraiyaṃ tu vyavasthitiḥ
10.d: बीजमेके प्रशंसन्ति क्षेत्रमन्ये मनीषिणः बीजक्षेत्रे तथैवान्ये तत्रैयं तु व्यवस्थितिः
10.e: Some wise men extol the seed, while others the soil; while yet others extol both the seed and the soil. The decision on this point is as follows.

10.s: akṣetre bījamutsṛṣṭamantaraiva vinaśyati abījakamapi kṣetraṃ kevalaṃ sthaṇḍilaṃ bhavet
10.d: अक्षेत्रे बीजमुत्सृष्टमन्तरैव विनश्यति अबीजकमपि क्षेत्रं केवलं स्थण्डिलं भवेत्
10.e: The seed sown on barren soil perishes prematurely; and soil without the seed would be a mere barren plot.

10.s: yasmādbījaprabhāveṇa tiryagjā ṛṣayo 'bhavan pūjitāśca praśastāśca tasmādbījaṃ praśasyate viśiṣyate
10.d: यस्माद्बीजप्रभावेण तिर्यग्जा ऋषयो ऽभवन् पूजिताश्च प्रशस्ताश्च तस्माद्बीजं प्रशस्यते विशिष्यते
10.e: Because through the power of the seed, those born of animals became sages, honoured and extolled, therefore it is the seed that is more important.

10.s: anāryamāryakarmāṇamāryaṃ cānāryakarmiṇam saṃpradhāryābravīddhātā na samau nāsamāviti
10.d: अनार्यमार्यकर्माणमार्यं चानार्यकर्मिणम् संप्रधार्याब्रवीद्धाता न समौ नासमाविति
10.e: Having examined theNon-āryabehaving like anĀryaand theĀryabehaving like theNon-Ārya, the creator declared ‘that these are neither equal nor unequal.’

10.s: brāhmaṇā brahmayonisthā ye svakarmaṇyavasthitāḥ te samyagupajīveyuḥ ṣaṭ karmāṇi yathākramam
10.d: ब्राह्मणा ब्रह्मयोनिस्था ये स्वकर्मण्यवस्थिताः ते सम्यगुपजीवेयुः षट् कर्माणि यथाक्रमम्
10.e: Brāhmaṇasof pureBrāhmaṇa-birth, intent upon their duties, should duly perform the six acts in due order.

10.s: adhyāpanamadhyayanaṃ yajanaṃ yājanaṃ tathā dānaṃ pratigrahaścaiva ṣaṭ karmāṇyagrajanmanaḥ
10.d: अध्यापनमध्ययनं यजनं याजनं तथा दानं प्रतिग्रहश्चैव षट् कर्माण्यग्रजन्मनः
10.e: Teaching, studying, sacrificing for oneself, sacrificing for others, giving and receiving gifts are the six functions for the ‘first born’.

10.s: ṣaṇṇāṃ tu karmaṇāmasya trīṇi karmāṇi jīvikā yājanādhyāpane caiva viśuddhācca pratigrahaḥ
10.d: षण्णां तु कर्मणामस्य त्रीणि कर्माणि जीविका याजनाध्यापने चैव विशुद्धाच्च प्रतिग्रहः
10.e: From among these six functions, three are his means of livelihood:viz., sacrificing for others, Teaching and Receiving gifts from pure men.

10.s: trayo dharmā nivartante brāhmaṇāt kṣatriyaṃ prati adhyāpanaṃ yājanaṃ ca tṛtīyaśca pratigrahaḥ
10.d: त्रयो धर्मा निवर्तन्ते ब्राह्मणात् क्षत्रियं प्रति अध्यापनं याजनं च तृतीयश्च प्रतिग्रहः
10.e: From theBrāhmaṇacoming to theKṣatriya, three of these functions cease;—viz., Teaching, Sacrificing for others, and third, the Receiving of gifts.

10.s: vaiśyaṃ prati tathaivaite nivarteranniti sthitiḥ na tau prati hi tān dharmān manurāha prajāpatiḥ prati hitān dharmān
10.d: वैश्यं प्रति तथैवैते निवर्तेरन्निति स्थितिः न तौ प्रति हि तान् धर्मान् मनुराह प्रजापतिः प्रति हितान् धर्मान्
10.e: For the Vaiśya also these three should cease,—such is the law; sincePrajāpatiManu has not prescribed these duties for those two (castes).

10.s: śastrāstrabhṛttvaṃ kṣatrasya vaṇikpaśukṛṣirviṣaḥ ājīvanārthaṃ dharmastu dānamadhyayanaṃ yajiḥ
10.d: शस्त्रास्त्रभृत्त्वं क्षत्रस्य वणिक्पशुकृषिर्विषः आजीवनार्थं धर्मस्तु दानमध्ययनं यजिः
10.e: For theKṣatriyacarrying of arms and weapons, and for the Vaiśya, trade, cattle-tending and agriculture, are the means of livelihood; while giving, studying and sacrificing constitute their duty.

10.s: vedābhyāso brāhmaṇasya kṣatriyasya ca rakṣaṇam vārtākarmaiva vaiśyasya viśiṣṭāni svakarmasu
10.d: वेदाभ्यासो ब्राह्मणस्य क्षत्रियस्य च रक्षणम् वार्ताकर्मैव वैश्यस्य विशिष्टानि स्वकर्मसु
10.e: Among their respective occupations, the most useful are—constant Vedic study for theBrāhmaṇa, protection for theKṣatriyaand commercial dealings for the Vaiśya.

10.s: ajīvaṃstu yathauktena brāhmaṇaḥ svena karmaṇā jīvet kṣatriyadharmeṇa sa hyasya pratyanantaraḥ
10.d: अजीवंस्तु यथौक्तेन ब्राह्मणः स्वेन कर्मणा जीवेत् क्षत्रियधर्मेण स ह्यस्य प्रत्यनन्तरः
10.e: If theBrāhmaṇais unable to subsist by his own occupation as described above, he may make a living by the function of theKṣatriya; since this latter is next to him.

10.s: ubhābhyāmapyajīvaṃstu kathaṃ syāditi cedbhavet kṛṣigorakṣamāsthāya jīvedvaiśyasya jīvikām
10.d: उभाभ्यामप्यजीवंस्तु कथं स्यादिति चेद्भवेत् कृषिगोरक्षमास्थाय जीवेद्वैश्यस्य जीविकाम्
10.e: If he is unable to subsist by these two occupations, and the question arises as to how it should be,—he may live the living of the Vaiśya, having recourse to agriculture and cattle-tending.

10.s: vaiśyavṛttyā 'pi jīvaṃstu brāhmaṇaḥ ksatriyo 'pi vā hiṃsāprāyāṃ parādhīnāṃ kṛṣiṃ yatnena varjayet
10.d: वैश्यवृत्त्या ऽपि जीवंस्तु ब्राह्मणः क्सत्रियो ऽपि वा हिंसाप्रायां पराधीनां कृषिं यत्नेन वर्जयेत्
10.e: But even when subsisting by the occupation of the Vaiśya, theBrāhmaṇaor theKṣatriyashall carefully avoid agriculture, which involves injury to living creatures and is dependent upon others.

10.s: kṛṣiṃ sādhuiti manyante sā vṛttiḥ sadvigarhitāḥ bhūmiṃ bhūmiśayāṃścaiva hanti kāṣṭhamayomukham
10.d: कृषिं साधुइति मन्यन्ते सा वृत्तिः सद्विगर्हिताः भूमिं भूमिशयांश्चैव हन्ति काष्ठमयोमुखम्
10.e: People think agriculture to be good; but that occupation is despised by the righteous; the iron-tipped wood injures the earth and the earthly creatures.

10.s: idaṃ tu vṛttivaikalyāt tyajato dharmanaipuṇam viśpaṇyamuddhṛtauddhāraṃ vikreyaṃ vittavardhanam
10.d: इदं तु वृत्तिवैकल्यात् त्यजतो धर्मनैपुणम् विश्पण्यमुद्धृतौद्धारं विक्रेयं वित्तवर्धनम्
10.e: But there is this, that one who, under the stress of livelihood, renounces the strictness concerning his duties, may, for increasing his wealth, sell such commodities as are sold by Vaiśyas, with certain exceptions.

10.s: sarvān rasānapoheta kṛtānnaṃ ca tilaiḥ saha aśmano lavaṇaṃ caiva paśavo ye ca mānuṣāḥ
10.d: सर्वान् रसानपोहेत कृतान्नं च तिलैः सह अश्मनो लवणं चैव पशवो ये च मानुषाः
10.e: He shall avoid all savoury substances as also cooked food and sesamum, stores, salt, animals and human beings.

10.s: sarvaṃ ca tāntavaṃ raktaṃ śāṇakṣaumāvikāni ca api cet syuraraktāni phalamūle tathauṣadhīḥ
10.d: सर्वं च तान्तवं रक्तं शाणक्षौमाविकानि च अपि चेत् स्युररक्तानि फलमूले तथौषधीः
10.e: Every kind of woven article dyed (red) as well as that made of hemp, silk or wool, even when not dyed red; and also fruits and roots and medicinal herbs.

10.s: apaḥ śastraṃ viṣaṃ māṃsaṃ somaṃ gandhāṃśca sarvaśaḥ kṣīraṃ kṣaudraṃ dadhi ghṛtaṃ tailaṃ madhu guḍaṃ kuśān
10.d: अपः शस्त्रं विषं मांसं सोमं गन्धांश्च सर्वशः क्षीरं क्षौद्रं दधि घृतं तैलं मधु गुडं कुशान्
10.e: Water, weapons, poison, meat, soma and all kinds of perfume; milk, honey, curds, butter, oil, honey-wax, sugar and kuśa-grass.

10.s: āraṇyāṃśca paśūn sarvān daṃṣṭriṇaśca vayāṃsi ca madyaṃ nīliṃ ca lākṣāṃ ca sarvāṃścaikaśaphāṃstathā nīlīṃ
10.d: आरण्यांश्च पशून् सर्वान् दंष्ट्रिणश्च वयांसि च मद्यं नीलिं च लाक्षां च सर्वांश्चैकशफांस्तथा नीलीं
10.e: All beasts of the forest, fanged animals, and birds, wine, indigo, lac, and also all one-hoofed animals.

10.s: kāmamutpādya kṛṣyāṃ tu svayameva kṛṣīvalaḥ vikrīṇīta tilāṃśūdrān dharmārthamacirasthitān tilāṃśuddhān
10.d: काममुत्पाद्य कृष्यां तु स्वयमेव कृषीवलः विक्रीणीत तिलांशूद्रान् धर्मार्थमचिरस्थितान् तिलांशुद्धान्
10.e: But the agriculturist may, if he wishes, sell pure sesamum for sacred purposes, if he has cultivated them himself and has not kept these long.

10.s: bhojanābhyañjanāddānādyadanyat kurute tilaiḥ kṛmibhūtaḥ śvaviṣṭhāyāṃ pitṛbhiḥ saha majjati
10.d: भोजनाभ्यञ्जनाद्दानाद्यदन्यत् कुरुते तिलैः कृमिभूतः श्वविष्ठायां पितृभिः सह मज्जति
10.e: If one does with sesamum anything else, except eating, anointing and giving,—he becomes a worm and plunges into the ordure of dogs, along with his ancestors.

10.s: sadyaḥ patati māṃsena lākṣayā lavaṇena ca tryaheṇa śūdro bhavati brāhmaṇaḥ kṣīravikrayāt
10.d: सद्यः पतति मांसेन लाक्षया लवणेन च त्र्यहेण शूद्रो भवति ब्राह्मणः क्षीरविक्रयात्
10.e: By selling meat, lac and salt, theBrāhmaṇabecomes an outcast at once; and by selling milk theBrāhmaṇabecomes aŚūdrain three days.

10.s: itareṣāṃ tu paṇyānāṃ vikrayādiha kāmataḥ brāhmaṇaḥ saptarātreṇa vaiśyabhāvaṃ niyacchati
10.d: इतरेषां तु पण्यानां विक्रयादिह कामतः ब्राह्मणः सप्तरात्रेण वैश्यभावं नियच्छति
10.e: By selling, through greed, other commodities, theBrāhmaṇaassumes, in seven nights, the character of the Vaiśya.

10.s: rasā rasairnimātavyā na tveva lavaṇaṃ rasaiḥ kṛtānnaṃ ca kṛtānnena tilā dhānyena tatsamāḥ
10.d: रसा रसैर्निमातव्या न त्वेव लवणं रसैः कृतान्नं च कृतान्नेन तिला धान्येन तत्समाः
10.e: Savoury articles should be bartered for savoury articles, but never salt for another savoury article,—cooked food, for cooked food, and sesamum for corn, in equal quantities.

10.s: jīvedetena rājanyaḥ sarveṇāpyanayaṃ gataḥ na tveva jyāyaṃsīṃ vṛttimabhimanyeta karhi cit
10.d: जीवेदेतेन राजन्यः सर्वेणाप्यनयं गतः न त्वेव ज्यायंसीं वृत्तिमभिमन्येत कर्हि चित्
10.e: TheKṣatriya, fallen in adverse circumstances, shall subsist by means of all this; but he shall never think of arrogating to himself the higher occupations.

10.s: yo lobhādadhamo jātyā jīvedutkṛṣṭakarmabhiḥ taṃ rājā nirdhanaṃ kṛtvā kṣiprameva pravāsayet
10.d: यो लोभादधमो जात्या जीवेदुत्कृष्टकर्मभिः तं राजा निर्धनं कृत्वा क्षिप्रमेव प्रवासयेत्
10.e: If a man of low caste, through greed, subsists by the occupations of his superiors, him the King shall deprive of his property and quickly banish.

10.s: varaṃ svadharmo viguṇo na pārakyaḥ svanuṣṭhitaḥ viguṇaḥ paradharmāt svadhiṣṭhitāt paradharmeṇa jīvan hi sadyaḥ patati jātitaḥ
10.d: वरं स्वधर्मो विगुणो न पारक्यः स्वनुष्ठितः विगुणः परधर्मात् स्वधिष्ठितात् परधर्मेण जीवन् हि सद्यः पतति जातितः
10.e: Better one’s own duty imperfectly performed, and not the duty of another performed perfectly; he who subsists by the function of another, instantly falls off from his caste.

10.s: vaiśyo 'jīvan svadharmeṇa śūdravṛttyā 'pi vartayet anācarannakāryāṇi nivarteta ca śaktimān
10.d: वैश्यो ऽजीवन् स्वधर्मेण शूद्रवृत्त्या ऽपि वर्तयेत् अनाचरन्नकार्याणि निवर्तेत च शक्तिमान्
10.e: The Vaiśya, unable to subsist by his own occupations, may subsist by the occupations of theŚūdra, avoiding all improper acts. But he shall desist from them as soon as he is able to do so.

10.s: aśaknuvaṃstu śuśrūṣāṃ śūdraḥ kartuṃ dvijanmanām putradārātyayaṃ prāpto jīvet kārukakarmabhiḥ
10.d: अशक्नुवंस्तु शुश्रूषां शूद्रः कर्तुं द्विजन्मनाम् पुत्रदारात्ययं प्राप्तो जीवेत् कारुककर्मभिः
10.e: TheŚūdra, unable to do service for twice-born people, and threatened with danger to his wife and sons, may subsist by the occupations of craftsmen.

10.s: yaiḥ karmabhiḥ pracaritaiḥ śuśrūṣyante dvijātayaḥ tāni kārukakarmāṇi śilpāni vividhāni ca
10.d: यैः कर्मभिः प्रचरितैः शुश्रूष्यन्ते द्विजातयः तानि कारुककर्माणि शिल्पानि विविधानि च
10.e: That is, those occupations of craftsmen and other arts by the performance whereof the twice-born men are best served.

10.s: vaiśyavṛttimanātiṣṭhan brāhmaṇaḥ sve pathi sthitaḥ avṛttikarṣitaḥ sīdannimaṃ dharmaṃ samācaret
10.d: वैश्यवृत्तिमनातिष्ठन् ब्राह्मणः स्वे पथि स्थितः अवृत्तिकर्षितः सीदन्निमं धर्मं समाचरेत्
10.e: If aBrāhmaṇa, distressed through want of livelihood, pines, because resolved to stick to his own path, he does not adopt the occupation of the Vaiśya,—he shall adopt this (following) procedure.

10.s: sarvataḥ pratigṛhṇīyādbrāhmaṇastvanayaṃ gataḥ pavitraṃ duṣyatītyetaddharmato naupapadyate
10.d: सर्वतः प्रतिगृह्णीयाद्ब्राह्मणस्त्वनयं गतः पवित्रं दुष्यतीत्येतद्धर्मतो नौपपद्यते
10.e: Fallen into distress, theBrāhmaṇamay receive gifts from all; that anything which is pure should become defiled is not possible under the law.

10.s: nādhyāpanādyājanādvā garhitādvā pratigrahāt doṣo bhavati viprāṇāṃ jvalanāmbusamā hi te
10.d: नाध्यापनाद्याजनाद्वा गर्हिताद्वा प्रतिग्रहात् दोषो भवति विप्राणां ज्वलनाम्बुसमा हि ते
10.e: No sin attaches toBrāhmaṇas, either by teaching or by sacrificing for others or by receiving reprehensible gifts; for they are like fire and water.

10.s: jīvitātyayamāpanno yo 'nnamatti tatastataḥ ākāśamiva paṅkena na sa pāpena lipyate
10.d: जीवितात्ययमापन्नो यो ऽन्नमत्ति ततस्ततः आकाशमिव पङ्केन न स पापेन लिप्यते
10.e: If a man, threatened with loss of life, eats food from stray sources, he does not become tainted with sin, just asĀkāśais not defiled by mud.

10.s: ajīgartaḥ sutaṃ hantumupāsarpadbubhukṣitaḥ na cālipyata pāpena kṣutpratīkāramācaran
10.d: अजीगर्तः सुतं हन्तुमुपासर्पद्बुभुक्षितः न चालिप्यत पापेन क्षुत्प्रतीकारमाचरन्
10.e: Ajīgarta, buffering from hunger, went forward to kill his son; and as he sought a remedy for hunger, he did not become tainted with sin.

10.s: śvamāṃsamicchanārto 'ttuṃ dharmādharmavicakṣaṇaḥ prāṇānāṃ parirakṣārthaṃ vāmadevo na liptavān
10.d: श्वमांसमिच्छनार्तो ऽत्तुं धर्माधर्मविचक्षणः प्राणानां परिरक्षार्थं वामदेवो न लिप्तवान्
10.e: Vāmadeva, expert in the knowledge of right and wrong, when distressed, desired to eat dog’s flesh for saving his life,—and he did not become defiled.

10.s: bharadvājaḥ kṣudhārtastu saputro vijane vane bahvīrgāḥ pratijagrāha vṛdhostakṣṇo mahātapāḥ
10.d: भरद्वाजः क्षुधार्तस्तु सपुत्रो विजने वने बह्वीर्गाः प्रतिजग्राह वृधोस्तक्ष्णो महातपाः
10.e: Bharadvāja, a man of great austerities, accepted many cows from the carpenterVṛdhu, when tormented by hunger, along with his sons, in a lonely forest.

10.s: kṣudhārtaścāttumabhyāgādviśvāmitraḥ śvajāghanīm caṇḍālahastādādāya dharmādharmavicakṣaṇaḥ
10.d: क्षुधार्तश्चात्तुमभ्यागाद्विश्वामित्रः श्वजाघनीम् चण्डालहस्तादादाय धर्माधर्मविचक्षणः
10.e: Viśvāmitra, expert in the knowledge of right and wrong, when tormented by hunger, proceeded to eat the haunch of a dog, receiving it from the hands of aCaṇḍāla.

10.s: pratigrahādyājanādvā tathaivādhyāpanādapi pratigrahaḥ pratyavaraḥ pretya viprasya garhitaḥ
10.d: प्रतिग्रहाद्याजनाद्वा तथैवाध्यापनादपि प्रतिग्रहः प्रत्यवरः प्रेत्य विप्रस्य गर्हितः
10.e: Among Receiving of Gifts, Sacrificing and Teaching, the Receiving of Gifts is the meanest, and the most reprehensible for theBrāhmaṇa, in respect of his life after death.

10.s: yājanādhyāpane nityaṃ kriyete saṃskṛtātmanām pratigrahastu kriyate śūdrādapyantyajanmanaḥ
10.d: याजनाध्यापने नित्यं क्रियेते संस्कृतात्मनाम् प्रतिग्रहस्तु क्रियते शूद्रादप्यन्त्यजन्मनः
10.e: As for Teachng and Sacrificing, these are done always for only such men as have received the sacraments; while the Receiving of Gifts may be done even from the lowest-bornŚūdra.

10.s: japahomairapaityeno yājanādhyāpanaiḥ kṛtam pratigrahanimittaṃ tu tyāgena tapasaiva ca
10.d: जपहोमैरपैत्येनो याजनाध्यापनैः कृतम् प्रतिग्रहनिमित्तं तु त्यागेन तपसैव च
10.e: By the muttering of sacred texts and by the offering of libations is the guilt incurred by teaching and sacrificing removed; while that incurred by receiving gifts is removed only by renouncing them and by austerities.

10.s: śilauñchamapyādadīta vipro 'jīvan yatastataḥ pratigrahātśilaḥ śreyāṃstato 'pyuñchaḥ praśasyate
10.d: शिलौञ्छमप्याददीत विप्रो ऽजीवन् यतस्ततः प्रतिग्रहात्शिलः श्रेयांस्ततो ऽप्युञ्छः प्रशस्यते
10.e: TheBrāhmaṇa, unable to maintain himself, may take to gleaning ears of corn and picking up grains, even from stray places. Gleaning ears of corn is better than receiving gifts; and better even than picking up of grains.

10.s: sīdadbhiḥ kupyamicchadbhirdhane vā pṛthivīpatiḥ dhanaṃ vā yācyaḥ syāt snātakairviprairaditsaṃstyāgamarhati
10.d: सीदद्भिः कुप्यमिच्छद्भिर्धने वा पृथिवीपतिः धनं वा याच्यः स्यात् स्नातकैर्विप्रैरदित्संस्त्यागमर्हति
10.e: IfBrāhmaṇas, who have completed their study, suffer privation, or seek to obtain wealth and riches, they may beg of the king; and if he be unwilling to give, he should be given up.

10.s: akṛtaṃ ca kṛtāt kṣetrādgaurajāvikameva ca hiraṇyaṃ dhānyamannaṃ ca pūrvaṃ pūrvamadoṣavat
10.d: अकृतं च कृतात् क्षेत्राद्गौरजाविकमेव च हिरण्यं धान्यमन्नं च पूर्वं पूर्वमदोषवत्
